In a strong demonstration of national and international commitment to restoring momentum in the peace process, the Community Empowerment for Progress Organization (CEPO) held a high-level meeting with the leadership of the South Sudan Opposition Alliance (SSOA) faction led by Hon. Hussein Abdelbagi Akol.
The meeting took place on Wednesday at the South Sudan Council of Churches (SSCC) premises and was facilitated by the Inter-Faith Council and the Women Mediators, with representatives from RJMEC and the African Union attending as official observers.

This engagement forms part of CEPO’s broader consultation efforts aimed at reinvigorating political will and accelerating the implementation of the Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS 2018). The meeting occurs at a critical time when key provisions—such as the unification of the security sector and preparations for national elections—remain significantly delayed.

The SSOA delegation included:
 • Hon. Clement Juma – Deputy Chairman
 • Hon. Changkuoth Bichiock Reth – Secretary-General
alongside several senior political leaders who also serve as chairpersons of their respective constituent parties.

Speaking after the meeting, Hon. Clement Juma emphasized that the discussions focused on identifying the structural challenges hindering implementation of the peace agreement and outlining practical steps to guide future high-level dialogue.
He stated:

“We identified the issues that have stalled progress, deliberated on realistic solutions, and agreed on an initial framework for continued constructive engagement.”

Hon. Juma also informed the mediators and observers that SSOA is currently divided into two separate leadership structures—one led by Hon. Hussein Abdelbagi Akol and the other led by Hon. Josephine Joseph Lagu—each operating independently of the other.

Speaking on behalf of the Women Mediators, Elizabeth Adut described the engagement as both constructive and promising, affirming that SSOA leaders renewed their firm commitment to the full, transparent, and credible implementation of the peace agreement and expressed readiness to participate actively in upcoming consultations.

🔸 Valoriser les acteurs locaux engagés auprès de la jeunesse
🔸 Créer un espace d’échange entre institutions, associations et jeunes

A reminder for anyone walking into mediation:

Stop centering the conversation on how “terrible” the other parent is.
That goes nowhere.
It sounds defensive, emotional, and unfocused and it pulls the mediator into your personal history instead of the actual issue.

Mediation is not therapy.
It’s not where you unpack every wound, betrayal, or resentment.
It’s where you identify specific behaviors that put your child at risk and build a plan to protect them.
.
Keep it child-focused:
Not “He’s an alcoholic.”
But: “There were missed exchanges, impaired driving, and inconsistent care during his parenting time.”
Not “She’s unstable.”
But: “The kids weren’t fed, appointments were missed, and homework wasn’t supervised.”

Not “He’s a narcissist.”
But: “Communication breaks down, information isn’t shared, and decisions aren’t made in a timely way.”
These are behaviors, not accusations.
Behaviors can be documented.
Behaviors impact the child.
Behaviors give the mediator something to work with.
When you stay grounded in facts instead of feelings, you protect your child, your credibility, and the entire mediation process.
.
If you need help getting clear on what’s relevant and what’s just emotional noise, I offer 30-minute mediation prep sessions for $35.
.
Show up focused, prepared, and centered on the only thing that matters: your child’s safety and stability.

𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐃𝐓𝐈 𝐬𝐚𝐲𝐬 ₱𝟓𝟎𝟎 𝐢𝐬 𝐞𝐧𝐨𝐮𝐠𝐡 𝐟𝐨𝐫 𝐚 𝐟𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲’𝐬 𝐍𝐨𝐜𝐡𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐚.
𝐁𝐮𝐭 𝐥𝐞𝐭’𝐬 𝐛𝐞 𝐡𝐨𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐭 — 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐮𝐞 𝐰𝐚𝐬 𝐧𝐞𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐦𝐚𝐭𝐡. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐢𝐬𝐬𝐮𝐞 𝐢𝐬 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐜𝐨𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐱𝐭.

Yes, technically, if you choose the cheapest possible brands, buy only the bare minimum ingredients, and remove almost everything traditionally found on a Filipino Christmas table, you might squeeze out a “meal” worth ₱500.

But here’s the bigger problem:

𝟏. ₱𝟓𝟎𝟎 𝐍𝐨𝐜𝐡𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐚 𝐞𝐱𝐢𝐬𝐭𝐬 𝐨𝐧𝐥𝐲 𝐢𝐧 𝐚 𝐠𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐧𝐦𝐞𝐧𝐭 𝐬𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐝𝐬𝐡𝐞𝐞𝐭 — 𝐧𝐨𝐭 𝐢𝐧 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐬𝐞𝐡𝐨𝐥𝐝𝐬.

Real prices vary wildly depending on the barangay, the store, and the supply.
Fresh food is more expensive. Transport is more expensive. Everything is more expensive.

What DTI presented is the bare minimum, not the reality.

𝟐. 𝐈𝐭 𝐧𝐨𝐫𝐦𝐚𝐥𝐢𝐳𝐞𝐬 𝐩𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐢𝐧𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐚𝐝 𝐨𝐟 𝐚𝐝𝐝𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐬𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐨𝐧 𝐟𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐜𝐚𝐧’𝐭 𝐚𝐟𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐝 𝐟𝐨𝐨𝐝.

The question shouldn’t be:
“𝐊𝐚𝐲𝐚 𝐛𝐚 𝐚𝐧𝐠 ₱𝟓𝟎𝟎?”

The question is:
“𝐁𝐚𝐤𝐢𝐭 𝐡𝐢𝐧𝐝𝐢 𝐤𝐚𝐲𝐚 𝐧𝐠 𝐦𝐚𝐫𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐩𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐲𝐚 𝐚𝐧𝐠 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐞𝐧𝐭𝐞𝐧𝐠 𝐍𝐨𝐜𝐡𝐞 𝐁𝐮𝐞𝐧𝐚?”

Because:
• wages have not kept up with inflation
• food prices are unstable
• government support is inconsistent
• and yes — systemic corruption drains public funds meant for basic services

𝟑. 𝐘𝐨𝐮 𝐜𝐚𝐧’𝐭 𝐩𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐜𝐡 ‘𝐛𝐮𝐝𝐠𝐞𝐭 𝐭𝐢𝐩𝐬’ 𝐰𝐡𝐢𝐥𝐞 𝐛𝐢𝐥𝐥𝐢𝐨𝐧𝐬 𝐝𝐢𝐬𝐚𝐩𝐩𝐞𝐚𝐫 𝐝𝐮𝐞 𝐭𝐨 𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐫𝐮𝐩𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧.

Families are told to tighten their belts, be “wais,” and “manage spending”…
while:
• overpriced government procurement continues,
• infrastructure projects are delayed or abandoned,
• leakages and wastage run into the billions, and
• audit reports highlight the same issues year after year.

When corruption thrives, prices rise.
When systems fail, people pay the price.

That is the real context behind the ₱500 claim.

𝟒. 𝐏𝐨𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐭𝐲 𝐬𝐡𝐨𝐮𝐥𝐝𝐧’𝐭 𝐛𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐛𝐫𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐞𝐝 𝐚𝐬 ‘𝐫𝐞𝐬𝐨𝐮𝐫𝐜𝐞𝐟𝐮𝐥𝐧𝐞𝐬𝐬.’

A decent Noche Buena is not a luxury.
It’s not an extravagance.
It’s a cultural tradition that symbolizes dignity, family, and hope.

When government touts “₱500 is enough,” it unintentionally sends a message:

“𝐓𝐚𝐧𝐠𝐠𝐚𝐩𝐢𝐧 𝐧𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐧𝐚 𝐲𝐚𝐧 — 𝐩𝐚𝐠𝐭𝐢𝐲𝐚𝐠𝐚𝐚𝐧 𝐧𝐢𝐲𝐨 𝐧𝐚.”

That’s not guidance.
That’s resignation.

Filipinos deserve better.

𝟓. 𝐓𝐡𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐚𝐥 𝐬𝐨𝐥𝐮𝐭𝐢𝐨𝐧 𝐢𝐬𝐧’𝐭 𝐟𝐨𝐫𝐜𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐟𝐚𝐦𝐢𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐨 𝐚𝐝𝐣𝐮𝐬𝐭 — 𝐢𝐭’𝐬 𝐟𝐢𝐱𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐬𝐲𝐬𝐭𝐞𝐦.

We need:
✔ stable food supply
✔ stronger competition laws
✔ market monitoring
✔ fair wages
✔ ease of doing business
✔ efficient logistics
✔ clean, corruption-free budgeting

A system that works reduces prices.

Coexistence doesn’t fail when a negative encounter happens. It begins.

Moments of conflict between people, and/or dogs, and wildlife are reminders that our shared landscapes need renewed attention, clearer communication, and consistent actions from all of us.

Coexistence is not passive. It’s a daily intention: choosing behaviours that respect the needs of both humans and wild animals, and recognizing how our presence, including off-leash pets,  shapes local ecosystems. Responsible recreation, staying alert, managing attractants, and keeping dogs leashed in wildlife-active areas give every species the space they need to stay safe.

True coexistence is guided by science, shaped by lived experience, and supported by traditional ecological knowledge. Communities have shared the land with wildlife for generations; today, we continue that legacy with modern tools, better understanding, and a commitment to minimizing conflict.

Statements made by frustrated or upset members of the public that coexistence is failing are understandable, particularly after a traumatic event. However, it isn’t that coexistence is failing when negative encounters occur; it means that the current situation must be investigated, and coexistence strategies implemented. This may require reviewing, revisiting and reassessing current strategies and how they can be adapted.

The investigation is a critical aspect of coexistence both short and long-term. Often, negative encounters between people and wildlife are painted as ‘attacks’ in the media. When examined, however, many of these encounters are caused by ongoing food conditioning by people (teaching animals to approach humans), because people are perceived as a threat to the animal who may be with or near their dens and families, escorting or cautious behaviours misidentified as predatory, and many other possibilities.

Working together, we can ensure people, pets, and wildlife thrive in the places we all call home.
- Canid Response Team | Coyote Watch Canada

On 25th- 28th, November 2025, the Centre for Peace and Democracy - CPD in collaboration with the Dowlad‑Wanag Consortium and the Afgoye District Local Authority, jointly prepared and facilitated an Inclusive Social Accountability (ISA) workshop in Afgoye District, South West State of Somalia.

A total of 18 participants (5 women and 13 men) attended, representing rights holders’ institutions, including the youth caucus, women’s caucus, minority groups, individuals with disabilities, and other civil society organizations.

The ISA training aimed to equip rights holders with practical, hands‑on skills to implement ISA as a continuous accountability cycle.

Key concepts discussed included Inclusive Social Accountability (ISA): Defined as a set of procedures and tools enabling all people especially marginalized and vulnerable groups, to monitor duty bearers, engage with them, and hold them accountable for delivering public goods and services in a fair, transparent, and responsive manner.

RJMEC warns deteriorating security threatens peace agreement, elections

The Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC) has warned that South Sudan’s political and security situation significantly deteriorated in the last quarter, putting the implementation of the 2018 Revitalised Peace Agreement and the conduct of the 2026 elections at serious risk.

Presenting the RJMEC Quarterly Report to the Transitional National Legislative Assembly (TNLA) on Tuesday, Ambassador Berhanu Kebede, RJMEC Chief of Staff, said the latest findings—covering 1 July to 30 September 2025—show worrying regression.

“During the reporting period, the political and security situation continued to deteriorate significantly, undermining the implementation of the revitalized peace agreement,” he told lawmakers.

Kebede said the situation worsened following the Nasir incident, describing it as a major violation of the permanent ceasefire.

“The agreement faced renewed pressure following the Nasir incident, a major violation of the permanent ceasefire, and its aftermath, which triggered arrests, prolonged detention, and judicial process, as well as several political actions detrimental to trust building between the parties to the peace agreement and its implementation,” he stated.

While the RJMEC quarterly report warned of serious violations, it also acknowledged some positive steps, especially in governance, where the legislature managed to pass a number of bills into law.

“The TNLA resumed sittings after a six-month recess and made some progress on its legislative priorities, and this is a welcome development,” Kebede noted, adding that RJMEC appreciated being invited to present its report for the third consecutive time.

However, he raised concerns about the slow pace of judicial reforms.

“The implementation of the judicial reforms as contained in the recommendations of the Ad hoc Judicial Reform Committee, the report is still pending,” Kebede said.

He added that although new judges had been appointed to the Supreme Court and Court of Appeal, deeper reforms require “the review and implementation of the judiciary act, and the reconstitution of the judicial service commission, both of which are still pending.”

The report further warned that preparations for the December 2026 elections remain far behind schedule.

“The election-related institutions, such as the National Election Commission and the Political Parties Council, continued with institutional strengthening and capacity building activities, but lacked subject funding to discharge their mandates with time, fast running out,” Kebede stated. “If urgent steps are not taken to expedite progress, then holding elections as scheduled in December 2026 may be extremely difficult.”

“We appeal to this August House to prevail upon RTGoNU to provide funding to expedite the implementation of the critical pending elections-related tasks,” he added.

Upon its tabling in the House, Speaker Jemma Nunu Kumba committed the report to the committees of peace and reconciliation and justice and legislation, respectively, for scrutiny and ordered them to report to the House within 14 days.

Presenting the quarterly report to the Transitional National Legislative Assembly (TNLA), Ambassador Berhanu Kebede, RJMEC Chief of Staff, said that the period from 1 July to 30 September 2025 saw major regression, especially following the Nasir incident, which violated the permanent ceasefire and triggered arrests and political tensions.

While acknowledging progress in governance, including the passage of several bills by the legislature, Kebede raised concerns over slow judicial reforms and delays in preparing for the December 2026 elections.

“Election-related institutions lack sufficient funding and capacity to meet deadlines,” he warned, urging the government to act urgently to ensure elections can be held as scheduled.

The report has been referred to the peace and reconciliation and justice and legislation committees, with instructions to report back within 14 days.

Joint Statement from Troika Capitals on South Sudan 

The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America, the United Kingdom, and Norway.

Begin text.

When the Revitalized Agreement for the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS) was signed just over seven years ago, it was hoped that it would bring peace after the country’s initial years of independence were scarred by conflict, including brutal violence against civilians.

Despite the support of the international community, the optimism and relief that followed the R-ARCSS was undeserved. Under the terms of the R-ARCSS, President Kiir should be leading a transitional government of national unity. It does not live up to the name, with the principles of power sharing violated and no meaningful progress towards implementing the agreement. Public resources continue to be misused: public servant salaries are going unpaid and international donors are spending significantly more on delivering basic services to the people of South Sudan than the transitional government is itself. At independence, South Sudan’s oil revenue made it a middle-income country. It is now the world’s poorest, and its most corrupt. The leadership is continuing with destabilizing unilateral reshuffles, rather than focusing on governing the country or preparing for elections.

Most seriously, we have seen a return to widespread conflict across the country. It would be tragic for the people of South Sudan if we see a return to the levels of violence of 2013 and 2016. It would also represent a serious setback for South Sudan’s neighbors, already suffering the destabilizing influence of the conflict in Sudan.

For the good of the people of South Sudan and for the sake of regional stability, South Sudan’s leaders must urgently reverse course. All parties, especially the SPLM-IG and SPLM-IO, must stop armed attacks and immediately return to the nationwide ceasefire and to sustained leader-level dialogue. The transitional government must end its aerial attacks against its own citizens; release political prisoners; use public revenue to pay public sector employees; and fund health, education, and other essential services for its citizens.

Transitional government officials at all levels must also cease interfering in the operations of humanitarian assistance providers and regional and international organizations. The transitional government’s obstruction of departure as well as in-country movements of UN peacekeepers is a prime example of this behavior and must stop immediately.

All South Sudan’s friends and partners, and especially those neighboring South Sudan who have the most to lose from the prospect of renewed large-scale conflict, should be united in their messaging – that enough is enough. South Sudan’s leaders must stop the current conflict and focus on restoring the trust of its people and the international community through concrete actions. If they do so, they will attract the world’s support, investment, and respect.

End text.

No one really prepares you for what unfolds when you choose healing… when you begin to hold space for love, peace and unity in your life. When you remember that we are all connected, that everyone is worthy of love and healing and that we are living dreams of ancestors who prayed for futures they might never witness, yet celebrate through us in spirit. ❤️🙏🏽

There’s an idea that once you move through the darkness, the path becomes lighter and easier. But healing isn’t a place you arrive at… it’s something you continue to meet. Again and again, life gently asks whether you can stay rooted in love. Along the way, you encounter others who are finding their way too, sometimes expressing their pain in ways that are difficult to receive. Not because anyone is failing, but because we are all learning, unlearning and remembering in our own time.

What often goes unspoken is the quiet beauty within this process… how it softens you, deepens your understanding and allows compassion to grow naturally. When you’ve walked through your own uncertainty, you recognize it in others. You don’t need to fix or change anything. Sometimes simply being present, open and kind is enough to offer a moment of warmth or clarity.

As the holidays approach, joy and grief often exist side by side. Move gently, choose what feels aligned, and extend grace where you can… both to yourself and to others. Even small gestures of light matter. We are here together, for a reason. ✨ 

All our love this holiday season, to you and yours ❤️🙏🏽🦅

From a MOM’S perspective 🤍

🍏When people hear “face your demons”, they imagine something dramatic.

But motherhood teaches us the truth:

The “demons” are often quiet.

They look like:
 • snapping when you’re overwhelmed
 • shutting down when emotions get big
 • feeling guilty for needing space
 • overexplaining because you’re afraid to be misunderstood
 • tolerating disrespect because conflict feels unsafe
 • holding it all together until you collapse in private

Kids don’t just experience what we say — they absorb what we model.

So when a mother chooses healing, she isn’t being selfish.
She is interrupting inheritance.

She’s saying:

“The pain stops with me.”

And that is one of the bravest things a woman can do.

🍏What this quote is really saying (without the harshness)

“You either face your demons, or they raise your children.”

Translation:
 • 🍒If I don’t learn to regulate, my kids will learn to tiptoe.
 • 🍒If I don’t heal abandonment wounds, my kids may grow up over-attached or afraid to need.
 • 🍒If I don’t unlearn survival mode, my kids will think chaos is normal.

This isn’t blame.
It’s awareness.

Healing doesn’t make you flawless.
It makes you present.
And presence is what children remember.

⸻

🍏Facing demons without retraumatizing yourself 🌱

This part matters most.

You do not have to:
 • 🍒relive everything
 • 🍒dig up every memory
 • 🍒be healed all at once

You do need:

✨ Awareness

“Why did that moment trigger me?”

✨ Regulation

Learning to pause, breathe, ground — even imperfectly.

✨ Repair

Saying:

“I’m sorry. That reaction wasn’t about you.”

This alone is cycle-breaking.

✨ Compassion

Healing happens in layers, not leaps.

Your kids don’t need a healed mother.
They need a real one who models growth.

Some moms don’t need a “break.” What they truly need is permission.

Permission to sit without an explanation. To let their bodies rest, even when the world whispers that rest must be earned. Permission to stop trying to fix everyone and everything around them and simply exist in their own space. Permission to put themselves first without guilt, without apology, without hesitation.

It’s permission to say no and mean it, to let schedules slip, to leave dishes in the sink, to let the laundry wait. To allow the house to be noisy, messy, alive, without feeling responsible for controlling every detail. Because exhaustion isn’t always about how much we do—it’s about how much we carry alone. It’s about surviving while carrying the weight of a thousand expectations, constantly being told to “push through,” to smile, to keep giving.

You are not lazy for needing this. You are not weak for craving space. You are not wrong for wanting to honor yourself as much as you honor everyone else. Your body, your heart, your mind deserve care too. Your boundaries are not selfish—they are survival.

So here it is: permission. Permission to breathe fully, to rest unapologetically, to let go of the relentless pressure to perform. Permission to honor your limits and your needs, even if the world does not recognize them. This is your space, your time, your life, and it is okay to claim it.

Because sometimes, the most radical act a mom can do is simply take care of herself.

South Sudan’s cabinet fills gap left by Machar
 
December 24, 2025 JUBA
South Sudan’s cabinet has moved to fill a governance vacuum following the detention and trial of suspended First Vice President Dr Riek Machar.

In an extraordinary meeting in Juba on Tuesday, President Salva Kiir, other vice presidents and ministers nominated the Vice President for Gender and Youth Affairs, Rebecca Nyandeng de Mabior, to chair the governance cluster in Dr Machar’s absence.

Dr Machar, a key figure in the 2018 peace agreement, was placed under house arrest in March 2025 amid rising political tensions. He now faces treason and other charges in a special court set up in Juba, with proceedings that began in September.

It is unclear when the trial will end. Proceedings are ongoing, with the court having heard testimony from five of the 16 witnesses listed by the prosecution.

The Minister of Cabinet Affairs, Dr Martin Elia Lomuro, told reporters the cabinet had resolved that Ms Nyandeng would also assume the governance cluster responsibilities.

Ms Nyandeng represents the Former Detainees group (FDs) under the peace deal, while Dr Machar leads the main opposition party, the SPLM-IO.

It is unclear why the cabinet acted now to address the gap left since March, as Dr Machar’s trial is expected to continue for some time.

Peace deal changes

The cabinet also discussed and passed critical resolutions, including amendments to the revitalised peace agreement.

These changes , Dr. Martin said, would separate the constitution-making process, census, and housing data from the transitional constitution. If endorsed, this would allow the government to use the 2011 Transitional Constitution as amended, and potentially pave the way for elections without a new census or permanent constitution.

The amendments now await endorsement by the peace monitoring body, the Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC), and passage by parliament.

However, it is uncertain whether the RJMEC, which includes several other stakeholders, will approve the changes. Concerns have been raised by allies of Dr Machar, and there appears to be a lack of consensus.

Other cabinet decisions

The Council of Ministers confirmed the establishment of a mechanism to enable the Finance Ministry to pay salary arrears to civil servants and organised forces.

It also discussed the need for the government to co-finance and protect a health sector transformation project, which is funded by the World Bank and other partners. Dr Lomuro noted that slow global financing was putting pressure on health facilities nationwide.

The cabinet, which resumed its activities last month after a nine-month suspension, also deliberated on several other memoranda presented by ministerial clusters on critical matters.

Dr Machar, a key figure in the 2018 peace agreement, was placed under house arrest in March 2025 amid rising political tensions. He now faces treason and other charges in a special court set up in Juba, with proceedings that began in September.

It is unclear when the trial will end. Proceedings are ongoing, with the court having heard testimony from five of the 16 witnesses listed by the prosecution.

The Minister of Cabinet Affairs, Dr Martin Elia Lomuro, told reporters the cabinet had resolved that Ms Nyandeng would also assume the governance cluster responsibilities.

Ms Nyandeng represents the Former Detainees group (FDs) under the peace deal, while Dr Machar leads the main opposition party, the SPLM-IO.

It is unclear why the cabinet acted now to address the gap left since March, as Dr Machar’s trial is expected to continue for some time.

Peace deal changes

The cabinet also discussed and passed critical resolutions, including amendments to the revitalised peace agreement.

These changes , Dr. Martin said, would separate the constitution-making process, census, and housing data from the transitional constitution. If endorsed, this would allow the government to use the 2011 Transitional Constitution as amended, and potentially pave the way for elections without a new census or permanent constitution.

The amendments now await endorsement by the peace monitoring body, the Reconstituted Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC), and passage by parliament.

However, it is uncertain whether the RJMEC, which includes several other stakeholders, will approve the changes. Concerns have been raised by allies of Dr Machar, and there appears to be a lack of consensus.

Other cabinet decisions

The Council of Ministers confirmed the establishment of a mechanism to enable the Finance Ministry to pay salary arrears to civil servants and organised forces.

It also discussed the need for the government to co-finance and protect a health sector transformation project, which is funded by the World Bank and other partners. Dr Lomuro noted that slow global financing was putting pressure on health facilities nationwide.

The cabinet, which resumed its activities last month after a nine-month suspension, also deliberated on several other memoranda presented by ministerial clusters on critical matters.

Last year, we watched as institutions across South Sudan celebrated individuals for excellence and leadership. When public recognition filled our screens, it gave us a moment to pause and reflect, not on titles or awards, but on responsibility. What problem were we willing to take ownership of?

That question gave rise to Save the Nile in January 2025.

We started because plastic pollution along the Nile in Juba had become impossible to ignore. Over 70 percent of the waste on the riverbanks is single-use plastic. It threatens fishing livelihoods, degrades water quality, and fuels waterborne diseases in communities that rely on the river every day. Waiting was no longer an option.

Since then, Save the Nile has grown through action. Together with young volunteers, community members, churches, and student associations, we led multiple riverbank cleanups across Juba, from Hai Amarat and Hai Kasaba near Juba Bridge to community markets and learning spaces. We worked with the Juba City Council to ensure collected waste was safely transported and did not return to the environment.

But our work goes beyond cleanups. We believe knowledge drives lasting change. We brought students, NGOs, and policymakers together at the French Institute, University of Juba to talk honestly about plastic pollution and shared responsibility. Through a DIY Science Camp, young people learned how to identify plastic types using simple tools and make smarter choices in daily life. We used radio and social media to reach thousands more, turning awareness into participation.

The impact is tangible. Hundreds of kilograms of plastic removed. Cleaner public spaces. More young people stepping forward to protect the Nile.

Recognition may follow, but it is not our goal. Our purpose is clear: protect the river that sustains our lives and our future.

To every young person reading this, change does not begin with permission or applause. It begins with action. Join us.

Yakani: Stakeholders Meet SPLM Secretary General on Political Developments, Reaffirm December 2026 Elections

Mr. Edmund Yakani, Executive Director of the Community Empowerment for Progress Organization (CEPO), said today that a delegation of key stakeholders—including civil society representatives, women leaders, women mediators, academia, and members of the business community—held a consultative meeting with the Secretary General of the Sudan People’s Liberation Movement (SPLM) to discuss recent political developments in South Sudan.

Mr. Yakani described the meeting as constructive and productive, noting that several important positions and recommendations were agreed upon.

According to him, the meeting reviewed the Revitalized Joint Monitoring and Evaluation Commission (RJMEC) report on the sixth extension of the Transitional Period. Stakeholders unanimously resolved that there should be no further extension of the Transitional Period, and that general elections must be conducted as scheduled in December 2026. They emphasized that this resolution must be respected and honored by all parties.

The meeting reaffirmed that elections should be held on 22 December 2026, and stressed that the electoral process must be inclusive of all rightful signatories to the Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in the Republic of South Sudan (R-ARCSS).

Participants also discussed Articles 8.2 and 8.3 of the R-ARCSS, recommending that these provisions must not be deleted or altered, as they remain critical to the integrity and implementation of the peace agreement.

Furthermore, the meeting addressed the implementation of the 35 percent affirmative action for women in the December 2026 elections, underscoring the need to safeguard women’s political participation as guaranteed in the peace agreement.

The fate and administrative status of the Ruweng Administrative Area and the Greater Pibor Administrative Area were also discussed, with stakeholders calling for clarity and political consensus on their future within the framework of the R-ARCSS.

Mr. Yakani concluded by urging political leaders to respect the outcomes of such engagements and prioritize peace, inclusivity, and adherence to the peace agreement as the country moves toward elections.

Sometimes I'm physically present beside my kid, pouring every ounce of love into her, yet my thoughts wander elsewhere. Not from lack of wanting to stay grounded, but because a piece of me remains processing all the trauma I endured to build this life for us.
I'm reading her a story and suddenly I'm remembering the fight that led to me finally leaving. I'm watching her play and my mind flashes back to the chaos I had to escape to give her this peace. I'm tucking her in and I'm replaying every sacrifice, every hard decision, every moment I almost broke but kept going anyway.
It's not that I'm not present. It's that I'm holding two realities at once — the beautiful one I'm building with her, and the painful one I had to survive to get here. My body is here. My love is here. But my mind is still doing the work of untangling years of dysfunction, abuse, and survival mode.
Sometimes I feel guilty for it. Like I should be able to compartmentalize better. Like she deserves a mother who isn't still processing. But healing doesn't pause just because life keeps moving. Recovery doesn't stop because there are bedtime routines and school drop-offs and snacks to prepare.
I'm doing both. Loving her fiercely while healing from what it took to protect her. Being fully present while simultaneously working through a past that still surfaces in unexpected moments.
And maybe that's okay. Maybe it's enough that I'm here, that I chose her, that I'm breaking cycles even while still healing from them.

Critics, however, warn that such messaging risks alienating immigrant communities and reducing complex integration challenges to slogans. They argue that true integration also depends on access to education, jobs, housing, and equal opportunities — areas where governments often fall short.

The controversy highlights a wider European dilemma: how to balance humanitarian responsibility with national identity, cultural integration, and legal discipline. As migration increasingly influences elections and public discourse worldwide, Sweden’s debate shows how questions of inclusion, security, and shared values are colliding — demanding careful policy, not polarising rhetoric.

By HONORABLE MAKER LUAL 

HISTORICAL: Several Abortive Reconciliation Peace Conferences between the Greater Bor Dinka and the Murle Communities
Several Abortive Reconciliation Peace Conferences between the Greater Bor Dinka and the Murle Communities. When will this policy of ambiguity end?
By Hon. Maker Lual Kuol, Bor, Jonglei State
For nearly two centuries, Murle have continued to raid Bor; killing people, abducting children and robbing livestock to the extent that this inhuman and atrocious activity has become a lost a daily practice. It is not Bor alone that suffers from these raids but over other 12 communities such as Anyuak, Jie, Kachipo, Nuers, Toposa, Buoya, Pari, Lopit, Mundari, Bari, Lokoyo, Lotuka that surround the Murle suffer the same atrocities though at a lower magnitude.
Bor in this situation has the longest border extension with the Murle; approximately 250 kilometers from Bor South County border with Terekaka State to Duk North County Border with Fangak State. One fact known to all is that there are no contact areas where the two communities annually meet for water and pastures as these scarce resources are always the cause of disputes and conflicts between pastoralists.
The worst in this situation is that most Murle leaders and elites cover up the mistakes and crimes of their communities. Instead they consider the acts of the members of their communities as heroism and bravery of their people and the communities raided or affected are considered to be cowards. Unfortunately, those usual denials did not last in the face of the raids on Ethiopia in March 2016 when Ethiopia thrust armed to teeth forces into the South Sudanese borders.
And to evade the consequences, all the Murle leaders, hysterically in confusion, beginning from the governor of Boma State to the lowest in social hierarchy hurried up in recovering over one hundred abducted children in a very short period of time. Even for the first time, members of Murle who are always known for covering up of the devilish crimes of their people, started to point fingers at each other.
While the latest peace conference was on session in Pibor between the 1st and 4th December 2016, the Murle were actively busy in Greater Bor Area killing people, abducting children and robbing livestock. For instance, on 3rd Dec. 2016, two women were killed and a child abducted in Bor North County and on 5th Dec. 2016, the Murle greeted and welcomed back the returning delegation from the peace conference by killing two women (sisters) and abducting one child in Twic North County. Those activities were a clear defiance to the peace conference that was on process in Pibor.
Since independence of Sudan from the Condominium Rule in 1956 till independence of South Sudan from Sudan in 2011, 12 (Twelve)) major and minor peace conferences were held between the Murle and the Bor Dinka and after any of these peace conferences, the Murle commit more horrific crimes on the people of Bor. Below are the many conferences held between the two communities for over 50 years since 1962.
1. Bor Conference in 1962
----------------------------------
The first peace conference between Murleand Bor Dinka was held 52 years ago in 1962 in Bor. The conference was co-chaired by Abas Babikr, the commissioner of Bor District and al- Bashir al- Wagie, the commissioner of Pibor District. Also, some chiefs from the two communities headed by Paramount Chiefs of Bor District, Ajang Duot and Ajakoor of the Murle attended. As the conference was held in the open under trees, members of the public including us, as students at Bor Intermediate by the time used to hang around as spectators.
Among those colleagues, I could recall in witnessing the conference as spectators from Murle community, were late Rio Ajakoor (son of Murle Paramount Chief Ajakoor), Martin Lotigo and others. Unfortunately, the resolutions reached were not implemented and the Murle instead continued with their usual evil practices.
By that time, Murle had not acquired firearms. Only spears were the common weapons.
2. Pibor Conference in 1975
-----------------------------------
In 1975, another peace conference that involved most communities of Upper Nile was convened in Pibor. Senior authorities and officials from the Regional Government in Juba and Upper Nile Province led by Abel Alier, the vice president of the republic and president of the High Executive Council attended the conference. Other dignitaries included Enoch Mading de Garang, minister of culture and information and Peter Gatkuoth, commissioner of Upper Nile Province.
Among chief present were paramount Chief David Mabior Ngueny for Bor District, Ajakoor Korok for Pibor, Makuei Bil Kuei, Chief Andrea Farajala of Juba B court and many other chiefs from other communities of Upper Nile. Police inspectors of all the nine districts of Upper Nile attended the conference. At the conclusion of the conference, resolutions were drastic to the extent that some chiefs were dismissed for laxity in administering their communities.
The conference dispersed with high hopes of peace and tranquility but the Murle considered the affair to be a government affair and not theirs and as such continued to intensify their criminal activities against Bor Dinka in particular and the neighboring communities in general.
3. Gadiang Conference in 1981
----------------------------------------
The conference was attended by all communities of Jonglei Province that got sliced out from Upper Nile in 1976 when more provinces were created in Southern Sudan. Abel Alier, the vice president and president of the High Executive Council attended the conference among other dignitaries including Johnson Malual Leek, the Jonglei Commissioner by the time.
Paramount chiefs from the various communities such as David Mabior Ngueny of Bor District, Gatwich Dual, the current SPLM –IO Chief of General Staff representing Lou Nuer and the Murle Paramount Chief were also in attendance.
The glittering resolutions reached could not last as the Murle immediately resumed their culture of raids into Bor and other neighbors.
In 1983, especially after the rebellion of Battalion 105 in Bor, the Murles, during successive raids on Amoumeth, Anyidi, Machar Dehr, Alian and Paliau cattle camps where over 250 people were in a period of less than a year.
4. Liliir Conference in 2001
---------------------------------
While the peace negotiations between the SPLM and the Salvation Government were on at Machakos in Kenya, Sudan Council of Churches in coordination with South Sudan Law Society convened a peace conference at Liliir village north of Bor Town. The conference drew many from the communities of Jonglei State. Among the dignitaries who attended the conference were Cdr. John Koang Nyuon, the then governor of Upper Nile and His deputy Cdr. Peter Wal Athieu.
Some commissioners, including Nicodemos Arou Man, the hosting commissioner also attended. Dr. Harun from the Sudan Council of Churches and Justice Dengtiel Ayuen Kur acted as the facilitators of the conference. Even from Khartoum, elders such as late Isaiah Kulang Mabor and late Johnson Malual Leek among others attended the gathering.
But when the conference concluded its meetings, the Murle flexed their muscles for further deadly attacks on their usual vulnerable Bor People.
5. Boma Conference on 10th March 2004
--------------------------------------------------- 
A mini Peace Conference attended by both communities of Murle and Bor was convened in Boma. Unfortunately, Murle did not tune to the coexistence spirit.
6. Anyidi Conference on 20th March 2004
----------------------------------------------------
In 2004 when some Murle cattle camps migrated to Bor in search of water and pastures, the hosting communities dispersed them along the area in order to avoid congestion on water points. That opportunity was exploited by Philip Thon Nok, the peace project officer by the time in coordination with Bor South County Authorities to convene a mini peace conference between the Bor Dinka and the visiting Murle Community in the area led by chief Gulic.
Among the dignitaries who attended the conference included Cdr. Peter Wal Athieu, Cdr. Machar Akeu, Maker Chol Adol, Cdr. Kazakia Ruei Puot, the then Bor South County Commissioner and Panchol Jongkuc Kur, the SSRA Secretary.
That conference also ended with usual claims of opening a new page but the always defiant Murle continued their activities.
7. Bor Town Conference (November 2005)
-------------------------------------------------------
With the implementation of the Comprehensive Peace Agreement (CPA), a peace conference was convened in Bor Town between the two communities of Murle and Bor. That conference was attended by Philip Thon Leek and Ismail Konyi, former Governors of Jonglei State, Jude Jonglei, speaker of Jonglei State and Isaiah Chol Aruei, Abraham Jok Ariing and Mayen Ngor, commissioners of Twic East, Bor and Duk Counties respectively. Members of Jonglei Assembly from both Communities attended the conference. That conference met the same fate of the previous ones and the Murle resumed their activities against the people of Bor.
8. Gumuruk Conference in 2006
------------------------------------------
The conference brought along all the six communities of Jonglei State and importantly, the conference was attended by the top leadership of the Government of Southern Sudan (GOSS) headed by Dr. Riek Machar, the former vice president of the Government of the Southern Sudan, Daniel Awet Akot, former minister of Interior, Clement Wani Konga, former Governor of Central Equatoria, Philip Thon Leek, former Governor of Jonglei State, commissioners of various counties of Jonglei State, king of Anyuak beside paramount chiefs and chiefs of various present communities.
Of course, with that high-level attendance by the government authorities, people thought that was the end of conflicts between the Murle and the neighboring communities, but instead the Murle continued to violate the agreement.
9. The Jonglei Reconciliation and Peace Conference (2011)
---------------------------------------------------------------------------
The Government despite the continuous violations of agreements by Murles, Gen. Salva Kiir Mayardit, the President of the Republic of South Sudan thought of involving the church and as such decreed the formation of a peace and reconciliation committee under the chairmanship of His Grace Daniel Deng Bul, the Archbishop of the Episcopal Church of Sudan and South Sudan. And not to leave any stone unturned, committees were formed to visit all counties of Jonglei State in order to dig out the root causes of the conflicts.
When the committees compiled their reports, a general conference was convened in Bor where notes were compared and resolutions drowned. In order to assure commitment of all communities to the resolutions, the resolutions were signed by four paramount chiefs representing the Greater Counties of former Jonglei State; among them Ngatho, the paramount chief of Pibor.
The signing ceremony was witnessed by President Salva Kiir, Michael Makuei Lueth, the national minister of information, Gen. Kuol Manyang Juuk, former Governor of Jonglei State, His Grace Daniel Deng Bul, Archbishop of the Episcopal Church, myself as Bor County Commissioner by the time and many other dignitaries from the national and state governments.
The Murle did not care whether the president attended or not and as usual violated the agreement reached and vigorously continued to step up their raids into Bor and the neighboring communities.
10. Gumuruk Conference 19th August 2016
In trying to bring about peace between the Murle and Bor Dinka, both Baba Medan and Philip Aguer Panyang, the governors of Boma and Jonglei States thought of trying once more what the President, vice presidents, governors and church failed to achieve during 52 years period and as such convened a one day conference at Gumuruk in Boma State. Unfortunately, the conference did not bear fruits.
11. Bor Conference 20th 9 2016
-----------------------------------------
In reciprocating to the Gumuruk mini conference, another similar white washing conference was hurriedly convened at South Sudan Hotel in Bor amidst the roaring rotaries of UNMISS Choppers at Bor Airport. The result of the conference was launching more raids into Bor!
12. Pibor Conference 1st -4th Dec. 2016
---------------------------------------------------
Between 1st and 4th, the two states convened a peace conference in Pibor between the two communities of Murle and Bor Dinka attended by dignitaries from the two states of Jonglei and Boma led by the two governors Philip Aguer and Baba Medan. While the conferees were at the pomp of congratulating themselves on the great achievement for the lasting peace, the Murle were inflicting atrocities on the people of Bor.
On the 3rd December while the two parties were on the negotiating table, the Murle killed two women in Bor North County and abducted one child. On the 5th December 2016 when the conferees were returning to their places, the Murle attacked a village in Twic North County and killed two women who happened to be sisters, and walked away with one child.
It is reported that, while the two communities were negotiating, the Lou Nuer sent in an urgent message to the Boma State Government to immediately recover four Lou Nuer children the Murle abducted some few days earlier to the conference. The Lou Nuer gave an ultimatum of two days otherwise they would be forced to invade the area.
The Boma Government hysterically in no time recovered the four children among them a three-month-old baby! The Lou Nuer copied the example of the Ethiopian Government when she thrust thousands of her troops into the South Sudanese border. The usual techniques of denial by Mrule’s leaders could not work in front of the mighty Lou Nuer and the Ethiopian Government!!!
All the conferences held with the Murle are liken to a story of an Imam (A Muslim Cleric) who was advising a hyena against eating people’s sheep and goats as the consequences were going to be bad at the resurrection time. And while listening keenly to the Imam, a herd of sheep appeared in front of them. On seeing the sheep, the hyena appealed to the Imam to shorten his advice as he was going to miss the herd!!
Twelve Peace Conferences held in a span of 52 years of which some of them were attended by top leaders of South Sudan including President Salva Kiir, Vice President Abel Alier and Vice President Riek Machar but the Murle continued defiant!!!
The millions of Dollars or pounds spent on these twelve peace conferences between the Murles, Dinka, Nuers and others, had it been utilized on roads, water reservoirs, health facilities, schools and construction of security posts between the communities, at least the situation would have changed to some extent. It is not too late to catch up.
The unfortunate part is that Murle Community has no central authority. It is led by the generation group whose objective is to precede the previous generations in criminality. The best leader for them is the one who encourages malpractices ranging from robbery, child abduction to killing.
The International Community which is playing the role of sponsoring and supporting peace dialogue initiatives in South Sudan has no interest other than to continue accessing employment and training of their inexperience people such that when they return to their homes of origin, they would claim to be experts and to confer upon themselves the specialization in South Sudanese affairs.
From the above narrative, it is obvious that all the peace conferences failed miserably. No South Sudanese national in his full senses would applaud and support the death of his or her compatriots South Sudanese. Why not reverting to other options if the peace dialogues had reached a dead lock? It is time for the government to intervene in order to bring about a lasting peace among the communities of South Sudan.
If the IGAD, AU, TROIKA and UN could impose a solution on the opposition and the government on a conflict that lasted for two years only why not imposing a solution in order to resolve a conflict that lasted for nearly two centuries? The government should intervene in order to stop the bloodletting in the former Greater Jonglei State. But while the government is considering any other possible option, may I be allowed as a disturbed citizen to put forward the below suggestions:
(a) Short term solutions
Establishment of border security points.
Security roads to be constructed along the borders separating the neighboring communities that are consistently on conflicts. Security posts to be situated at every 10 kilometers’ interval. At Ajakgeer 53 kilometers east of Bor Town, UNDP constructed an observatory police post and wild life conservation office. Similar facilities were supposed to be concurrently constructed at Mach-Abol in Boma State.
2. Availing of Water for livestock and human.
As water is a crucial element for the pastoralist communities during the dry season, it is necessary that water reservoirs are constructed at strategic points for the drinking of both the livestock and the wild life. Also boreholes are to be drilled near the reservoirs for the provision of clean drinking water to the population.
3. A monitoring team where all the affected communities are to be represented. The team to be stationed in Pibor to monitor the criminal activities of the different communities.
(b) Long term Solution
There is a large semi empty area surrounded by the communities of the different states. That area is estimated at about five million hectares of arable land. That area could be converted into large agricultural schemes where by communities surrounding it can benefit from it. During the British Colonial period, a research conducted on sugar cane production in Mangala proved that sugar content in sugar cane planted was 14%.
That research made the area to be potential for the growth of sugar cane that could supply a sugar factory that can meet the country requirement from processed sugar. Unfortunately, our former colonialist, the Arab North constructed sugar factories at Geneid, Khashum al- Girba, Asalaya, West Sennar and Kenana. During Numiery industrial revolution, one sugar factory was constructed at Melut, but never started operations or production till present moment.
Initiatives for peaceful dialogues are commendable but if no progress seen in the horizon, other options are to be resorted to.
The author, Maker Lual Kuol, is the former commissioner of Bor County.

Hukum wanita haid membaca AL QUR'AN Di dalam mazhab syafi'i.

wanita haid, tidak boleh baca AL QUR'AN, kecuali mulutnya saja gerak-gerak tanpa keluar suara karena imam  Syafi'i di samakan dengan orang junub yaitu tidak boleh membaca AL QUR'AN. 

Merujuk pendapat kuat (pendapat Shahih) dalam mazhab Syafi’i hukumnya adalah haram.  

Argumentasi pendapat yang mengharamkannya adalah hadits riwayat At-Tirmidzi dan selainnya yang melarang orang junub dan haid membaca sedikitpun Al-Qur’an. Rasulullah saw bersabda:

لَا يَقْرَأْ الْجُنُبُ وَلَا الْحَائِضُ شَيْئًا مِنْ الْقُرْآن

ِArtinya: 

“Janganlah orang junub dan wanita haid membaca sesuatupun dari Al-Qur’an". (HR At-Tirmidzi, Al-Baihaqi dan lainnya). 

Meski hadits sempat dinilai dhaif oleh Imam An-Nawawi, namun memiliki penguat dari riwayat lain sehingga berstatus hasan, sebagaimana  ditegaskan oleh Ibnu Hajar Al-Haitami dan Al-Mundziri. 

Demikian pula menurut Ibnu Jamaah dalamTakhrijul Ahaditsir Rafi’i, setelah menelitinya kemudian ia menegaskan bahwa hadits ini menjadi kuat dengan hadits-hadits lain yang mendukungnya.(Ibnu Hajar Al-Haitami,Al-Minhajul Qawim).

Tapi wanita haid boleh membaca dzikir,meskipun Dzikir tersebut ada dalam AL QUR'AN,dan membaca Do'a untuk perlindungan seperti Do'a mau tidur dsb. 

suatu kemudahan dalam syariat islam yaitu mazhab Malik,wanita boleh  membaca AL QUR'AN dengan syarat : 

 1.tidak boleh menyentuh atau memegang AL QUR'AN.  

2.hanya untuk belajar, mengajar termasuk menjaga hafalannya atau menambah hafalan nya dengan syarat tidak boleh sampai khatam. 

 وَذَهَبَ الْمَالِكِيَّةُ إِلَى أَنَّ الْحَائِضَ يَجُوزُ لَهَا قِرَاءَةُ الْقُرْآنِ فِي حَال اسْتِرْسَال الدَّمِ مُطْلَقًا، كَانَتْ جُنُبًا أَمْ لاَ، خَافَتِ النِّسْيَانَ أَمْ لاَ. وَأَمَّا إِذَا انْقَطَعَ حَيْضُهَا، فَلاَ تَجُوزُ لَهَا الْقِرَاءَةُ حَتَّى تَغْتَسِل جُنُبًا كَانَتْ أَمْ لاَ، إِلاَّ أَنْ تَخَافَ النِّسْيَان - وزارة الأوقاف والشؤن الإسلامية الكويت، الموسوعة الفقهية الكويتية، الكويت- دار السلاسل

“Kalangan dari madzhab maliki berpendapat bahwa orang yang haid boleh baginya membaca Al-Qur`an dalam kondisi masih mengeluarkan darah secara mutlak, baik dalam keadaan atau tidak, atau adanya kekhawatiran lupa hafalan Al-Qur’an-nya atau tidak. 

Adapun setelah haidnya terputus maka ia tidak boleh membacanya sebelum mandi besar, baik dalam keadaan junub atau tidak, kecuali ia khawatir akan lupa hafalannya”. (Wazarah al-Awqaf wa asy-Syu`un al-Islamiyyah Kuwait,al-Mausu’ah al-Fiqhiyyah al-Kuwaitiyyah, Kuwait-Dar as-Salasil, juz, 18, h. 322 H) 

Jadi anda boleh membaca nya tanpa harus menyentuhnya,biarkan santri anda yang menyentuh dan membuka nya,dan membaca nya secukupnya kalau santri anda sudah bisa membaca nya anda tidak perlu membaca nya. 

Larangan bagi wanita haid atau wanita nifas : 

1.sholat. 

2.puasa 

3.thowaf 

4.menyentuh AL QUR'AN. 

5.membawa AL QUR'AN 

6.membaca AL QUR'AN. 

7.masuk Mesjid jika khawatir mengotori. 

 

Larangan bagi orang junub : 

1.sholat 

2.thowaf 

3.berdiam di Mesjid 

4.memegang atau menyentuh AL  QUR'AN 

5.membaca AL QUR'AN 

6.membawa AL QUR'AN. 

7.Sujud tilawah 

8.Sujud syukur. 

9.Sujud sahwi. 

WalloHu'alam bishowab.

As this year comes to a close, I can honestly say I chose peace and focus above everything else.

I have been intentionally quiet and to myself, not because I was lost, but because I was building. This year was about alignment, discipline, and protecting my energy. I stopped explaining. I stopped forcing. I stayed focused.

I poured into my two kids, strengthened relationships that showed authenticity, and created distance from anyone who lacked loyalty or was not a true fit in my life. I chose quality over proximity and peace over familiarity.

I also take full responsibility for my life, both past and present experiences. Every lesson, every shift, and every outcome played a role in shaping who I am today.

I learned that growth does not always need an audience. Sometimes the real work happens in silence.

This year reminded me to
- Choose myself without guilt
- Move with intention not urgency
- Honor my boundaries and keep them firm
- Let go of what no longer fits
- Trust the process even when it feels slow
- Stay authentic even when it is uncomfortable

I am proud of how I showed up for myself. Calm. Grounded. Focused. Clear.

Not everything needs to be shared. Some chapters are meant to be lived.

Grateful for the lessons. Ready for what is next.

I’m the mother. You don’t get to disrespect me, make my life hell, try to break me, and still expect full access to me and my child without consequences.

You don’t get to tear me down and then act like nothing happened. You don’t get to treat me like I’m disposable and still demand I make everything easy for you. You don’t get to hurt me repeatedly and face zero accountability.

I will always prioritize my child. But that doesn’t mean I have to tolerate your disrespect, your manipulation, or your attempts to destroy my peace.

Co-parenting requires mutual respect. If you can’t give that, then boundaries will be set. Consequences will follow. And access to me—my time, my energy, my cooperation—will be limited to what’s necessary for our child.

I’m done being a doormat. I’m done accepting mistreatment in silence because “it’s easier.” I’m done pretending your behavior is acceptable just to keep the peace.

Respect me or expect boundaries. It’s that simple.

You chose how you treated me. Now deal with the consequences.

As we welcome the New Year 2026, we pause to reflect with gratitude on a year that shaped us. قيادة تحالف قوى المعارضة (SSOA) تعلن التبرؤ من “فصيل جوزفين” وتؤكد التزامها باتفاق السلام

جوبا | الحرية 

أعلنت قيادة تحالف قوى المعارضة في جنوب السودان (SSOA)، برئاسة الفريق حسين عبدالباقي أكول، تبرؤها الرسمي والقاطع من مجموعة يُشار إليها علنًا باسم “فصيل جوزفين داخل SSOA”، متهمةً إياها بمخالفة القرارات الجماعية وتقويض مسار السلام والانتقال الديمقراطي في البلاد، وذلك في بيانٍ تحصّلت عليه "الحرية".

وقال التحالف، في البيان، إن القرار جاء عقب مشاورات واسعة وتقييم شامل للسلوك السياسي للفصيل المعني، الذي دأب بحسب البيان على اتخاذ مواقف تتعارض مع وحدة الهدف والتوجه الاستراتيجي للتحالف، وتنتهك روح ونص اتفاقية السلام المُنشَّطة.

وأوضح البيان أن الفصيل المتبرأ منه عارض قرارًا قياديًا جماعيًا يقضي بالتخلي عن القوات وألقاب القائد العام لصالح القائد الدستوري الأعلى الوحيد، رئيس الجمهورية الفريق أول سلفاكير ميارديت، عبر حملات دعائية وتصريحات عامة هدفت إلى نزع الشرعية عن القرار وإفشاله، رغم اتخاذه خدمةً للوحدة الوطنية وإصلاح القطاع الأمني وتحقيق السلام المستدام.

وأضاف التحالف أن الفصيل رفض كذلك قرار قيادة SSOA التخلي عن الجناح العسكري وتسليمه للقائد الأعلى للقوات النظامية، ما يعرقل عملية إعادة الدمج والنشر، ويسعى إلى الاحتفاظ بعناصر مسلحة لخدمة مصالح شخصية وسياسية ضيقة.

وأشار البيان إلى أن الفصيل أبدى معارضة واضحة لإجراء الانتخابات الديمقراطية المرتقبة، بما يقوض إرادة وتطلعات شعب جنوب السودان، ويعرقل انتقال البلاد نحو نظام دستوري ديمقراطي شرعي. كما اتهم البيان السيدة جوزفين بمحاولات متكررة لعرقلة مبادرة قيادة التحالف الهادفة إلى توحيد القيادة الدستورية العليا، وإزالة بنود مُجازة أصولًا من جدول أعمال مجلس الوزراء، في ما وصفه التحالف بنمط متعمد من التعطيل تحكمه المصالح الذاتية.

وكشف البيان أن بعض أعضاء الفصيل، رغم عضويتهم في اللجنة القانونية الرئاسية التي شكّلتها الرئاسة الموسعة، امتنعوا عمدًا عن التوقيع على خارطة الطريق الفنية والاستراتيجية المتفق عليها لإنقاذ المرحلة الانتقالية والتمهيد لإجراء الانتخابات في ديسمبر 2026، إضافة إلى تحشيد بعض أعضاء آلية المراقبة والتقييم المُعاد تشكيلها (R-JMEC) لمعارضة قرارات أُجيزت واعتمدت قانونيًا من قبل الرئاسة الموسعة ومجلس الوزراء.

وأكد تحالف قوى المعارضة في جنوب السودان التزامه الثابت بالتنفيذ الكامل لاتفاقية السلام المُنشَّطة، وإصلاح القطاع الأمني، وإجراء الانتخابات الديمقراطية، وتحقيق انتقال سلمي للسلطة. ودعا جميع الأحزاب المكوِّنة للتحالف وأعضائه وأنصاره إلى النأي بأنفسهم عن القيادات “الانتهازية والمُفرِّقة”، والوقوف بحزم إلى جانب السلام والوحدة والشرعية المؤسسية مع دخول البلاد المرحلة الانتخابية.

وختم البيان بالتشديد على أن تحالف SSOA سيظل ثابت العزم على دفع مسار المصالحة الوطنية، وتعزيز الوحدة الوطنية، وبناء مستقبل ديمقراطي سلمي لجمهورية جنوب السودان.

The Leadership of the South Sudan Opposition Alliance (SSOA), under the chairmanship of Hon. This decision follows extensive consultations and a thorough assessment of the political conduct of this group, which has consistently acted contrary to the collective resolutions, unity of purpose, and strategic direction of SOA, as well as the spirit and letter of the Revitalized Peace Agreement.

The disowned group has persistently adopted positions that fundamentally undermine peace, stability, and democratic transition, including:

1. Actively opposing and undermining the collective leadership decision of SSOA to relinquish its forces and Command-in-Chief (C-in-C) titles to the sole constitutional Commander-in-Chief, HE. Salva Kiir Mayardit, through sustained propaganda, misinformation, and public statements intended to delegitimize and sabotage this historic and lawful decision, taken in the supreme interest of national unity, security sector reform, and lasting peace.

2. Rejecting the decision taken by SSOA Leadership under Hon. Hussein Abdelbagi Akol to relinquish the military wing from SSOA to the Supreme Commander of regular forces, HE. Gen. Salva Kiir Mayardit, thereby obstructing the reintegration and deployment of SOA forces, and attempting to retain armed elements for narrow personal and political interests.

3. Demonstrating clear opposition to the forthcoming democratic elections, thereby undermining the will and aspirations of the people of South Sudan and obstructing the country's transition toward a legitimate constitutional and democratic order.

4. Hon. Josephine has persistently attempted to block the leadership initiative of Hon.Hussein Abdelbagi Akol aimed at relinquishing SSOA forces and C-in-C titles to establish one constitutional Commander-in-Chief, a cornerstone decision essential for unifying the security sector and consolidating peace. Her efforts to have this duly adopted agenda removed from Cabinet consideration further demonstrate a deliberate pattern of obstruction driven by self-interest rather than national interest.

Furthermore, it is on record that members of Josephine’s faction, despite being part of the Presidential Legal Committee formed by the Expanded Presidency, deliberately refused to append their signatures to the agreed technical and strategic roadmap intended to rescue the transtition, restore confident and create minimum political and legal conditions necessary for a peaceful and credible end to transitional period for the timely conduct of  elections in December 2026. This refusal exposes their real intention to sabotage the ammendments process. More troubling is their continued mobilization of members of R-JMEC to oppose decisions lawfully passed and adopted by both the Expanded Presidency and the Council of Ministers in the RJMEC meeting, thereby undermining the peace implementation framework.
 
SSOA reiterates its unwavering commitment to the full implementation of the Revitalized Peace Agreement, security sector reforms, democratic elections, and a peaceful transition in the Republic of South Sudan.
 
In light of the above, the Leadership of SSOA strongly urges all constituent parties, members, and supporters of the Alliance to distance themselves from such self-serving and divisive leaders, and to stand firmly on the side of peace, unity, institutional legitimacy, and democratic transition as the country enters the electoral period.
 
SSOA remains resolute in advancing reconciliation, national unity, and a peaceful democratic future for South Sudan.

On behalf of the SSOA Leadership

Despite these challenges, Ms Wilson noted that what stood out most was the faith leaders’ deep commitment to their communities and their shared dedication to a respectful celebration of all faiths within Australia’s multicultural society.

PRESS STATEMENT
Date: January 4, 2026
For Immediate Release

SPLM-IO STRONGLY CONDEMNS THE ATTACK ON PROTECTION OF CIVILIANS (POCs) SITES IN UNITY STATE.

The Sudan People’s Liberation Movement–In Opposition (SPLM-IO) strongly and unequivocally condemns the attack on Protection of Civilians (POCs) sites in Unity State. This attack constitutes a grave violation of international humanitarian law and a direct assault on innocent civilians who are entitled to protection under both national and international legal frameworks.

The Unified Forces stationed in the POCs were deployed there pursuant to an agreed security arrangement with the Government of the Republic of South Sudan. Their mandate was clear and limited solely to the protection of civilians. At no time were the POCs intended to serve as a military base for SPLM/A-IO or any other armed group. Any attempt to justify attacks on civilians under such false pretexts is misleading, unacceptable, and unlawful.

Even if Government forces withdrew from the area due to heightened tensions, such a withdrawal does not, and can never justify attacks on civilians. Unity State contains several SPLM/A-IO forces located outside civilian areas; however, the SSPDF has conspicuously avoided engaging those forces and instead targeted POCs where displaced and unarmed civilians reside. This deliberate conduct demonstrates intent and reflects a cowardly and unlawful use of force in and around civilian populations.

These actions constitute serious violations of Common Article 3 of the Geneva Conventions, Additional Protocol II, and may amount to war crimes and crimes against humanity under Articles 7 and 8 of the Rome Statute of the International Criminal Court. Those responsible, including individuals who ordered, facilitated, or condoned these attacks, bear criminal responsibility under international law.

The SPLM-IO calls upon the United Nations, UNMISS, the African Union, IGAD, and the wider international community to take urgent note of this attack on displaced civilians in Unity State and to act decisively to ensure accountability and the immediate protection of civilians. The continued targeting of displaced populations, predominantly Nuer civilians, is nothing but a  continues systematic and ethnically motivated violence that must not be ignored this time.

The protection of civilians is a binding legal and moral obligation. Violations of this principle threaten the prospects for lasting peace and stability in South Sudan.

The SPLM-IO remains fully committed to the protection of civilians and to strict adherence to international humanitarian and human rights law.
Yours truly,

Hon. Reath Muoch Tang, 
Acting Chairperson, National Committee on Foreign Relations, and former Member of the Transitional National Legislative Assembly,  SPLM-IO

SPLM-IO STRONGLY CONDEMNS THE ATTACK ON PROTECTION OF CIVILIANS (POCs) SITES IN UNITY STATE.

The Unified Forces stationed in the POCs were deployed there pursuant to an agreed security arrangement with the Government of the Republic of South Sudan. Their mandate was clear and limited solely to the protection of civilians. At no time were the POCs intended to serve as a military base for SPLM/A-IO or any other armed group. Any attempt to justify attacks on civilians under such false pretexts is misleading, unacceptable, and unlawful.

Even if Government forces withdrew from the area due to heightened tensions, such a withdrawal does not, and can never justify attacks on civilians. Unity State contains several SPLM/A-IO forces located outside civilian areas; however, the SSPDF has conspicuously avoided engaging those forces and instead targeted POCs where displaced and unarmed civilians reside. The continued targeting of displaced populations, predominantly Nuer civilians, is nothing but a  continues systematic and ethnically motivated violence that must not be ignored this time.

The protection of civilians is a binding legal and moral obligation. Violations of this principle threaten the prospects for lasting peace and stability in South Sudan.

The SPLM-IO remains fully committed to the protection of civilians and to strict adherence to international humanitarian and human rights law.

Patriarch Ibrahim Ishaq and Patriarch Youssef Absi Congratulate Pope Tawadros II on the Nativity

— القاهرة | 05 يناير (كانون الثاني) 2026 

⭕️ استقبل قداسة البابا تواضروس الثاني، بابا الإسكندرية وبطريرك الكرازة المرقسية، اليوم بمقره البابوي بالعباسية، غبطة البطريرك الأنبا إبراهيم إسحق، بطريرك الإسكندرية للأقباط الكاثوليك ورئيس مجلس البطاركة والأساقفة الكاثوليك بمصر، وغبطة البطريرك يوسف العبسي، بطريرك أنطاكية والإسكندرية وأورشليم وسائر المشرق للروم الملكيين الكاثوليك، في زيارة تهنئة بمناسبة عيد الميلاد المجيد ورأس السنة الميلادية.

🎄استهل غبطة البطريرك الأنبا إبراهيم إسحق كلمته بالتعبير عن سعادته بلقاء قداسة البابا، مؤكدًا على المحبة المتبادلة التي تجمع جميع المسيحيين في جسد المسيح الواحد، متمنيًا أن يكون عيد الميلاد مناسبة للسلام والرجاء في مصر والعالم أجمع.

🎄 من جانبه، ألقى قداسة البابا تواضروس الثاني كلمة روحانية تناول فيها سرّ الجمع والوحدة في المسيح، مشيرًا إلى أن الإفخارستيا تمثل علامة الوحدة الحقيقية بين جميع المسيحيين. وأكد قداسة البابا أن المسيح جاء من أجل الفقير والغني، ومن أجل جميع البشر، ليكون الجميع واحدًا فيه، داعيًا إلى تعزيز روح المحبة والتعاون بين جميع الكنائس في خدمة المجتمع والشهادة للمسيح.

🎄وألقى غبطة البطريرك يوسف العبسي كلمة أشار فيها إلى أن سرّي المعمودية والتجسّد يجمعان جميع المسيحيين في جسد المسيح الواحد، مؤكدًا أن الميلاد الإلهي هو مصدر الرجاء والوحدة، داعيًا إلى استمرار الحوار المسيحي والتعاون بين الكنائس لما فيه خير الشعب المصري والعالم المسيحي.

🎄واختتمت الزيارة بتبادل التهاني والهدايا التذكارية، في أجواء من الألفة والمحبة المسيحية، تأكيدًا على الروابط الروحية التي تجمع الكنائس المختلفة في مصر.

▫️نيافة المطران كريكور أغسطينوس كوسا، مطران أبرشية الإسكندرية و مصر والسودان للأرمن الكاثوليك

▫️الخورأسقف بولس ساتي للفادي الأقدس، المدبر البطريركي للكلدان بمصر
