EU warns of rising violence, urges constitution-making continuity

The European Union has expressed concern over rising violence in South Sudan and called for the uninterrupted continuation of the country’s permanent constitution-making process.

Ambassador Pelle Enarsson, Head of the European Union Delegation to South Sudan, made the remarks during a workshop on federalism organised by the National Constitutional Review Commission (NCRC) in Juba.

Speaking at the opening on Wednesday, Enarsson said the EU was “deeply concerned” by the recent escalation of violence, and stressed the need for dialogue and political agreements to halt fighting and restore full implementation of the 2018 revitalised peace agreement.

“There is a clear need for more dialogue and for political agreements to stop the violence and come back to the implementation of the peace agreement,” he said.

He added that, despite political and security challenges, the work of the NCRC on the permanent constitution must continue, and urged mechanisms to ensure continuity beyond the current transitional period.

Enarsson reaffirmed the EU’s support for the constitutional process through its partnership with the Max Planck Foundation for International Peace and the Rule of Law.

“We are really proud to be able to support this project,” he said, wishing participants a successful workshop.

The federalism workshop is part of an ongoing series designed to inform South Sudan’s constitution-making through public consultations and technical discussions on governance structures.

Dr Kathrin Scherr, senior legal expert at the Max Planck Foundation, said the three-day session focuses on legislative and executive design in federal systems and the role of local government. She noted that it builds on four previous workshops since 2024 covering power sharing, fiscal devolution, wealth sharing, and constitutionalism.

Scherr praised the NCRC for conducting public consultations in eight states and said the workshop was shaped by feedback from the commission to address issues most relevant to South Sudan’s federal governance debate.

Dr Riang Yier Zuor, chairperson of the NCRC, said the workshop is the fifth in the federalism series launched in 2024 and the first for 2026. He said discussions include comparative case studies, local government structures, functions, and fiscal arrangements.

Zuor expressed hope the engagement would strengthen the commission’s understanding of federal governance and announced plans for an additional workshop on models and management of federal capitals. He thanked the Max Planck Foundation and the European Union for their continued support.

Last month, the presidency and cabinet approved amendments to key provisions of the 2018 peace agreement, delinking the December 2026 elections from the permanent constitution-making process, a national census and other institutional reforms.

The amendments also removed provisions stating that the peace agreement takes precedence over the transitional constitution.

The proposed amendments are currently under review by the monitoring body RJMEC.

OEM คืออะไร? สำคัญยังไงกับธุรกิจนำเข้าส่งออก?

OEM (Original Equipment Manufacturer) = "ผู้ผลิตตามสั่งให้แบรนด์อื่น"

หมายความว่า...
คุณไม่จำเป็นต้องมีโรงงานเอง ก็สามารถมีสินค้าเป็นของตัวเองได้ แค่จ้างโรงงาน (OEM) ผลิตสินค้า แล้วนำไปติดแบรนด์คุณเอง

แล้วเกี่ยวอะไรกับการนำเข้าส่งออก?

ผู้นำเข้า: สามารถสั่งสินค้าจากต่างประเทศให้ผลิตตามแบรนด์ตัวเอง

ผู้ส่งออก: ไทยสามารถรับจ้างผลิตสินค้าให้แบรนด์ต่างชาติ แล้วส่งออกไปขาย

สร้างแบรนด์ไทยขายต่างประเทศ โดยไม่ต้องมีโรงงานเอง

เพิ่มมูลค่า เพิ่มโอกาสทางการตลาด

ข้อดีของการใช้ OEM:

ไม่ต้องลงทุนโรงงาน

คุมดีไซน์และแบรนด์ได้เอง

เหมาะกับคนเริ่มต้นธุรกิจหรืออยากขยายตลาดเร็ว

ยกตัวอย่างง่ายๆ:
คุณอยากขายน้ำผลไม้พร้อมดื่มที่ออสเตรเลีย
คุณออกแบบแบรนด์ → จ้างโรงงานในไทยผลิต → ส่งออกไปขาย
= ใช้ระบบ OEM เต็มรูปแบบ

ขนส่งทางเรือ VS ทางอากาศ: แบบไหนใช่สำหรับธุรกิจคุณ?

เมื่อพูดถึงการนำเข้าสินค้าจากต่างประเทศ คำถามสำคัญที่เจ้าของธุรกิจหลายคนต้องเจอคือ “จะส่งทางเรือหรือส่งทางอากาศดี?” ทั้งสองแบบมีข้อดีข้อเสียแตกต่างกัน ขึ้นอยู่กับความต้องการและลักษณะของสินค้า มาดูกันว่าแบบไหนเหมาะกับคุณมากที่สุด

#ขนส่งทางอากาศ (Air Freight) เหมาะกับสินค้าที่ต้องการความรวดเร็ว เช่น สินค้าแฟชั่นตามฤดูกาล อะไหล่เครื่องจักรที่ต้องใช้ด่วน หรือของที่มีมูลค่าสูง น้ำหนักเบา ข้อดีคือใช้เวลาน้อยมาก โดยส่วนใหญ่ภายในไม่กี่วันสินค้าก็ถึงปลายทางแล้ว อีกทั้งยังปลอดภัยจากความเสียหายเพราะไม่ต้องเจอความชื้นหรือระยะเวลาขนส่งที่ยาวนานเหมือนทางเรือ

แต่ข้อเสียสำคัญของการส่งทางอากาศคือ “ราคา” เพราะค่าขนส่งต่อกิโลกรัมค่อนข้างสูง ยิ่งถ้าสินค้ามีน้ำหนักมากก็ยิ่งแพง จึงไม่เหมาะกับการส่งสินค้าจำนวนมากหรือสินค้าที่มีน้ำหนักเยอะ

#ขนส่งทางเรือ (Sea Freight) เป็นทางเลือกยอดนิยมสำหรับการนำเข้าสินค้าปริมาณมาก เช่น เฟอร์นิเจอร์ เครื่องจักร หรือสินค้าสต๊อก เพราะต้นทุนต่อหน่วยถูกกว่ามาก โดยเฉพาะเมื่อใช้ตู้คอนเทนเนอร์แบบเต็มตู้ (FCL) หรือแชร์ตู้ร่วมกับผู้นำเข้ารายอื่น (LCL)

อย่างไรก็ตาม การส่งทางเรือต้องใช้เวลาเป็นสัปดาห์ หรือในบางเส้นทางอาจเกือบเดือน และยังมีความเสี่ยงเรื่องล่าช้าจากพิธีการศุลกากร หรือสภาพอากาศที่ไม่แน่นอน จึงเหมาะกับสินค้าที่ไม่เร่งด่วน

สรุปง่ายๆ:

ถ้าคุณต้องการความเร็ว และสินค้าไม่หนักมาก → เลือกส่งทางอากาศ

ถ้าคุณต้องการประหยัดต้นทุน และสามารถรอสินค้าได้ → ส่งทางเรือคือคำตอบ

การเลือกวิธีขนส่งให้เหมาะสมไม่เพียงแต่ช่วยประหยัดงบ ยังเพิ่มประสิทธิภาพในการวางแผนธุรกิจอีกด้วย

รู้จัก "21 หมวด HS CODE" พื้นฐานสำคัญของการนำเข้าส่งออก ที่เจ้าของธุรกิจต้องเข้าใจ!

หลายคนอาจเคยได้ยินคำว่า HS CODE หรือ พิกัดศุลกากร เวลาเราจะนำเข้าหรือส่งออกสินค้า แต่รู้ไหมว่าแต่ละรหัสไม่ได้ตั้งมั่วๆ — ทุกอย่างมีระบบที่ "ใช้กันทั่วโลก" และไทยก็ใช้เหมือนกันใน 6 หลักแรก!

HS CODE (Harmonized System) คือ ระบบจัดหมวดหมู่สินค้ามาตรฐานสากล โดยใช้ตัวเลขเพื่อบอกว่า "สินค้านั้นคืออะไร" ใช้ทำอะไร และทำจากอะไร เพื่อให้ด่านศุลกากรของทุกประเทศรู้ตรงกัน
ปัจจุบันมี 21 หมวดหลัก ซึ่งเป็นหมวดเดียวกับที่ใช้ในไทย และประเทศอื่นๆ ส่วนมากก็ใช้เหมือนกัน

---

21 หมวด HS CODE มีอะไรบ้าง? (อ่านง่าย จำได้เลย)

1. สัตว์มีชีวิต / สินค้าจากสัตว์

2. สินค้าจากพืช / วัตถุดิบเกษตร

3. ไขมัน น้ำมันจากสัตว์และพืช

4. อาหาร เครื่องดื่ม สุรา น้ำตาล

5. ผลิตภัณฑ์แร่ เช่น เกลือ หินแร่

6. เคมีภัณฑ์ เช่น ปุ๋ย สี สารเคมี

7. พลาสติกและยาง

8. หนังแท้ หนังเทียม และผลิตภัณฑ์จากหนัง

9. ไม้และของที่ทำจากไม้

10. เยื่อไม้ กระดาษ กล่อง บรรจุภัณฑ์

11. สิ่งทอ ผ้า เสื้อผ้า ของทำจากผ้า

12. ของสำเร็จรูป (ของเบ็ดเตล็ดทั่วไป)

13. หิน แก้ว เซรามิก เครื่องปั้นดินเผา

14. ไข่มุก เพชรพลอย รัตนชาติ

15. โลหะและผลิตภัณฑ์จากโลหะ

16. เครื่องจักร อุปกรณ์ไฟฟ้า อิเล็กทรอนิกส์

17. ยานยนต์ เครื่องบิน เรือ

18. อุปกรณ์ทางการแพทย์ เครื่องดนตรี ฯลฯ

19. อาวุธและกระสุน

20. ของเบ็ดเตล็ด (ที่จัดไม่เข้าหมวดอื่น)

21. ศิลปะ โบราณวัตถุ ของสะสม

แล้วประเทศไทยใช้เหมือนต่างประเทศไหม?

ตอบเลยว่า “เหมือน” ใน 6 หลักแรก

ทุกประเทศที่ใช้ระบบ HS ต้องยึด 6 หลักแรกให้ตรงกัน เช่น ถ้า "กล้วยสด" คือ 0803.90

แต่แต่ละประเทศ สามารถขยายได้เอง เช่น ทำเป็น 8 หรือ 10 หลัก เพื่อควบคุมภาษีหรือระเบียบเฉพาะในประเทศตัวเอง

ทำไมเจ้าของธุรกิจควรรู้เรื่องนี้?

จะได้ใส่รหัส HS Code ให้ถูกตอนส่งออกหรือนำเข้า

ช่วยประเมินอัตราภาษีที่ต้องจ่ายล่วงหน้า

ป้องกันปัญหาติดด่านศุลกากร

และยังใช้ในการขอใบอนุญาตหรือเอกสารที่เกี่ยวข้องอีกด้วย

สรุปสั้นๆ:
HS Code คือภาษากลางของโลจิสติกส์และการค้าระหว่างประเทศ

มือใหม่โลจิสติกส์ต้องรู้! CY, CFS,CY IN คืออะไร

1. CY/CY (Container Yard to Container Yard)
คือรูปแบบการขนส่งที่ตู้คอนเทนเนอร์จะถูกส่งตรงจากลานต้นทาง (CY ต้นทาง) ไปยังลานปลายทาง (CY ปลายทาง)
เหมาะกับใคร: ผู้ส่งและผู้รับที่มีปริมาณสินค้ามากพอจะเหมาทั้งตู้ (FCL)
ประโยชน์: ลดการขนถ่ายหลายต่อ ลดความเสี่ยงสินค้าเสียหาย

ตัวอย่าง:
โรงงานในกรุงเทพฯ บรรจุของลงตู้ที่ลาน CY ลาดกระบัง ส่งตรงถึง CY ที่ท่าเรือญี่ปุ่น โดยไม่ต้องเปิดตู้ระหว่างทางเลย

2. CFS (Container Freight Station)
ใช้สำหรับการขนส่งแบบ LCL (Less than Container Load) คือสินค้าไม่พอจะเหมาทั้งตู้
กระบวนการ:

ที่ต้นทาง: สินค้าจากหลายผู้ส่งมารวมกันที่ CFS

ที่ปลายทาง: แยกสินค้าให้แต่ละผู้รับที่ CFS ก่อนส่งต่อ

HARARI DECONSTRUCTS THE ISRAELI NARRATIVE FROM WITHIN.  Yuval Noah Harar is neither a politician nor an agent of state power, but a globally respected social thinker. 

In a substantial essay published recently in the Financial Times, Harari does not position himself as a champion of the Palestinian story. He does something more unsettling: he dismantles the Israeli narrative from within, stripping it of the historical sanctity long used to justify force.

He states plainly that the land between the river and the sea is not too small to accommodate both peoples, and that what obstructs coexistence is not geography but myth.

He acknowledges that Palestinians are not latecomers to the land, and that they possess a full and legitimate right to live on it—not as guests, nor as “potential inhabitants,” but as children of the place, as rooted as Jews and perhaps more deeply woven into its daily life.

He reminds readers that after most Jews left the land, they were never barred from returning. Neither Romans nor Arabs nor Ottomans closed the gates.

The uncomfortable truth, he argues, is that Jews did not wish to return, and that the land now framed as an “eternal dream” was, for centuries, a destination for only a very small minority.

He then punctures another foundational myth: prayer, however sincere, does not constitute a deed of ownership.

His analogy is sharp: if one prays daily for a neighbour’s house to become one’s own, after how many prayers may one claim it at the land registry?

With this, Harari dismantles the emotional core of Zionist reasoning—the idea that religious longing can be converted into political entitlement.

He also situates Palestinians in their historical reality.

When the first Zionists arrived in the late nineteenth century, the land was far from empty.

It was alive with cities—Acre, Jaffa, Gaza, Nablus, Hebron—and with hundreds of villages forming a deep social and cultural fabric.

And even if Palestinian national identity was not fully crystallised at the time, that does not negate its existence today. Seven million Jews with nowhere else to go, and seven million Palestinians with no other homeland. This fact alone undermines every absolute claim and every narrative that seeks to erase the other.

 I often wonder why some immigrants fail to be law-abiding as a simple show of gratitude to the countries that welcomed them. Many of us in Africa grow up dreaming of opportunities that, in places like America, are everyday realities. What we consider luxuries are basic necessities in the West. Stable electricity, quality infrastructure, human capital development, rule of law, and strong institutions. 

When immigrants fall into crime, chronic dependency, or reckless behaviour, it can feel like a loss of perspective—and a forgetting of the values and struggles that shaped us back home. Respect for the law and hard work matter, not just for personal success, but for the health of the society that opened its doors.

This is why some of us support strong immigration enforcement, including the work of ICE—not out of hatred, but out of a belief in responsibility, accountability, and gratitude to the host nation.

"Ya Ibrahim." na furta hakan, ba tare da nasan na kira sunan ba.
Zuciyata na wani irin bugawa da ƙarfi.
Gaba ɗaya ya canja min, ya ƙara wani irin cika da kyau da haske ga wani irin kwarjini na musamman da ya min.

Nan da nan jikina ya fara rawa, kunya ce tsoro ne?   Ba zan iya banbance abinda na ke ji ba, amma gaba ɗaya jina nake kamar wadda aka dasa a wajen, na kasa gaba na kasa baya.
Sai zuba masa ido da nayi, sai lokacin na fahimci gaba ɗaya bama a cikin hayyacin sa ya ke ba.

Idanun sa gaba ɗaya a runtse suke, sai ƙara ja baya ya ke kamar wanda yaga abin tsoro.
Da ƙarfi ya fara magana wannan karon "Dan Allah ki daina bibiya ta Salmah ya isa haka, ya isa nace."

Rikicewa nayi na juya da sauri da nufin barin wajen. Saboda na tabbatar duk wanda ya ke gidan, tabbas zai ji Muryar Ya Ibrahim da ya ke faɗin na daina bibiyar shi, saboda da ƙarfi ya ke maganar ba tare da yana cikin hayyacin sa ba.

Sai dai kash na makara, ina shirin buɗe ƙofar na shige, naji an saki salati da ƙarfin gaske. A tsorace na juya, Ya Ibrahim na gani zube a ƙasa, sai matar dake salatin iya ƙarfin ta, wadda ba zan taɓa manta fuskar ta ba.
Wato Aunty Ruk'ayya Yayar shi.

Kasa ɗaga ƙafata nayi, tamkar wadda aka zarewa laka, nan da nan wani irin tsoro ya mamaye ni, me ya same shi? Nake tambayar kaina jikina na wata irin rawa.

Nan da nan sai ga mutanen gidan su firfito, tun daga kan Ummanmu Abbanmu,  Halima wadda nake tunanin tare suke da su Aunty Ruk'ayyar, sai Inna mai aiki zuwa mai gadin mu,
Hatta yaran gaba ɗaya.

Kowa na ganin Ya Ibrahim kwance, sai ya ja baya a tsorace yana tambayar me ya same shi?.
Babu zato naji muryar Aunty Ruk'ayya cikin kukan da ta fara, ganin mutane wanda ada ba tayi shi ba, ta shiga nuna ni da hannu tana faɗin "Gata nan ku tambaye ta, zuwa nayi na tarda ta tana shirin guduwa shi kuma a kwance a yadda kuka gan shi ɗin nan.
Ku tambaye ta ko wani abu ta masa, tunda burinta a baya bai cika ba, shine yanzu ta dawo ta ƙarasa mana shi baki ɗaya."
Ta ƙarasa maganar tare da rushewa da kuka, ta shiga jijjiga Ya Ibrahim da hannu, tana kiran sunan shi akan Ya tashi. Sai dai kamar bada shi ta ke ba, ko motsi bai yi ba.

Gani nayi gaba ɗaya kowa dake wajen, ya zubo min ido suna jefo min kallon tuhuma.
Wayyo Allah na, wata irin zuba ce ta shiga  karyo min, haƙiƙa Aunty Ruk'ayya ta matuƙar girgiza ni da maganganun ta, wai ko na masa wani abin ne, ina shirin guduwa.
Ni kuwa me zan masa? banyi zaton har yanzu tsana ta na ranta ba, ga shi yanzu banji ba ban gani ba ta ƙulla min sharri. Ya Allah, gaba ɗaya kallon da ake min yafi ruɗa ni, kasa haɗa ido nayi da kowa na sunkuyar da kaina kamar munafuka.

Ban gama fita a wannan furgici ba, Aunty Ruk'ayya ta cigaba da magana cikin kuka
"Wallahi da ace na san in mun zo gidan nan, abinda zai faru kenan, da ban yarda mun zo ba.
Amma kaine da jarabar ka, kace sai mun biyo kaga uwar taka data kawo ka duniya, gashi nan ai muguwar taka ta dawo, tana neman ƙarasa mana Kai."

Gaba ɗaya Ummanmu da Abba sun rasa me zasu ce, kallona suke cike da zargi, ga hayaniyar Ruk'ayya dake ƙara ƙarfi, sai kururuwa take tana zuzuta abin.
Ga kalmomin da take faɗa marasa daɗi.

Halima ce takaici da haushin, yadda ƴaƴar tata ke neman ciwa su Umman mutumci, yasa, ta ƙarasa wajen ta,  tare da kama ta ta shiga jijjiga da ƙarfi tace "Haba Aunty Ruk'ayya ki nutsu mana, Ya daga zuwa baki san me ya faru ba, kawai kice wani abu ta masa, yanzun nan fa muka shigo gidan.
Kina sane da ko cikin gidan bai shiga ba, aka kira shi a waya yace mu shiga yana zuwa.
Me ke damun ki ne? Har kike faɗin kalamai irin waɗannan?."

Ture hannun Halimar Aunty Ruk'ayya tayi, tare da cewa "Dallah tashi, wadda bata kishin ɗan uwan ta, mara zuciya kawai ke kullum kina goyon bayan surukai.
Ba dan ke da kika dage mu biyo, zaki gaida su ba me zai kawo ni gidan nan, da daga gidan gaisuwar zan wuce gida.
Kuma shima Ibrahim ɗin da ace nasan, zamu zo mu tarda wannan bak'ar kadar Wallahi ba zan bari ya zo ba."

Kuma naji matuƙar mamaki jin cewa har yanzu yana sona.

Ace duk irin cutarwar da na masa bai daina sona ba. Shin wannan wacce irin so ce haka.

Ni yanzu na cire batun aure a rayuwata tuni, bana jin zan iya kallon Ya Ibrahim da sunan soyayya muddin ina da kunya, bare har nayi tunanin aure ya shiga tsakanin mu.

Kasa ce mata komai nayi, har ta gama tijarar ta, ta fice daga gidan tana banbamin faɗa.
Lokacin gidan babu kowa tuni sun tafi asibiti.
Daga ni sai yara, sai Inna Mai aikin mu, Inna ce ta jani ta kaini farlo ta zaunar ganin kamar ba'a hayyacina nake ba.

Haka ta dinga tausa ta, tan bani baki, dan tayi matuƙar tausayamin sosai. Yaran ma duka sai suka zagaye ni suka yi tsuru-tsuru, Salim Sarkin zuciya idanun nan sun kaɗa sun yi ja, alamar yaji zafin abinda Ruk'ayya ta min.

Kenya-led Tumaini Initiative unveils framework to resolve S. Sudan’s political deadlock

South Sudan’s prolonged political deadlock could be moving toward a breakthrough as the Kenyan-led Tumaini Initiative unveiled a framework to guide talks on a draft National Consensus Charter. 

Mediators said on Saturday that the move aims to pave the way for credible elections and inclusive governance.

The framework was handed over to President Salva Kiir’s special envoy, Tut Gatluak Manime on January 29th in Nairobi, and shared with major opposition groups, including the SPLM-IO, the United Peoples’ Alliance (UPA), and the South Sudan Opposition Movements Alliance (SSOMA).

It was also circulated among the South Sudan Council of Churches and civil society leaders.

The initiative, spearheaded by retired Kenyan Lt. Gen. Lazaro Sumbeiywo, described the proposed dialogue as a “significant paradigm shift,” emphasizing a people-centered process in which all parties participate as equal stakeholders. 

Mediators stressed the talks would move away from adversarial posturing and zero-sum politics, focusing instead on peace, security, and accountable governance, while discouraging sectarian or ethnic agendas.

Initial discussions are expected to cover cessation of hostilities, stabilization, civilian protection, and humanitarian access. 

Longer-term issues, to be tackled by a future elected government, include permanent constitution-making, transitional justice, and security sector reform.

While building on the 2018 Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS), the initiative aims to address current political and security challenges by learning from past shortcomings. 

The framework, mediators say, represents a South Sudanese-led and South Sudanese-owned path toward free, fair, and timely elections.

The Secretary General of the Middle East Council of Churches (MECC) Professor Michel Abs concluded his visit to the Arab Republic of Egypt in a meeting with His Eminence Bishop Jean-Marie Chami, Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarchal Vicar General of Egypt, Sudan, and South Sudan, at the Melkite Greek Catholic Patriarchate_ Cairo.

Professor Abs was accompanied by a delegation from the Council, including the Coordinator of Dialogue, Social Cohesion, and Human Dignity Programs at MECC Professor Laura Abi Khalil, and the Coordinator of Church Relations and Media at MECC Journalist Lea Adel Maamary.

The meeting focused on fruitful topics cantered on the activities, youth, and the Church.

During the meeting, His Eminence and the Secretary General discussed matters related to the Week of Prayer for Christian Unity and youth activities. The Secretary General explained that the Council is currently preparing a series of activities related to dialogue, human dignity, and media.

For his part, Bishop Jean-Marie Chami expressed his support for the ideas presented by Secretary General Professor Michel Abs regarding the Council's work and future vision, praising the activities it implements.

He also spoke about the activities carried out by the Diocese on various levels, particularly with the youth, who represent the present of the Church and its future.

Professor Michel Abs offered to His Eminence the two new MECC publications, available on its digital platforms. The first publication includes 23 seminars and roundtables organized by the Dialogue, Social Cohesion, and Rehabilitation of Human Dignity Program.

The second publication prepared by the Council's Theological and Ecumenical Department, is entitled “Towards a Common Date for Easter”, the Aleppo Statement 1997 in Arabic.

ABOUT THE MOTHER OF PEACE
Dr. Hak Ja Han was born on February 10, 1943 in Anju, South Pyeongan Province, in what is now North Korea. At the age of six, she fled to South Korea with her mother and grandmother, risking their lives to cross the border in the dead of night.

From a very young age, Dr. Han developed an intimate father-daughter relationship with God. When she married the late Rev. Sun Myung Moon in 1960, their mutual desire to see a true world of peace led her to join him on a pioneering course as the Mother of Peace.

As the Parents of Peace, Rev. Moon and Dr. Han presented models for bridging conflict, division, and resentment in the fields of education, politics, arts, sciences, media and human rights, all united under the banner of the Unification movement.The cornerstone of her legacy is the Marriage Blessing, which transcends race, culture, nationality, denomination and ideology

Since the first Marriage Blessing officiated by Rev. Moon and Dr. Han in 1960, this tradition has expanded to become an inter-religious affirmation of the universal importance of marriage and family. The Marriage Blessing transcends boundaries and religious affiliations, and creates a shared experience as one family under God.

Dr. Han teaches that women, as true daughters of God, must play a central role in creating a just and peaceful society. To this point, she established the Women’s Federation for World Peace in 1992, championing the vital role of women in peace building at the United Nations, the United States Capitol, the Great Hall of the People in China and the Korean National Assembly.

Since her husband’s passing in 2012, Dr. Hak Ja Han has lead the worldwide ministry of the Unification movement. She is prioritizing the education of young people, challenges facing the environment, and human disasters, such as the growing refugee crisis. 

Dr. Han’s most recent humanitarian efforts include the founding of the prestigious  Sun Hak Peace Prize, which honors exceptional men and women working to solve global issues, and the Peace Starts With Me world tour of rallies which have brought thousands of people together, challenging them to become peacemakers, starting with themselves.

Dr.Han has invested in loving all of God’s children as her own. She has lived her life for the sake of lasting world peace, securing a bright future for generations to come.

I threw my back out yesterday. Completely immobilised. Every movement made me gasp in pain.

A few years ago, this would have sent me into a spiral.

I’ve had chronic back pain since my early 20s. Before that, an eating disorder in my late teens. My relationship with my body has been… complicated to say the least!

I’ve spent years hating it. Punishing it. Wishing it was different.

Yesterday, I could barely take a few steps and, although I’m still in bed today, something feels significantly different this time.

Instead of spiraling into panic and self-hatred, I feel… grateful.

Grateful to my body for trying to protect me. For my muscles spasming to prevent greater damage to my spine. For forcing me to slow down and stop doing all the things.

I’ve still had a lovely weekend with my kids - reading, talking, playing board games. Present in a way I couldn’t have been if I’d been stuck in the old pattern of hating my body for “failing” me.

Yesterday afternoon I did a Y.E.L.L. Method breathwork session.

My intention: “I intend for my body to move easily and freely and to have complete confidence in it.”

Today I’m still in pain, but so much more mobile. I’ve been able to shower unaided. Use the toilet without help. Walk without gasping.

And with each bit of progress, I’m celebrating myself and my body - something I would have never dreamed of doing before.

Here’s what I love most about The Y.E.L.L. Method:

You can bring ANYTHING to a session.

It doesn’t just have to be about yelling at your kids or feeling overwhelmed in parenting.

You can work on your relationship with your body. Your chronic pain. Your anxiety. Your patterns around food or money or relationships.

And here’s the magic: when you address the root cause of one struggle, other areas of life improve too. Because it’s all connected, stored in the same nervous system, waiting to be released.

The woman who battles with her body? She’s still here. But she’s softer now. More compassionate. More grateful.

That’s the shift The Y.E.L.L. Method creates.

The Inherited Madness and Mad Doctrine of William T. Sherman: Tyranny Unleashed on the American Republic

By Chet McAteer 

In the shadowed halls of American history, few figures embody the grotesque perversion of republican ideals more starkly than William Tecumseh Sherman. As a key architect of the North’s war machine under Abraham Lincoln’s Radical Republican regime, Sherman orchestrated a campaign of unbridled terror against the Southern States, particularly South Carolina, not out of any noble pursuit but from a seething hatred for the very foundations of the Republic. 

His political contrivances—cloaked in the rhetoric of “union” preservation—were nothing short of a deranged crusade to eradicate the principles of federalism, States’ Rights, and self-government enshrined in the Constitution. The Lincoln years were, in a very real sense, a Coup against the Republic of Sovereign States, the very definition of Constitutional Treason!

This madness was no isolated aberration but a torment inherited from a familial tapestry of melancholy, manifesting in personal breakdowns that fueled his genocidal wrath. This essay exposes Sherman’s absurd doctrine as utterly divorced from the Framers’ vision, citing his own venomous words that reveal a mind unhinged by nationalist fanaticism and genetic affliction. 

Alongside his Radical Republican cohorts, Sherman represented a cabal of ideologues whose actions bordered on insanity, transforming a Constitutional dispute into a holocaust of civilian suffering to impose centralized despotism.
During the initial phases of the War of Northern Aggression—a brutal invasion that ravaged the Sovereign South—Sherman embodied the torment of inherited madness, his profound depression rendering him paralyzed and unfit for command, culminating in his desperate request for relief from duties in Kentucky on November 9, 1861. 

Wire services swiftly branded him insane, with the Cincinnati Chronicle headline screaming “Genl Wm T Sherman Insane” weeks later, nearly obliterating his Union career and sending shockwaves through Northern ranks. Sherman’s own raw admission to Ulysses S. Grant—“Grant stood by me when I was crazy, and I stood by him when he was drunk, and now we stand by each other”—highlighted the severity of his collapse, marked by exaggerated fears of Confederate forces, demands for 60,000 to 200,000 unattainable reinforcements, and sleepless nights plagued by delusions of utter ruin.

This mental fragility was no aberration but a thread in a familial tapestry of melancholy (bipolar disorder), beginning with his father Charles Robert Sherman’s sudden death in 1829 at age 40 from respiratory illness, leaving eleven children, including nine-year-old William, scattered among relatives—a chaos that biographers like Lloyd Lewis argue sowed seeds of lifelong insecurity and abandonment. 

On his paternal side, a chronic “melancholic” uncle suffered recurrent despondency, mirroring Sherman’s own early breakdown at 27 amid career failures and pressure from father-in-law Thomas Ewing, as psychiatrist Nassir Ghaemi notes in A First-Rate Madness: “A paternal uncle of Sherman’s also likely suffered from recurrent depression, a genetic link that supports this diagnosis,” amplifying his bipolar-like swings between manic frenzy—chain-smoking, relentless pacing, feverish orders—and suicidal lows of inertia, insomnia, and lost appetite.

Sherman’s wife, Ellen Ewing Sherman—married in 1850 despite her father’s disapproval and whispered by contemporaries as temperamentally volatile, earning the moniker “crazy wife” in family lore—rushed to Louisville in 1861, finding him a gaunt specter, barely eating or sleeping, obsessing that “the whole country is gone irrevocably & ruin & desolation are at hand.” 

Drawing from the family’s laced history of melancholy, she nursed him with Shakespeare readings and home comforts, having witnessed prior “seizes” of madness that isolated him from humanity, which she later confided stemmed from “insanity to which your family is subject.” 

Though Ellen’s Ewing lineage leaned toward rigid Catholic piety rather than overt fragility, her father Thomas’s disciplinarian demands exacerbated Sherman’s anxiety, as he wrote: “I am up all night… I find myself riding a whirlwind unable to guide the storm.” 

Foster brother Hugh Ewing alluded in letters to the “family melancholy” haunting their household, while Ellen’s vigilance amid raising eight children during the war’s turmoil masked strains from Sherman’s absences, infidelities, and paranoia—fueled by extreme mood shifts, as Ghaemi describes.

Well-documented collapses throughout the conflict exemplified modern diagnoses of bipolar or major depressive illness, with erratic highs of productivity and lows of despair attributed to this torment; his brother John received confessions of suicidal thoughts during 1861-62 recovery in Ohio, where William admitted, “I am more nervous than [Grant] is… it scares me like hell.” 

Descendant E. Chris Evans recounted grandfatherly kin declaring, “He was crazy, you know,” echoed by Secretary of War Simon Cameron’s “unbalanced” verdict, the Chicago Tribune’s “stark insanity,” and Frank Leslie’s Illustrated Newspaper’s quip that “it is charitable to think so.” 

These manifested as intense mania with anxiety—pacing corridors, twitching in “quick, sharp…odd gestures,” a “bundle of nerves” observed by New York journalists—pouring chaos into letters to Ellen about betrayal, vanished appetite, and a mind swirling in “failure and humiliation” that “nearly makes me crazy—indeed I may be so now.” 
Ghaemi posits these swings birthed a hyper-empathetic ruthlessness from his hellish abyss.

This familial insanity erupted in Sherman’s merciless tactics against defenseless Southern civilians, turning manic highs into unnecessary devastation of lives, property, and spirit, profoundly demoralizing a resilient people under unjust invasion. Sherman’s worldview was a feverish rejection of the Republic’s core tenets. The Constitution, crafted as a compact among Sovereign States, explicitly reserves undelegated powers to the states and the people via the Tenth Amendment. 

It was designed to prevent the very consolidation of power that Sherman championed—a voluntary union where states retained the right to govern themselves, including the ultimate remedy of Secession if the federal government overstepped. 

Yet Sherman dismissed this as heresy. In a January 31, 1864, letter to Major R.M. Sawyer, he lambasted the war’s origins as “the result of a false political doctrine that any and every people have a right to self-government.” 

Here, Sherman explicitly scorned the Jeffersonian principle that governments derive their just powers from the consent of the governed—a cornerstone not only of the Declaration of Independence but also implicit in the Constitution’s ratification by sovereign states. To Sherman, self-government was not a right but a delusion, a “false political doctrine” that justified his genocidal wrath.

This hatred extended to the Constitution’s safeguards of liberty. In the same letter, Sherman derided States’ Rights, freedom of conscience, and freedom of the press as “trash” that had “deluded the Southern people into war.” 

Such language betrays a profound contempt for the Bill of Rights: the First Amendment’s protections for speech and press, and the Tenth’s affirmation of states’ sovereignty. Sherman’s doctrine posited that these were not inviolable pillars but disposable “trash,” obstacles to his vision of an omnipotent central state. 

This was no mere rhetorical flourish; it was the ideological fuel for his “total war” strategy, which targeted civilians to break the spirit of self-determination. His subordinates echoed this madness, with Major George W. Nichols labeling South Carolinians as “the scum, the lower dregs of civilization” who were “not Americans; they are merely South Carolinians,” and General Carl Schurz deeming the state “deserving of special punishment” for instigating Secession. 

These sentiments, rooted in Sherman’s influence, reveal a collective psychosis among Lincoln’s generals—a belief that Southern adherence to Constitutional federalism equated to treason warranting extermination.

Sherman’s insanity manifested most vividly in his fixation on South Carolina, the cradle of secession and thus the symbolic heart of States’ Rights. Far from a campaign against slavery—as postwar myths propagated by the Lincoln cult would claim—Sherman’s march was a vendetta against the idea of decentralized governance. 

In a letter to General Henry Halleck shortly before the invasion, Sherman confessed that “[T]he whole army is burning with an insatiable desire to wreak vengeance upon South Carolina.” 

Weeks later, he reiterated to Halleck that “The whole army is crazy to be turned loose in [South] Carolina.” These admissions expose a commander not guided by military necessity but by a pathological urge for retribution. An embedded New York newspaperman noted the troops’ “extreme bitterness towards the people of the State of South Carolina,” while the Philadelphia Inquirer hailed the state as “that accursed hotbed of treason.” 

South Carolina’s sin? Not its slaveholding, which was widespread across the South, but its bold assertion of Sovereignty, echoing the Framers’ intent that States could Withdraw from a Union turned tyrannical.

As Sherman saw Slavery: "All congresses on earth can't make the negro anything more than what he is; he must be subject to the white man, or he must amalgamate or be destroyed...Two such races cannot live in harmony except as master or slave." -Sherman 7/10/1860

In the 1864 March to the Sea, his scant-sleep frenzy unleashed savagery across Georgia, sacking Atlanta and torching 300 miles of farms, rails, and homes in a plague of fire and plunder that starved and shattered innocents. 

Dismissing Atlanta’s mayor’s mercy pleas with unhinged fatalism—“You might as well appeal against the thunder-storm as against these terrible hardships of war… God will judge us”—he twisted his prewar warning to Professor David F. Boyd: “This country will be drenched in blood… It is all folly, madness, a crime against civilization!” into self-justification for embodying “mad passions,” displacing the elderly and feeble while reducing their havens to ash. 

New York Tribune reporter T.A. Post saw derangement confirmed: Sherman “seemed determined to prove that the allegations of insanity were true,” channeling breakdowns into paradoxical empathy that intensified suffering to hasten the South’s subjugation.

The Radical Republicans under Lincoln shared this derangement, viewing the war as an opportunity to rewrite the Republic into a nationalist empire. Lincoln himself suspended habeas corpus, imprisoned dissenters without trial, and manipulated elections—acts that shredded the Constitution’s due process clauses. 

His acolytes, like the Reverend Henry Ward Beecher, gloated over the ruins, proclaiming under a U.S. flag in Charleston: “Let no man misread the meaning of this unfolding flag! 

It says, ‘GOVERNMENT hath returned hither.’ 
It proclaims in the name of vindicated government, peace and protection to loyalty; humiliations and pains to traitors. This is the flag of sovereignty. The nation, not the States, is Sovereign. Restored to authority, this flag commands, not supplicates . . . . There may be pardon [for former Confederates], but no concession . . . . The only condition of submission is to submit!” 

Beecher’s rant inverted the Constitution’s structure: Article VII confirms States’ Sovereignty in ratification, and the Preamble vests power in “We the People” through their States, not a supreme nation. Yet this Hamiltonian superstition—perpetuated by figures like John Marshall and Daniel Webster—became the Radicals’ gospel, justifying Sherman’s atrocities.

The human cost of this lunacy was apocalyptic. Sherman’s army, unleashed like a horde of barbarians, ravaged defenseless civilians in a bid to prove federalism’s “delusion.” General Charles Van Wyck boasted that “nearly every house on our line of march has been destroyed,” while reporter David P. Conyngham described towns reduced to “smoking ruins . . . tall, black chimneys looking down upon it like funeral mutes” amid “old women and children, hopeless, helpless, almost frenzied, wandering amidst the desolation.” 

These acts—rape, murder,  looting, and arson after Confederate forces had withdrawn—were not warfare but sadistic theater, aimed at humiliating a people who dared cling to Constitutional self-rule. Northern tourists flocked to gawk at the carnage, reveling in the “proof” that states were mere provinces of an imperial center.

Post-Appomattox, this mania extended westward against American Indians, mirroring Southern scorched-earth tactics in vindictive extermination policies targeting nomadic tribes with cold precision. As commanding general, he orchestrated buffalo annihilation to starve Sioux and Cheyenne into barren reservations, endorsing a genocide-by-proxy that decimated millions of animals. 

To Philip Sheridan, he proposed inviting global sportsmen for a “Grand Buffalo hunt” to “make one grand sweep,” protecting slaughters like Buffalo Bill Cody’s 4,280 kills, asserting, “As long as the buffalo roamed, [Native Americans] would follow them.” Vowing “vindictive earnestness… even to their extermination, men, women, and children,” he seized sacred lands for railroads and miners, echoing Ellen’s familial curse now etched in orders that obliterated indigenous worlds, rendering John’s consolations hollow against a “nervous” genius turned boundless storm.

The curse endured in Sherman’s descendants, most tragically in eldest son Thomas Ewing Sherman, born 1856, whose severe depression echoed his father’s, leading to homelessness, delusions, institutionalization at St. Joseph’s Hospital in 1925, and death in 1933 amid “nervous afflictions,” as the New York Times noted. 

Rejecting law for Jesuit priesthood against parental wishes, Thomas triggered Sherman’s relapse at 58: “It nearly makes me crazy—indeed I may be so now,” magnifying unresolved grief. Siblings like Minnie endured chronic invalidism possibly from emotional strain, and Philemon showed erratic banking behaviors, but Thomas’s institutional end—Ghaemi observing he “was deeply depressed, sometimes homeless, and ultimately died in an institution”—underscored the genetic cycle Sherman escaped only through wartime resolve.

Sherman’s doctrine, utterly alien to the Republic’s foundations, marked him as a madman in uniform. The Constitution’s architects—Madison, Jefferson, Hamilton in his Federalist days—envisioned a limited federal government to protect liberty, not crush it. 

Sherman’s dismissal of self-government as “false” and liberties as “trash” betrayed a totalitarian impulse, shared by Lincoln’s Radicals who sought to “vindicate” a sovereign nation through blood. This insanity birthed the modern leviathan state, where federal overreach eclipses States’ Rights. 

In exposing Sherman’s hatred—through his own words—we honor the true Republic, warning against the cults that still rewrite history to glorify such tyrants. To delve deeper, consider how Sherman’s contrivances prefigured modern statism: his “total war” philosophy, divorced from constitutional restraint, inspired later despots. 

The Lincoln cult’s ongoing commemorations—rewriting Secession as treason—perpetuate this madness, ignoring that the war’s true aggressors were those who trampled the Compact. Ultimately, Sherman stood as a nexus in this web of inherited anguish, where bipolar storms fueled a ruthless military mind that inflicted incalculable harm on the noble South and beyond, eroding even his guarded home. Sherman’s legacy is not heroism but horror, a testament to how unhinged ideology can and did, in fact, dismantled a republic from within.

In Liberty and Eternal Vigilance,
C.M.McAteer

I am a chronic negative self-talker. I am hypercritical of myself and expect nothing less than perfection. I overanalyze, undervalue, and am never satisfied with myself. And I bring that into my work (which can be both a good and a bad thing). 

But with that being said, I am damn proud of myself and the business I have created. I have poured my heart and soul into every single aspect of Cakes By Callie. This is my baby, and I have failed to give myself the proper credit I deserve. 

People are oftentimes misinformed when it comes to owning, running, and establishing your own business. If I had a dollar for every time someone has told me this isn’t a real job, I could retire right now. “How do you make a living?”, “What else do you do for work?”, “You do this full time?”, “What’s your actual job?”, “Are you still making those cute little cakes?”, “Oh, you’re a cake decorator? How sweet.” And to that respectfully say - I make a living working my ass off and doing what I love. I am a baker, decorator, content creator, photographer, videographer, marketer, advertiser, financial planner, strategist, operations manager, saleswoman, customer relations specialist, human resources director, producer, leader, professional, risk taker. I work more hours now than I ever have working for someone else. THIS is my actual job. I sure as hell am making “those cute little cakes” that are literal pieces of art. And being a cake decorator is sweet. It is sweet to get to wake up every day and be truly happy with my career choice. It is sweet to do the #1 most important thing to me, which is to help and make people happy. It is sweet to not be debilitated by my mental health every single second of every single day. It is sweet to be able to “work to live” instead of “live to work”. 

Furthermore, I put my blood, sweat, and tears into every single order I take. Unless you are a cake decorator, you have no idea the time, energy, cost, patience, and expertise that goes into every little detail. It’s like the millions of people saying “Patrick Mahomes sucks”, “We need a new QB”, “I’m done watching the Chiefs”. When in reality, Patrick Mahomes has more talent in his left pinky than these same people have in their entire bodies. Once you’ve been in the NFL, you can talk. Similarly, once you’ve been a cake decorator, you can talk. But until then, you can politely keep your mouth shut and let the professionals do their thing. You cannot tell someone else how to do their OWN job. With me personally, I have found that the less involved the client is, the more satisfied they are with their end result. When I am given creative freedom, my best work is brought to life. I will never “copy” or replicate someone else’s work. That is like cheating on a math test. It’s not my work, and I would never claim to be able to restore the original version. Even I can’t make an exact duplicate of my own cake. It’s like art; every piece is going to be different. And I would never take an order that I don’t feel 100% capable of perfecting. That is my name that I am putting on your cake. I am a type A, OCD, perfectionist…you really think I would send you on your way with something I’m not proud of? And while I cannot control the narrative you form about me and my business based on others’ opinions, I would encourage you to do your own research and educate yourselves before blindly following along. If you know someone who says I have a “bad reputation”, “terrible attitude”, or “would never recommend this business”, please “@“ them below so I can have a personal conversation with them and address their concerns. I’m just a little confused because if you have a problem with me, I would figure you would bring it up with ME. And I have only had 3 people in my 5 years of operating my business bring up negative experiences with me. Then I have corrected those experiences and moved forward. That is not to say that those 3 individual experiences were not difficult to maneuver, because they were. 3 is more than 0, which is what I have always aimed for, but that is unrealistic. What’s important is that I didn’t give up. And I won’t let 3 negative experiences outweigh the thousands of positive experiences my clients have had with me. 

Another great thing about my business is that it is MY business. There are always going to be people who disagree with me, and that is their choice. Yes, I cater to my clients and strive for their complete satisfaction. But I will NOT compromise my beliefs in order to achieve this. I know this is going to make a lot of people mad…but the customer is not always right. Yes, I said it. And yes, I meant it. If you don’t like how I choose to run my business, then you don’t have to follow or engage with me. It’s really that simple. Is my business perfect? Absolutely not. Are there things I could improve upon? Absolutely. One thing to know about me is I take accountability and own up to my shit. I will never quit learning, improving, and working on myself. If I am wrong, I will admit it. If I mess up, I will apologize and learn from it. But on the flip side, I will not just say I am wrong to placate anyone. I will take full accountability right now and say that my biggest area of improvement in my business is my communication skills. Or should I say, lack thereof. I SUCK at replying to people. Not just in my business, but in my personal life, too. If you were in jail and had ONE call to make, I should be the LAST person you think of. I get so many requests, messages, and correspondence in a single day that sometimes I do just forget. As I’ve said before, I am a one-woman show. I do this all by myself. I don’t have a separation between work and life, which can be tricky at times. I’m not justifying my behavior, making excuses, or asking for sympathy. I am simply just explaining why I am so bad at getting back to you. Is this a good business practice for me to have? No. Would I be upset if I was trying to get something done and it was taking longer than I thought necessary? Yes. But am I working on it? More than you know. I am not proud of this. But I also know why I struggle so much with this. And those reasons can be saved for another time. Because it goes much deeper than anyone understands. I am just asking for a little bit of grace and patience when it comes to this issue. It is NEVER personal. I am not purposely ignoring you. I am not ghosting you. I am just overwhelmed and am actively working to fix this. 

Another sensitive subject for a lot of people: pricing. MY prices are based on my knowledge, skill set, total costs, talent, experience, competition, area, and most importantly, value. I’ve said it once and I’ll say it again - one man’s trash is another man’s treasure. You don’t go into Prada expecting to pay Walmart prices. Let me make it clear - I love Walmart and will choose shopping there over high-end brands all day, every day. Prada is just not a necessity to me; it is a luxury. Just like my cakes are a LUXURY. They are custom-made, and every single cake is uniquely personalized to the client. My base prices are for a plain white frosted cake. No decoration, piping, etc. My smallest plain white frosted round cake will be $75.00. But a $75.00 cake can become an over $100.00 cake real quick when you add glitter, cherries, edible images, bows, pearls, toppers, etc. That is why I have my “Upcharges” list posted on my page. So you can have a full breakdown on additional charges before booking with me. My prices are not tailored to your financial situation, and I will not alter them based on you thinking I’m “too expensive”. There are so many talented cake decorators in the Wichita area, and I firmly believe that there is room for all of us here. So if I am not within your budget, you don’t like my communication skills, or you don’t want to pay up front, then I will always recommend you to my fellow bakers. Except for the one person who makes it her life’s mission to try and control all of us other cake decorators and stays in their business…like that’s her job instead of actually decorating cakes. It’s okay if you don’t want to place an order through me. But if you can’t afford my prices, just say so. Yes, this is my main source of income. Yes, I want to make money. But I will never let greed impact my choices and who I am. I have given away more free cakes than I can count. I have donated to homeless shelters, local businesses, and single moms who are struggling. I have offered free wedding cakes to couples whose families changed their minds on helping them. If I have extra cookies or cupcakes, I bring them to my neighbors, gym, or church. I don’t do this expecting anything in return. I don’t do this because it will make my business look good. I don’t do this to save face. I don’t do this as a PR strategy. I bet some people are actually reading this and thinking I need PR training. But I’m resilient, strong-headed, and can be very stubborn. I don’t do anything I don’t want to do, even if everyone around me is telling me I’m wrong. I do this because I WANT to. I do this because giving back makes my heart full. I do this because it makes me feel good. I do this because it’s just the type of person I am.

Lastly, for all the people who might comment mean, negative, rude things on this or any other posts related to my business, go for it. You can sit behind your computer or phone and talk about me all day long. If that is how you choose to spend your time, then all the power to you. In fact, I welcome you to comment the most appalling, nasty, negative, disgusting things about me or my business on this post. I am giving you permission to express your hatred and disdain for me. My absolute favorite is when it comes from people who have never even met me before. It just really goes to show how much you truly loathe me for simply existing. I personally don’t have the time, effort, or energy to be mean to anyone, but that might be because I’m too busy running a successful business and focusing on myself. You will never see me responding to negative people or comments because you are honestly not worth my time. A lion does not concern itself with the opinions of sheep. You WANT me to comment. You WANT me to engage with you and get angry. You WANT to see me break. But you won’t break me. Ever. You won’t threaten or scare me by saying you’ll blast my business on social media. Do it. Blast away. That says more about you than it will ever say about me. Not once have I ever written a negative review, because I would never want to ruin anyone’s livelihood. Because I realize everyone is human and deserves to be treated with respect. Because I would rather encourage others than tear them down. As much as I didn’t want to make this post, I will not allow my character to be put into question. I have now received my first negative review on my page. And while it is unfortunate, that is just part of being a business owner. Contrary to popular belief, Facebook business pages cannot remove reviews. So what you see is what you get. Even if I did have the power to remove negative reviews, I wouldn’t. That would be misleading and inauthentic of me to do. You are never going to please everyone. I would say that, historically speaking, the more successful you are, the more hate you are going to get. Some people don’t like to see you win. But I’ll let you in on a little secret of mine…the more someone doubts me, the more motivation I have to prove them wrong. This has lit a fire under my ass, and I promise you I am going to come back from this better than I ever have before. You are here right now on my business page because you know who I am. You have seen my work, you have seen my reviews. You don’t know me. You don’t know my heart. You don’t know my soul. You don’t know the person behind the business logo. Let me introduce myself. My name is Callie Biddle. I am the PROUD owner of Cakes By Callie, and I am one of the kindest human beings you will ever meet. 

To my supporters, I love and appreciate you more than you will ever know. Whether you have been here from the beginning or are new here, I thank you from the bottom of my heart. You have allowed me to live out my dream, and my business is where it is because of YOU. I am forever grateful and will keep creating cakes for as long as you let me. Word of mouth is the best form of advertising, so if you have ordered with me and would like to leave a review on my page (positive or negative), that would mean the world to me. Just like the best way to show your support for a business is to follow, like, 

If you have made it through to the end of this novel, you are a real one 😂 And I will be giving this gold studded star cake to one of you! No following, liking, sharing, tagging, or reposting needed. Just simply comment that you would like to have it! First person who comments, gets it! It is a moist chocolate cake with fresh strawberries and an Oreo/vanilla buttercream frosting! Delicious! 😋

In an extraordinary Council of Ministers meeting chaired by Governor Emmanuel Adil Anthony, the Government of Central Equatoria State have unanimously agreed to form two committees tasked to probe revenue infringement and illegal logging activities reportedly in Kajo-keji and Lainya Counties.

The decision follows a memo presented by Hon. Alex Lotiyu,the State Minister of Animal resources, Fisheries and Tourism on Continued Unconstitutional infringement on State Hotels' revenue Collection Mandate by the National Ministry of Wildlife Conservation and Tourism. While the State Government reiterated its commitment in working together with National Government institutions, the Council pointed out continued challenge in hotel revenue Collections due to violation of article (179) of the Transitional Constitution of the Republic of South Sudan (2011) which gives the State Government right to of collecting revenue Collections within its jurisdiction. 

After deliberating on the memo, the Council directed the State Ministers of Animal resources, Fisheries and Tourism, and Finance, Planning and Investment to effectively execute their Constitutional mandate of managing and collecting hotel Revenue within the State's jurisdiction. Further,  the State Government formed a committee headed by the Deputy Governor to address revenue encroachment related issues and to strengthen government inter linkages, while calling on all hotels within the State Jurisdiction to fully comply and recognize the constitutional rights of the State in collecting Revenues. 

Subsequently, the meeting also discussed a memo tabled by Hon. Lily Kapuki Jurkin, the State Minister of Agriculture, Environment, and Forestry on illegal logging activities in Kajo-keji and Lainya counties. Following its deliberation, the State Government banned all illegal logging activities in the State with immediate effect and formed a Committee headed by the State Minister of Agriculture, Environment, and Forestry alongside Minister of Finance, Planning, and Investment to conduct findings on the volume of logs established  on ground.

She’s home. And I’m still trying to breathe through the emotions.

My sweet Westie girl, Daisy, made it through surgery this morning—
and seeing her like this hurts in a way I can’t put into words.
The shaved patch along her side.
The neat line of stitches.
The faint bruising beneath her white coat.
Every mark tells a story I wish she never had to live.

But she’s here.
She’s breathing.
She’s fighting.

When we walked through the front door, she didn’t cry.
She didn’t panic.
She moved slowly to the couch,
carefully climbed up,
and curled into her favorite spot like she’s done a thousand times before.
Her body was exhausted,
her eyes heavy with that deep post-surgery tiredness—
but the moment I sat beside her,
she leaned her little head into my lap.
Softly.
Trustingly.
As if to say, I’m okay now. I’m home.

Westies don’t understand surgery.
They don’t understand why their body suddenly hurts,
why strangers touched them,
why everything feels different.

Commentary on Online Media Houses and Social Media Platforms as Tools of Tribal Incitement South Sudan My Homeland. Kolongdit online Media SOUTH SUDAN EAGLE MEDIA

Online media houses and social media platforms, particularly Facebook and WhatsApp, have increasingly been weaponized in South Sudan as instruments of tribal incitement and conflict escalation. Rather than serving as spaces for dialogue and civic engagement, these platforms have, in many cases, functioned as arenas of digital warfare, amplifying ethnic hatred, misinformation, and direct calls for violence.

1. Digital Platforms as Instruments of Tribal Mobilization

A defining feature of this phenomenon is the targeting of specific ethnic groups, often aligned with political allegiances. Numerous online pages and media outlets have been accused of mobilizing one community against another, most notably framing political struggles as ethnic confrontations, including narratives that pit Dinka against Nuer populations. Such framing deliberately reduces complex political disputes into tribal binaries, making violence appear justified or inevitable.

2. Role of Certain Online Media Outlets

Reports and monitoring initiatives have highlighted platforms such as Eagle Media–linked pages, South Sudan My Land, FM, and Kolongdit Online Media as examples of outlets accused of amplifying divisive, tribalistic, and at times genocidal rhetoric. These platforms are frequently criticized for:

Promoting dehumanizing language against specific communities

1) Encouraging collective blame rather than individual accountability
2) Undermining national reconciliation by normalizing ethnic hostility

Their content often blurs the line between political commentary and ethnic incitement, with severe implications for social cohesion.

3. Diaspora-Driven Amplification

A significant portion of inflammatory rhetoric originates from these online media outlines which use online media and social platforms to influence events on the ground. While physically distant from the consequences, these actors are able to:

1) Escalate tensions rapidly
2) Spread unverified or fabricated claims
3) Encourage violence without bearing immediate risk

This amplification of tribal deepens internal divisions and complicates peacebuilding efforts.

4. Use of Genocidal and Dehumanizing Language

Observers, human rights organizations, and UN-related reports have repeatedly noted the use of language implying extermination, removal, or collective punishment of certain ethnic groups such as Nuer. Such rhetoric is not merely offensive; it constitutes a serious early-warning indicator of mass atrocity risks, as it normalizes violence and strips targeted communities of their humanity.

5. Misinformation and Disinformation Ecosystem

Approximately 50.5% of harmful online content in South Sudan is classified as misinformation or disinformation. This includes:

1) Fabricated or recycled images and videos
2) False claims presented as breaking. 
3) Manipulated narratives designed to provoke fear, anger, and revenge. 

These materials are deliberately circulated to inflame emotions and accelerate cycles of retaliation.

6. Platforms and Mechanisms of Spread

Facebook: Accounts for nearly 90% of documented online hate speech incidents, aided by widespread access through “free mode” mobile services. WhatsApp Groups: Used to rapidly circulate rumors and mobilize local violence at community level. Fake Profiles and Bots: Enable anonymous dissemination of hate speech, reducing accountability and evading moderation.

7. Impact on the Ground

The consequences of online hate speech are direct and tangible, including:

1) Physical violence, where online incitement correlates with targeted attacks
2) Forced displacement, as communities flee areas following ethnicized campaigns
3 Threats to humanitarian workers, forcing aid agencies to suspend or withdraw operations

These outcomes demonstrate that online rhetoric is not abstract—it translates into real-world harm.

8. Mitigation and Response Efforts

Several initiatives seek to counter these dangers: Monitoring and Mapping: Organizations such as Digital Rights Frontlines (formerly #defyhatenow) and PeaceTech Lab track and analyze hate speech trends. Regulatory Warnings: The South Sudan Media Authority has issued warnings urging media houses to adhere to responsible journalism and ethical standards. Fact-Checking Initiatives: Platforms like 211 Check work to debunk false and misleading information before it spreads further.

9. Understanding Tribal Bigotry

A tribal bigot is an individual who holds rigid, hostile, and irrational prejudices against other ethnic or tribal groups, believing their own group to be inherently superior. Key features of this mindset include:

Reliance on harmful stereotypes,  Systematic discrimination based on identity rather than merit, Promotion of “us versus them” narratives that erode national unity, Political manipulation, where leadership contests become ethnic headcounts, Deep intolerance toward diversity and dissenting views, Tribal bigotry functions in the same way as racial or religious bigotry: it dehumanizes, divides, and prepares the ground for violence.

Concluding Observation

The misuse of online media and social platforms for tribal incitement by these Regime based online media platform represents one of the most serious contemporary threats to peace and reconciliation in South Sudan. Addressing it requires ethical journalism, platform accountability, digital literacy, and firm rejection of tribal bigotry in all its forms. Without these measures, digital spaces will continue to serve not as tools for nation-building, but as accelerants of conflict.

#INSIGHTS 

South Sudan South 🇸🇸 is fundamentally a civil state, not a religious one, and it is not founded on a single faith. Therefore, the South Sudan Council of Churches does not have the authority to control people’s beliefs or impose guardianship over worship.

The Constitution clearly guarantees freedom of religion, belief, and worship, granting this right to all citizens without discrimination—whether Christian, Muslim, or followers of other beliefs.
Regarding claims that sometimes arise about individuals coming from outside the country and being labelled as false prophets, this is not the responsibility of the Council of Churches alone. Such matters fall under public awareness, legal regulation, and the responsibility of the state, not religious institutions.

Addressing these issues requires:
enforcement of the law,
public education, and
protection of citizens from religious exploitation,
rather than accusations or misplaced blame.

MINISTER BAK UNVEILS AN ECONOMIC STABILIZATION AND STRUCTURAL REFORMS POLICY 

Wednesday, February 4, 2026- Juba
Department of Communication and Media- MoFP

The Minister of Finance and Planning, Hon. Dr. Bak Barnaba Chol held a press conference to introduce a cabinet endorsed “Economic Stabilization and Structural Reforms Policy” document as a national framework aimed at improving the economy and strengthening the country’s financial sector.

Minister Bak reiterated that the policy document came as a result of a collective effort by key financial institutions, sector ministries and relevant authorities after assessing the current economic situation in the country that is marred with currency instability, over-reliance on oil, fiscal pressures and inflationary tendencies. 

The policy document also emphasizes on the fiscal discipline, budget credibility, halting public sector recruitment, cancellation of non-statutory tax exemptions, introduction of VAT, implementation of Treasury Single Account and timely disbursement of salaries to civil servants, organized forces and foreign missions.

The Honorable Minister outlined the need to prioritize investment and promotion of agriculture, mining, tourism, livestock and fisheries sectors to diversify the economy and build a strong public private partnership to improve productive sector and support Small and Medium Enterprises.

Minister Bak highlighted the implementation matrix of this policy as being anchored on inter-ministerial coordination and a regular reporting to Council of Ministers in an effort to stabilize the economy, improve livelihoods and ensure sustainable and inclusive growth affixed on policy articulation and disciplined implementation based on transparency and accountability in the spirit of Public Financial Management reforms.

The press conference was attended by the Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning, Technical Advisor, two undersecretaries and Directors General, all of whom were tasked to ensure that the policy document is implemented at the technical level.

WHAT IF?

Once in a while … you come to the end of the road with a dream. I have come to the end of that road more times than I care to remember. Most times … it just didn’t turn out the way I thought, more times I gave up.

I will confess my greatest failing… impatience.

In a sense I was spoilt, at least that’s what people keep telling me. That I was too used to getting my way, that I didn’t know how to take no for an answer, and that when things didn’t go my way … I would be no different than the terrible twos who came to my clinic on a daily basis and screamed and kicked 😂 even before they got in the door.

The only difference was that my tantrums were covered in the veil of adulthood… understated but clear to those who watched closely. I would shout first … then I would bargain, and then I would go through all the stages of grief one by one. In the end I would get to the acceptance stage, but no, I would not accept, I would just walk away, I would forget … and in time the pain and reality of failure would fade away.

To this day I cannot say I have moved passed my toddler phase … maybe that is why despite their tantrums … I would still not have it any other way. They forever remain the patients I love the most. But my faith and my stubbornness to let go of things, replaced my impatience with loyalty.

You see every cloud has a silver lining, and that was mine. The dedication to see things through and only give up if there was truly no other way to go, was the only reason I stood my ground. Even when those closest to me told me I was a fool to think my ideas and in fact this blog would ever amount to anything.

Because of that, I was able to build, destroy and rebuild again. Because of that, the things that would have destroyed me only left scars that I believe time, in its benevolence, will one day heal.

So why do I talk about this, I talk about it because I have met many who have had more courage than me, more patience. The young man who started a start up right out of campus that became a slogan for the youth of my country to defy hate. That took him all over the world, that saw him named one of the most influential youth of our time before he turned 30.

The young poet who did not refer to herself as one and yet had the courage to take a step of faith and believe in herself and who will one day be named among the poetry and literary greats in my country. Who was braver than me when it came to using her voice. Whose courage has now set others free to follow their paths in a continent that shuns the creative arts 🎭.

So why even try? You ask … we try because we ask ourselves what if … what if it works out better than we ever imagined … what if we succeed beyond our wildest dreams? What if we shatter the glass ceiling that the world and our self sabotage has put in our paths, the barriers that prevent us from soaring above the skies? What if we become everything we are meant to be and more?

Today, when the dark clouds of doubt seek to take away your dreams, never forget to ask yourselves… What if?

When destiny calls to us, when the fire within us refuses to be quenched and that still soft voice refuses to be silenced. We must listen, we must rise and we must take the leap.

If we do not fall … then at least we will learn to fly. The end of one dream is the beginning of another. Hope and Faith is all we have.

Take the leap!

🇺🇸 HOW TO VERIFY INFORMATION …NOT JUST BELIEVE THE HEADLINE

We live in an age where anyone can post anything…and many people take it as truth without checking…

Between AI-generated images, half-truths, misleading claims, and viral videos, misinformation spreads faster than real facts. Here’s a practical guide to help you separate fact from fiction.

🧠 WHY IT’S EASY TO BELIEVE SOMETHING

When something sounds plausible…or fits what you already think …most people stop questioning it. 

That’s human nature. 
But headlines are designed to trigger emotions, not accuracy. So before you repost or react:

Pause. Breathe. Ask a few key questions…

🧪 KEY PRACTICES TO VALIDATE INFORMATION..

📍1. Check the Source

• Is it from a well-known news organization? If so, who owns it.. that will help you identify if it is bias.. 
• Are multiple reputable outlets reporting it? And if so, HOW are they reporting it? 
• Avoid screenshots without a link or at least a source and publication date… 

Educated sources matter …fringe sites and “anonymous screenshots” often distort or exaggerate… 

🧐2. Look for Primary Evidence..

• Is there an original document, video, or direct quote?
• Does the claim link to an official report, public record, or court filing?
• Sometimes a simple Google search can verify or debunk…

🤔3. Understand the Difference Between:

✔ Opinion or interpretation
vs
✔ Verifiable claims of fact

Opinions are fine …they’re personal. But facts need evidence…

🧠4. Beware of AI-Generated Images..

With today’s AI tools, photos can be created that look real but never happened.
Ask yourself:
• Does this image have a credible source?
• Is it verified by news outlets?
• Are there inconsistencies in shadows, reflections, proportions, or context?

If not, treat it with skepticism.

👀 SHORT EXAMPLES OF MISINFORMATION WHAT IT WAS VS WHAT REALLY HAPPENED

🔹 EXAMPLE 1 — Epstein Files Misleading Spin

Many posts on social media claimed explosive, secret “blackmail lists” or unverified gossip were proof of crimes…
But in reality the files contain:
• unverified tips
• hearsay
• investigative notes that don’t equal guilt
• redacted reports with missing context

The mere presence of a name or copied snippet doesn’t mean wrongdoing happened….

Lesson: Documents without context aren’t proof they’re starting points for investigation, not conclusions….

🔹 EXAMPLE 2 — 5-Year-Old Boy & ICE

Some outlets and posts claimed ICE used a 5-year-old boy as “bait” to arrest his father implying intentional cruelty.
But federal officials specifically rejected that narrative, saying the father ran from agents and abandoned the child….DHS described the “bait” allegation as a false framing, not what actually happened.￼..

Lesson: Always look for official statements or government responses …they often clarify what really happened vs what went viral…

🧠 QUESTIONS TO ASK BEFORE YOU SHARE

➡ Who reported this?
➡ Are there multiple independent sources?
➡ Is it an opinion, or is it backed by evidence?
➡ Could this be a manipulated image or out-of-context quote?
➡ Am I reacting to a headline, a screenshot, or an actual report?

If you can’t answer these confidently …don’t share it yet…

🧾 TRUST BUT VERIFY..

Truth isn’t about who shouts loudest …it’s about what can be proven with sources you can actually check…

Learning how to validate information isn’t just helpful …it’s essential in a world of instant posts, AI images, and viral claims.

Be curious, not gullible.
Be informed, not influenced.

Nthabiseng is jolted awake by the piercing sound of police sirens blazing outside the mansion, the shrill wail piercing through the darkness like a scream. She springs off the bed, her heart racing like a jackrabbit on steroids, and snatches her phone to check the time with trembling hands. 12:00 AM stares back at her, the midnight hour casting an eerie glow on her tense face, illuminating the fear etched on her features. "What are they doing here?" she mutters, a shiver running down her spine, her voice barely audible over the cacophony of sirens and her own ragged breathing.

Her mind instantly flashes back to the scuffling mess with Kanyisa, her estranged... whatever she was. The argument had gotten heated, things got out of hand, and now... now the police are at her door, their presence looming like a dark cloud over her head. A loud, insistent knock jacks her anxiety up a notch, making her jump like a startled cat. She almost loses her footing, stumbling backward as her bare feet hit the cold floor.

"Nthabiseng, open the door. I know you're in there," Kanyisa's voice booms from the other side, her tone dripping with an unsettling calmness that sends a chill down her spine. Good thing she had the foresight to lock the door, her fingers had automatically clicked the latch shut, a habit she'd developed over the years. Panic sets in, and she frantically reaches for her phone, her fingers flying across the screen as she dials Tshepo's number, her heart pounding in her ears like a drumbeat. Luckily, he picks up on the first ring, his voice a welcome lifeline in the storm.

"Tshepo, it's the police, they're here, I-" she starts, but Tshepo cuts her off, his tone dripping with malice, like venom injected into her veins.

"Good, I called them for you, since you beat up my wife." Nthabiseng's eyes widen, and she freezes, lost for words, her mind reeling in shock. The words hang in the air like a bad omen, making her stomach twist into knots.

"I'm pregnant, carrying your baby, Tshepo. I can't go to jail," she says, her voice cracking as desperation creeps in, her words spilling out in a tearful rush. The police bang on the door again, making her jump, the sound echoing through her like a thunderclap.

"Open the damn door!" they shout, their voices a harsh intrusion on her fragile composure.

Nthabiseng's mind is racing – she wants to hide, to run far away, to escape the nightmare unfolding around her, but she's stuck upstairs, trapped like a bird in a gazing, fluttering against the bars. Jumping out the window isn't an option; she can't risk breaking a bone or worse, not with a baby on the way, not with her life stretching out before her like a fragile thread.

The police move swiftly, breaking through the door with a loud crash, as Nthabiseng scrambles backward, her eyes wide with fear, her heart racing like a jackrabbit on steroids. Tshepo's face is a mask of cold fury, his jaw clenched tight as he stares at Nthabiseng, his eyes flashing with anger, his gaze piercing like a dagger.

"Arrest her," he says, his voice firm, as if daring Nthabiseng to defy him, his words dripping with authority.

Nthabiseng's world crumbles, her legs buckling beneath her as she collapses to the ground, her body shaking with sobs. "No, no, they can't. I'm pregnant. I..." Her words are lost in a wail as she rolls on the ground, crying, her hands covering her face, her fingers grasping at her hair, as if trying to hold onto something, anything.

"Tshepo, I'm carrying your child, you can't do this to me," she says, her voice piercing, as if trying to reach some hidden part of him, her words echoing off the walls, filling the room with desperation. "She's the one that attacked me first, I fought back in self defence." She adds.

Kanyisa's anger boils over, her face reddening, her eyes blazing with fury. "I started the fight? Girl, you started it even though I told you to leave my premises, but you forced your way in. That's trespassing, and hitting me on top of that. I'm opening a case against you, so next time you learn to stay away from married men!" she half-shouts, her words laced with venom, her body trembling with rage.

She's not just angry at Nthabiseng, but at Tshepo too. Why would he cheat on her, when she does everything for him? God knows he has nothing under his name, and still taking chances on losing everything? The injustice of it all fuels her anger, making her words sharper, her tone colder, her eyes flashing with a mix of hurt and betrayal.

Nthabiseng's sobs intensify, her body shaking with grief, as the police move to take her away, their hands firm but gentle, as if trying to calm a wild animal. "Please, no, don't take me. Tshepo, don't do this," she pleads.

"Take her," Tshepo demands, his voice cold, cutting off Nthabiseng's desperate pleas. The police nod, their faces expressionless, as they haul Nthabiseng away, her cries and sobs echoing down the corridor, her body struggling against their grip.

As soon as the door closes behind them, Kanyisa turns to Tshepo, her eyes blazing with a deadly glare, her face twisted in a mixture of anger and hurt. Tshepo's eyes flicker, but he stands his ground.

"I swear I don't know her," he says, his voice smooth, his words dripping with innocence.

Kanyisa's laughter is low and menacing. "I never said you do, but she came here and said you're her boyfriend and that you two are expecting." She shakes her head, her eyes rolling in disgust. Lord, why are men like this? she thinks, her mind reeling with the betrayal.

Tshepo's denial is instant. "She must got a loose screw, my love. I swear I don't know her." He takes a step closer to Kanyisa, his hands reaching out to placate her, but she shrugs him off, her body language screaming "back off".

Kanyisa's voice is ice. "Yazin, Tshepo. I will find out the truth, and once I do... we're getting a divorce." She turns on her heel, her exit swift and silent, leaving Tshepo looking uneasy, his mask slipping for a fraction of a second.

She stalks off to check on their children, hoping they didn't see the ugly scene, her mind racing with the implications, her heart heavy with betrayal.
