The biggest myth in Israeli public discourse is that “Israelis will never accept a Palestinian state.”

I hear it all the time. Usually from people who are absolutely convinced they understand the Israeli public better than anyone else.

So I decided to test it.

I struck up a conversation with a random stranger. No politics at first. Then I asked how he votes. Long-time right-wing, Likud supporter. Not anti-state, not “peace camp,” not someone who trusts Palestinians.

I told him the goal I’m working toward: creating a stable, peace-seeking Palestinian state alongside Israel.

His reaction was immediate and sharp:
“Impossible. It’s not in their nature. Look at the region. Look at Gaza. Look at the Arab world.”

This is the standard Israeli response. Not hatred. Not ideology. Fear — built from experience.

Then I explained the actual approach. Not slogans. Not “trust them.”
A staged process.
Security first.
Governance benchmarks.
Time for Palestinian leadership to develop.
Clear Israeli conditions.
No leap into the dark.

When I finished, his answer changed completely:

“If you can actually do that — blessings on you.”

Not enthusiasm. Not conversion.
But openness.

And that’s the point most people miss.

The barrier inside Israel is not a principled rejection of Palestinian statehood. It’s a rejection of risk. Israelis don’t believe a Palestinian state will be peaceful or stable. They believe it will become another Gaza.

Change that assumption — and Israeli attitudes change with it.

Most Israelis are not attached to the territories for ideological reasons. They are attached to survival. If a credible path exists that reduces danger rather than increases it, support expands far beyond what people imagine.

The real work, then, is not convincing Israelis that “peace is good.” Everyone knows that.

The work is building a plan that feels safe enough that ordinary Israelis — including right-wing ones — can say:
“Maybe. If it really works that way.”

That is the task ahead.

Not shouting.
Not moralizing.
Not assuming Israelis are blind or Palestinians are saints.

Building a path that addresses fear, step by step, until acceptance becomes possible.

Lawyer Juol Nhomngek Daniel, member of the SPLM-IO, tells Radio Tamazuj that South Sudan’s conflict is not just about political power—it stems from weak institutions, exclusionary governance, militarized politics, historical grievances, and the collapse of social trust.

He highlighted:

● The 2018 Revitalised Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS) is the only comprehensive framework capable of delivering positive peace.

● Positive peace means justice, accountable governance, inclusion, and social cohesion—not just silenced guns.

● R-ARCSS replaces zero-sum politics with dialogue, power-sharing, and collective responsibility, creating a unified presidency and transitional government.

● It addresses security sector reform, disarmament, and professional national forces, crucial for restoring civilian trust.

● Transitional justice mechanisms—truth, accountability, reparations, and guarantees of non-repetition—anchor sustainable peace.

● The Agreement promotes territorial federalism, fair resource management, and safe return of displaced citizens, linking political reform to economic stability.

● Elections are mandated after meaningful reforms, ensuring democracy is built on a solid foundation.

Juol Nhomngek Daniel warns: abandoning R-ARCSS risks perpetual collapse. It is not just a peace deal—it is a state-building blueprint for justice, inclusion, and lasting stability.

The phone call came at dawn. Four bodies had been found in shallow graves outside a small Salvadoran town.

Sister Maura Clarke was one of them.

Just two days earlier, she'd been laughing with friends at a conference in Nicaragua. At 49, Maura had spent more than half her life serving the poorest people in Central America. She could have stayed safe in Nicaragua, where the revolution had finally brought hope.

Instead, she chose El Salvador. The most dangerous place on earth for anyone who dared help the poor.

Maura grew up in Queens, New York, in an Irish Catholic family that believed faith meant action. While other girls her age dreamed of marriage and children, Maura felt called to something different. Something bigger.

At 19, she joined the Maryknoll Sisters. A missionary order that sent women to the furthest corners of the world.

In 1959, they sent her to Nicaragua.

The poverty hit her like a physical blow. Children with bloated bellies from hunger. Families living in shacks made of cardboard and tin. People dying from diseases that could be cured with medicine that cost pennies.

Maura rolled up her sleeves and got to work.

She taught children who had never owned books. She held dying babies in her arms. She learned Spanish from women who couldn't read their own names but could recite every prayer by heart.

For years, Maura believed charity was enough. Feed the hungry. Heal the sick. Comfort the dying.

Then the earthquake came.

On December 23, 1972, the ground beneath Managua shook like the world was ending. Buildings collapsed. Thousands died. International aid poured in to help the survivors.

But Maura watched in horror as dictator Anastasio Somoza and his cronies stole the relief money. They built mansions while earthquake victims starved in refugee camps.

That's when she understood. You couldn't heal people and then send them back to the same system that was killing them.

She started supporting protesters. She marched with students demanding justice. She occupied government buildings. Her fellow nuns worried she'd gone too far.

But the Nicaraguan people had a different name for her. They called her "the angel of our land."

In 1979, the Nicaraguan people finally overthrew Somoza. Maura wasn't there to see it – she was back in the United States, teaching other Americans about what their government was really doing in Central America.

When she heard the news of victory, friends said she was "bubbling with joy."

She returned to Nicaragua in 1980 to help rebuild the country she'd served for two decades. It should have been the happiest time of her life.

But then came the urgent call from El Salvador.

Archbishop Oscar Romero had been murdered while saying Mass. Death squads were hunting anyone who worked with the poor. Bodies appeared on roadsides every morning. Families searched for loved ones who would never come home.

The Maryknoll Sisters needed help. Desperately.

Maura could have said no. She was 49 years old. She'd already given enough. She deserved to stay in Nicaragua and celebrate their hard-won freedom.

Instead, she packed her bags.

Her first weeks in El Salvador were like living in hell. She searched for the disappeared. She buried mutilated bodies. She comforted mothers whose children had been tortured.

In her letters home, she wrote with brutal honesty: "My fear of death is being challenged constantly as children, lovely young girls, old people are being shot and some cut up with machetes."

But she also wrote this: "There is real peace in spite of many frustrations and the terror around us. God is very present in His seeming absence."

In late November, Maura traveled back to Nicaragua for a regional meeting of all the Maryknoll Sisters. Her friends begged her not to return to El Salvador.

She told them she had to go back. "If we leave the people when they suffer the cross, how credible is our word to them?"

On December 2, 1980, Maura and her fellow nun Ita Ford flew back to El Salvador. Their friends Dorothy Kazel and Jean Donovan picked them up at the airport in a white van.

The four women never made it home.

Members of El Salvador's National Guard, acting on orders from above, stopped their van on an isolated road. They dragged the women to a remote field.

They beat them. They raped them. They shot them. They buried them in shallow graves.

Jean Donovan was 27 and engaged to be married. Dorothy Kazel was 40 and beloved by everyone who knew her. Ita Ford was 40 and still mourning another friend who had died serving the poor. Maura Clarke was 49 and had spent half her life loving people the world forgot.

All four died because they refused to abandon the poorest of the poor.

Their murders became an international scandal. Presidents condemned the killings. Aid was suspended. The world paid attention to El Salvador like never before.

But for Maura's family back in Queens, no amount of international outrage could fill the hole in their hearts.

The woman who had left home as a shy 19-year-old novice had died as a martyr. She'd kept the promise she made all those years ago – to love God by serving the least of these.

Even when it cost her everything.

Today, stained glass windows in her childhood church show Maura's face alongside the saints. Schools bear her name. Every December 2nd, people gather to remember four women who chose love over safety.

Maura Clarke proved that ordinary people can do extraordinary things. That a girl from Queens can change the world. That faith isn't about feeling safe – it's about doing right even when you're terrified.

Her last words still echo across the years: "God is very present in His seeming absence."

Sometimes the most powerful presence is found in the places that seem most abandoned. Sometimes love shows up strongest in the darkest moments.

Maura Clarke knew that. She lived it. She died for it.

And her light still shines.

After an 18-hour shift, I came home and found my daughter asleep. Hours later, I tried to wake her—no response. When I confronted my mother, she shrugged. “She was annoying. I gave her some pills to make her quiet.” My sister laughed. “She’ll wake up. And if she doesn’t? At least we’ll finally have peace.” I called an ambulance. The medical report they handed me made my hands go numb.

The fluorescent lights of the hospital corridor screamed overhead, a familiar electric hum that had morphed into something sinister, slicing through my senses like a razor. It wasn't just background noise anymore; it was the soundtrack to a nightmare. I sat rigid in the plastic waiting room chair, my hands clasped so tightly the knuckles turned bone-white, aching with tension. Six hours earlier, pure adrenaline had carried me through a chaotic storm of sirens, shouted commands, and pools of blood. Now that the chemical rush had evaporated, all that remained was a shaking exhaustion and a hollow, consuming dread that I couldn't outrun.
My name is Evan Harper. I’m 34 years old, an emergency room nurse at St. Mary’s General Hospital who has survived the trenches for nearly a decade. I’ve seen bodies mangled in ways that defy physics. I’ve plugged bullet holes with my bare hands, talked families through the shattering of their worlds, and mastered the art of keeping my voice steady while my insides screamed. I had just finished a brutal 18-hour shift, bouncing from cardiac arrests to traumas without a moment to breathe. The cruel irony was laughing at me now as I sat powerless, waiting to hear if my own daughter would survive the shift I wasn't there for.
When I finally dragged myself home a little after 2 a.m., my apartment was dark and possessed a heavy, unnatural silence. I moved like a ghost down the narrow hallway. Clara’s bedroom door was slightly ajar, bleeding a sliver of warm light. I peeked in and saw her curled up, dark hair fanned out, clutching Mr. Peanuts, her battered stuffed elephant.
She looked peaceful, blissfully unaware of the chaos I carried on my skin. I remember smiling, that moment acting as the only antidote to the horrors of my day. I whispered goodnight to the air, promising to make it up to her later, and collapsed into my own bed, thinking everything was fine.
My living situation was a disaster held together by duct tape. After my ex-wife Hannah chased a new romance to California, leaving Clara behind, my mother, Linda (58), moved in to help. Shortly after, my sister Natalie (26) crashed with us after getting evicted. It was supposed to be a village raising a child.
But Linda was controlling and narcissistic, treating Clara more like a noisy appliance than a granddaughter. And Natalie... she used to be sweet, but lately, she had morphed into someone bitter and sharp, snapping at Clara for existing, acting as if a five-year-old’s laughter was personally ruining her life.
I slept the deep, dreamless sleep of the dead. When I woke around 10 a.m., sunlight mocked me through the blinds. The apartment was terrifyingly quiet. Usually, Clara would be thundering down the hall, demanding breakfast or playtime.
I rushed to her room. She was in the exact same position as 2 a.m. Face to the wall. A cold knot formed in my gut. "Clara, sweetheart," I said, sitting on the bed. "Time to wake up."
She didn't move.
I shook her shoulder. Her skin was clammy, cold, and possessed the terrifying limpness of a ragdoll. My training kicked in instantly. Breathing: shallow, ragged. I lifted an eyelid: pupil dilated, sluggish, barely reacting.
My heart slammed against my ribs like a trapped bird. "MOM!" I roared. "NATALIE! GET IN HERE NOW!"
Linda appeared in the doorway, coffee mug in hand, wearing an expression of supreme annoyance, as if I’d interrupted a crucial TV show. Natalie shuffled behind her, eyes bloodshot, looking utterly bored.
"What is with the screaming?" Linda snapped.
"Something is wrong with Clara," I said, my voice vibrating with suppressed rage. "She’s unresponsive. Her breathing is failing. What happened while I was asleep? Did she fall? Did she eat something?"
Linda hesitated. I saw it—the flicker of guilt, the look of a liar buying time. She sipped her coffee. "She was fine when she went to bed," she lied, the words practiced.
"I DIDN'T ASK ABOUT BEDTIME," I bellowed. "WHAT HAPPENED AFTER I GOT HOME?"
The silence stretched, thick and suffocating. Natalie leaned against the doorframe, inspecting a hangnail. Linda’s grip tightened on her mug, and she finally went on the defensive. "She was being so annoying. Kept waking up around midnight, crying about a bad dream. She wouldn't shut up. So I gave her something to calm her down."
The world tilted on its axis. "You gave her what?"
"Just my sleeping pills," Linda said fast, dismissing it. "Maybe two. It’s not a big deal. She needed sleep. You needed rest."
I stared at her, bile rising in my throat. "YOU GAVE A FIVE-YEAR-OLD ADULT SLEEPING PILLS? WHAT KIND? HOW MANY?"
"Zulpadm. Ten milligrams. I think I gave her two, she's big for her age, I thought it would be fine," she retorted, her tone daring me to challenge her logic.
Natalie let out a short, sharp laugh that sounded like glass breaking. "She’ll probably wake up," she said casually. "And if she doesn't, well, at least we'll finally have some peace and quiet around here."
The cruelty hit me harder than a physical blow. I looked at my sister and saw a stranger—a monster. There was no time to scream. Clara’s breathing hitched, a terrible rattling sound, and her head lolled lifelessly against my chest.
I wrapped her in a blanket and dialed 911, my hands shaking violently while my voice switched to a chillingly calm, clinical tone. "This is Evan Harper, ER nurse at St. Mary’s. My five-year-old daughter is unresponsive. SUSPECTED ZULPADM OVERDOSE. ADULT DOSAGE. I need a bus now."
The paramedics arrived, shattering the morning peace. Maria Santos took one look at Clara and her face went pale. "We need to move," she commanded, starting lines and bagging her.
The ride to the hospital was a blur of beeping monitors and the smell of oxygen. I held Clara’s limp hand, riding in the back of an ambulance not as a nurse, but as a terrified father watching his world crumble.
At St. Mary’s, Dr. Jennifer Walsh took over, her face a mask of focus. I was pushed back, forced to be a spectator. When she finally turned to me, the look in her eyes was devastating.
"Evan," she said sharply. "I need the exact dosage. Now."
I told her everything—the pills, the time, my mother’s horrific justification. Jennifer nodded slowly, grimly. "Zulpadm at that dose for a child her size causes severe respiratory depression and potential organ failure. We're running a full tox screen and starting dialysis, but this is... critical."
I sat there, staring at the closed trauma bay doors, my mind looping Natalie’s cruel laugh and my mother’s casual excuse. When Dr. Walsh returned with the initial scan results, the specific medical words she used made my chest implode and my ears ring with a deafening high-pitched whine.

NQOBILE

Olwemihla wanted to take a day-off today, just to sit and nurse me, her older sister who should be nursing her. I’ve failed her in some way, that’s how it feels because I went from getting in this marriage for her studies to staying because I love that man. Part of the reason I refused to let her be shacked up with me is because of guilt, that she could have had a brighter future than I did had I forgot about my problems and focus on getting everything of hers finalized.
I’m such an idiot, Mrs X se foot! Look at me now, there is nothing to show for it on me. I’m just a sad, little girl who just wasted three weeks of her miserable life and ended up making a mess of it at the same time. 

I roll off bed in regret, my headache is banging both back and front – misery at its best and it’s only after my yawn do I remember, I was deadass intoxicated last night. Tipsy at most and heartbroken too. 
It feels like shit to think about all the things I said now, it feels like a very awful dream that Olwemihla will wake me up from. Still, I’m glad I left because man having slept the whole night without wondering what evil is coming our way, what phone call will we get and so on, is the best feeling ever. It feels light. 
First thing I do after my toilet trip is check my phones, then after that I will go make food for everyone and clean the house. Yup, I still remember the routine. 
There are missed calls, four – all from Bakho. I don’t get excited immediately, maybe he wants to remind me I left my underwear in his bathroom and I must come fetch it or something.
Scrolling through my notifications – his contact pops up again. An SMS this time around boldly reminding me to purge and steam. 
Shit! Why do important things slip my mind all the time? It’s like I’m running away from responsibility just like Beauty. 
Ugh, why am I even bringing that woman up now? I still hate her. It’s Sibahle whom I’d like to have a chat with, if she is ever still up for it.
If possible, I will even ask Zinhle to be present so she can help me say the right damn thing before I become an enemy of hers as well.
[SMS: Good Morn…]
There is nothing good about this morning. I erase that stupid line and start a new again, opting for something more proper and formal, the last thing I want to do is the give impression that I’m having regrets, even though I am.
[SMS: Morning Bungobakho Xolani Ximba, thank you for the reminder. Will do.] 
Yeah, that doesn’t sound suspicious at all. He won’t suspect that I’m still in my pyjamas at this shocking hour, terrible migraine, scratchy throat and a heartbreak to top off the cake. 
[SMS: Look out for yourself there, if you ever need anything let me know.] 
Well, I needed him. Just him. 
Sigh. This is what obsession feels like? I say fire to it in the name of the Lord! 
All I want to do is coddle him, smell him and look at him while counting his greys hairs that are beginning to grow heavy on his beard. 
That lump on my throat threatens me again, it’s difficult to ignore but c’mon Nqobile, you’ve seen it all now. There is nothing left to break you, everything has happened. You just have to get through this one as you did the previous hurdles.
I take my herbs and make my way to the kitchen with my ears fully closed. If Nonkanyiso is home, she will bark as always. 
If my father is home, well, I’m not sure about him anymore. Did he even come home last night? 
Imagine that, a whole anointed paster sleeping in shebeens with hookers who are there to pickpocket nothing else. That’s another kind of disgrace in my eyes. One I’ll have to swallow because I have nowhere else to stay but this roof of his. 

No one is roaming around the house by the time I’ve reached the kitchen. Mh good start to a bad morning. 
I grab the en from the cupboard, there’s no time for pots that thing takes too long and right now, all I want to do is eat.
“You will be cooking, mabuyemendweni.” Celebrated too quickly. 
I don’t want to think about what she could have said to me last night, it cannot be anything graceful for sure, so I’m fine still fuzzy and unable to make out anything other than the fact that Mr X and I are no longer together.
“Okay.” 
“I can’t believe you chose strangers over your own family. Ma is out of this house because of you, Nqobile. uBaba kicked her out because of you.” Hhayi this girl must not test my already boiling waters.
“Baba chased her because of her own ill mannerisms. Not me, I’ve had nothing to do with their mess before and I have nothing to do with it now. But for some fucked up reason, I’m always the child getting put to the blame. And I’ve had enough of that, so stick to your lane with me.” My spirit shouldn’t be this angry while doing this, isn’t? the anger spoils the whole process.
“What have you done for Baba and Ma, Nqobile? Im sorry to break it you but it’s nothing. They’ve taken care of you for free all these, I have taken care of you for more than two years whilst I was working in Aunt’s house. But I never complain, why do you always have to complain all the time?” she wouldn’t try to understand me even if it could save my life.
I’m not entertaining her, not today. 
“Did you hear you boyfriend, that’s what he is now ain’t he? He got arrested last night as well his brothers, for kidnapping a child. Mmmh, Nqobile, these are the kind of people you chose to associate with?” she’s shaking her head. 
“Can you put your nonsense to rest, Soso? It won’t do anything for you, not anymore. Mr x and I are done.” 
“Suit yourself with that evil family of yours, kidnapping children.” 
“You kidnapped me too, didn’t you? So why are you so quick to judge them, what gives you the slightest right to do that?” she’s trying to get on my nerves, Soso always does this. 
I close my eyes and try to picture Nolithemba’s cunning attitude towards her sister, I try to remember how she managed to whisper in Leleti’s ear the same way Soso is whispering in mine. But then I begin recalling the other bits I wasn’t intending on bringing up. The bits where I proudly hit my chest and said: ‘The only difference between Leleti and I, is that I will fight for my marriage.’ 
Lmao, marriage where? 
“You’re not a child and I was doing you a favour. Clearly God was showing you that you aren’t meant to be in that family.” Her  tongue is still just as sharp and I don’t see it ever changing.
“Have you always been this angry and hurt, Soso? Were you pretending to be kind and loving all those years? When you did my hair for school, did you maybe ever wish to strangle me with it?” it wouldn’t take me by surprise if she did. 
All these emotions can’t be something new to her; it must be how she has always felt because why else would she still harbour hatred for me even after I’ve left her fantasy husband alone?
“Hm, maybe. It’s a pity it wasn’t long enough.” Nonkanyiso shrugs and walks out the kitchen leaving me all by myself. 
I wait for her to get out before ever letting the mask slip off my face. I’m hurt by what she said, but most of all, I’m hurt she became this person because of me. What’s the difference between this and killing your brother? That there is no bloodshed in my hands but the crime stays. 
Is it even my fault? 
And Bakho, was it his fault?
I couldn’t have known any better, even if my wish was to tell her she doesn’t have to burden herself because of me, I was too young then to understand that my sister isn’t tying my buns crooked – but she’s fighting me for what I’m putting her through. 
But she was the adult. She should have chose herself. 
Even him, my husband, he should have chose himself. 
Instead, they chose to carry the burden. They did that not me; I can’t be blamed for that. I refuse!
I have to choose me, that’s my choice – Me, Me, Me and my sanity. 
Not their guilt, not their … 
Gracious! 

This is not choosing myself, me running to my bedroom and scrolling for MaZondi’s number is not me choosing myself. 
She picked up the call rather quickly. 
“MaGoqo.” That’s delightful, I thought she’d be calling me all sorts of names by now. 
“Hey MaZondi. What happened?” I forgot to greet but listen, no one would be okay if their husbands are in jail.
“Many things, a lot was revealed yesterday. Including your departure.” She doesn’t sound bitter about it, so I’ll explain to her as much as I can.
“It’s not you, any of you. I just got tired and scared – clueless. What am I doing with my life, you know? Where is my life taking me, because that’s the only person I’ll ever truly have MaZondi. Me.” 
“I think that’s a little ungrateful of you to believe you’ve only had yourself all this while when we’ve tried to show up for you as well as we possibly could. However, a girl must do what a girl’s gotta do, I wish you luck and try not to be Martha Stewart airing our dirty linen for publishing companies and the world to see.” Her giggles make me smile for once since the miserable mayhem begun.
“Will they be out soon?” it’s a rhetorical question, those are the Ximbas of course they will be out soon.
“Yah, they will be out but this is Nolithemba we are talking about. She won’t stop until her fetish is over.” Hold on…
What was Sinikiwe telling me? 
“Nolithemba had them arrested? I thought the article said they were arrested for kidnapping.” I haven’t even seen said article.
“It was all orchestrated by her. Nqanawe is Myalezo’s son, but because Kangaroo Madea was too busy humping every dick in town, she couldn’t tell who is the father until only later when the boy started looking like Kwame and Baba. And even then, she chose not to come forth with the child because she didn’t know where she would begin explaining how she gave birth to a fully grown child after 4 years so she continued hiding him between her many hoes from different area codes.” It’s her thing to be this unserious with such a delicate and serious question. 
“That is fucked up, Niki. But at least, they know who she is now right?” 
“Oh girl, you have been gone for too long already. Don’t you know our problems multiple and give birth to twins each? The retard waited for the guys to be arrested only then did she start threatening Leleti to file for divorce. Lele refused, and that bitch threatened to make their lives a living hell. That’s when she told us about her messy history.” It’s messy alright.
I’m glad Leleti stood ten toes for her marriage though. It deserved a second chance, hopefully Noli would be out of the picture by then.
“I hope Nolithemba does not succeed this time, Lele needs a break from her toxic ass.” 
“It’s hard to walk out on family.” She sighs.
“Even when it kills you?” 
“Even when it kills you, I think you’re living proof of that too.” The conversation is steering towards the direction I didn’t want it to.

“How is he?” why am I still asking? He wants nothing to do with me; I should do the same.
“Bungo is always one thing – hectic. Yesterday though he just seemed a little more finished nje, tired to an extreme point. Honestly, you’d think he has survived suicide four times this week alone.” 
“I didn’t want to hurt him.” 
“That’s none of our business, the marriage belongs to the two of you so you both have to fix it. Me advise though would be, stay where you are until you are certain of where you want to be. It takes balls in the stomach to survive here; it takes a certain level of stubbornness to make it here. Not because it’s hard or chaotic, but because we don’t know anything. We don’t know what we are doing, it seems to be working though so we keep doing it, unfortunately it doesn’t work all the times. Some days we actually have to take the L and welcome the defeat with open arms, next day again we must get up and fight again. Now that’s the exhausting part, it takes you being willing to bleed on your own chair placed on the high table, to get here. We are not perfect, but we are not bad people.” Ah, it’s that mantra again.
Now though I have a bit of understanding of it, I’ve witnessed it myself. They aren’t bad people, just very troubled people. And that is indeed, exhausting to deal with.
“And I think I see why African households believe in individualism in practise, forget what we preach – that ubuntu anthem is a theatre. Individualism is easy, Nqobile. You take no one on the ride with you but yourself, it makes sense and it’s peaceful. In African households we don’t meet for fun and drink and find ways to grow the clan into generational wealth – not just financially but with wisdom too, teachings and learnings. We don’t uplift each other and walk each other through life, because we are so broken and messy no one has the time to pick up the other’s pieces. Maybe that’s why the white man owns us all? He’s an oppressor but he gathers his own family to teach them how to oppress you, can you see that kind of unity? We are hoping to have that someday, and I trust we will when the stars have aligned. Bye girl, I have to go.” 
She drops.
I’m not going back; I can’t go back. 
I have to choose me.

Bab’Mkhize pivots in his garden couch, his eyes light up like a child’s eyes I swear. Whenever you need a faithful wingman, call Bab’Mkhize and recite his clan names every now and again.
“Ngcob’omhlophe. Ozal’uGasela. Fuze. Mavela.” 
“Mafuz’afulele njengefu lemvula.” We recite these ones together, and because he is a man, he’ll want to have the last praise, he says, “Sihayo!” still dancing on his one leg like he doesn’t have chronic joint issues.
“How are you are doing today, Baba?” I ask, lowering myself on the empty chair adjacent to his comfortable couch.
“Ai, we are still alive Gasela, we show gratitude for that. Our forefathers have showed us grace for this long.” He is such a cry-baby, this man is still fresh. If he wasn’t already married, I’d give Beauty a small shoutout.
“We live in  the world of the living, where sin was born and where sin is cleansed and repented. “You know nothing while living on this Earth, we know nothing Ngcob’omhlophe. the eye is envious and quick to betray you; you should never trust it because it will always lead you astray.” Poor old man, he sounds so pained and hopeless.

It will take you places you have no cooking clue how to get out of.
“She is grown, Baba. There is nothing you can do to save her from herself. Absolutely nothing.”

Be her protector and her first special male, she deserves that.” 
He's laughing now and mocking his first time meeting oBaba. I’ve learned a fun fact, Bab’omdala intimidates people in an offish way. 
Anway, the old man has too many stories, if I let him continue my children will be orphaned for the day. 

Lele is sleeping on the couch, thumb in her mouth. I can’t imagine how much Myalezo hates seeing her do that. He always a problem with Nozipho always doing the same, at some point he threatened to cut her finger off. 
“Wakey-wakey sleepyhead.” I poke her cheek and wait for her to get a fright of her life, with that fugitive sister of hers on a run, anything is possible
“MaNgcobo.” She stretches and makes some space for me.

“I came to see how you are doing?” she looked well into shock last night.
And I don’t blame her, those cops treated us like we were a drug bust or something. Sinikiwe had to psychically push her to the ground to lie on her stomach because she just froze in the moment. They took them all, all of them and that bitch was there with them, arms crossed and chest high like she had achieved something she’s been waiting years to do.
It took everything in all of us not to gut her with that noodle spoon that was on the table. 
“I’m nowhere near okay, MaNgcobo. I trusted her so blindly, she fooled me for years and years on end. I let her into every part of my life, not knowing I was inviting a snake in my territory. ⚠️BID'AH BULAN RAMADHAN

Oleh : 
Ustadz Abu Sa’id 
Satria Buana

Muroja’ah : 
Ustadz Abu Salman

*Bulan Ramadhan adalah bulan yang penuh dengan barakah dan penuh dengan keutamaan.* Allah subhanahu wa ta’ala telah mensyariatkan dalam bulan tersebut berbagai macam amalan ibadah yang banyak agar manusia semakin mendekatkan diri kepada-Nya. Akan tetapi sebagian dari kaum muslimin berpaling dari keutamaan ini dan membuat cara-cara baru dalam beribadah. Mereka lupa firman Allah ta’ala, “Pada hari ini Aku telah menyempurnakan agama kalian.” (QS. Al-Maidah: 3). Mereka ingin melalaikan manusia dari ibadah yang disyariatkan. Mereka tidak merasa cukup dengan apa yang telah dicontohkan oleh Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam dan para sahabat beliau ridhwanullahi ‘alaihim ajma’iin.

Oleh sebab itu pada tulisan ini kami mencoba mengangkat beberapa amalan bid’ah yang banyak dilakukan oleh kaum muslimin, yaitu amalan-amalan yang dilakukan akan tetapi tidak diajarkan oleh Nabi kita shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam maupun para sahabat beliau, semoga dengan mengetahuinya kaum muslimin bisa meninggalkan perbuatan tersebut.

*🛑 BID'AH BERZIKIR DENGAN KERAS SETELAH SALAM SHALAT TARAWIH*

Berzikir dengan suara keras setelah melakukan salam pada shalat tarawih dengan dikomandani oleh satu suara adalah perbuatan yang tidak disyariatkan. Begitu pula perkataan muazin, “assholaatu yarhakumullah” dan yang semisal dengan perkataan tersebut ketika hendak melaksanakan shalat tarawih, perbuatan ini juga tidak disyariatkan oleh Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam, tidak pula oleh para sahabat maupun orang-orang yang mengikuti mereka dengan baik. Oleh karena itu hendaklah kita merasa cukup dengan sesuatu yang telah mereka contohkan. Seluruh kebaikan adalah dengan mengikuti jejak mereka dan segala keburukan adalah dengan membuat-buat perkara baru yang tidak ada tuntunannya dari mereka.

*🛑 MEMBANGUNKAN ORANG-ORANG UNTUK SAHUR*

Perbuatan ini merupakan salah satu bid’ah yang tidak pernah dilakukan pada masa Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam, beliau tidak pernah memerintahkan hal ini. Perbedaan tata-cara membangunkan sahur dari tiap-tiap daerah juga menunjukkan tidak disyariatkannya hal ini, padahal jika seandainya perkara ini disyariatkan maka tentunya mereka tidak akan berselisih.

*🛑 MELAFAZKAN NIAT*

Melafazkan niat ketika hendak melaksanakan puasa Ramadhan adalah tradisi yang dilakukan oleh banyak kaum muslimin, tidak terkecuali di negeri kita. Di antara yang kita jumpai adalah imam masjid shalat tarawih ketika selesai melaksanakan shalat witir mereka mengomandoi untuk bersama-sama membaca niat untuk melakukan puasa besok harinya.

Perbuatan ini adalah perbuatan yang tidak di contohkan oleh Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam juga orang-orang saleh setelah beliau. Yang sesuai tuntunan adalah berniat untuk melaksanakan puasa pada malam hari sebelumnya cukup dengan meniatkan dalam hati saja, tanpa dilafazkan.

*🛑 IMSAK*

Tradisi imsak, sudah menjadi tren yang dilakukan kaum muslimin ketika ramadhan. Ketika waktu sudah hampir fajar, maka sebagian orang meneriakkan “imsak, imsak…” supaya orang-orang tidak lagi makan dan minum padahal saat itu adalah waktu yang bahkan Rasulullah menganjurkan kita untuk makan dan minum. Sahabat Anas meriwayatkan dari Zaid bin Sabit radhiyallahu ‘anhuma, “Kami makan sahur bersama Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam kemudian beliau shalat. Maka kata Anas, “Berapa lama jarak antara azan dan sahur?”, Zaid menjawab, “Kira-kira 50 ayat membaca ayat al-Qur’an.” (HR. Bukhari dan Muslim)

*🛑 MENUNDA ADZAN MAGRIB DENGAN ALASAN KEHATI-HATIAN*

Hal ini bertentangan dengan perintah Nabi shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam yang menganjurkan kita untuk menyegerakan berbuka. Rasulullah bersabda,

لاَ يَزَالُ النَّاسُ بِخَيْرٍ مَا عَجَّلُوا الْفِطْرَ

“Manusia senantiasa berada dalam kebaikan selama mereka menyegerakan berbuka.” (HR. Bukhari Muslim)

*🛑 TAKBIRAN*

Yaitu menyambut datangnya ied dengan mengeraskan membaca takbir dan memukul bedug pada malam ied. Perbuatan ini tidak disyariatkan, yang sesuai dengan sunah adalah melakukan takbir ketika keluar rumah hendak melaksanakan shalat ied sampai tiba di lapangan tempat melaksanakan shalat ied.

*🛑 BADUSAN*

Yaitu Mandi besar pada satu hari menjelang satu ramadhan dimulai. Perbuatan ini tidak disyariatkan dalam agama ini, yang menjadi syarat untuk melakukan puasa ramadhan adalah niat untuk berpuasa esok pada malam sebelum puasa, adapun mandi junub untuk puasa Ramadhan tidak ada tuntunannya dari Nabi kita shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam.

*🛑 MENDAHULUI PUASA SATU HARI ATAU DUA HARI SEBELUMNYA*

Rasulullah telah melarang mendahului puasa ramadhan dengan melakukan puasa pada dua hari terakhir di bulan sya’ban, kecuali bagi yang memang sudah terbiasa puasa pada jadwal tersebut, misalnya puasa senin kamis atau puasa dawud. Rasulullah bersabda, “Janganlah kalian mendahului puasa ramadhan dengan melakukan puasa satu hari atau dua hari sebelumnya. Kecuali bagi yang terbiasa melakukan puasa pada hari tersebut maka tidak apa-apa baginya untuk berpuasa.” (HR. Bukhari dan Muslim)

*🛑 PERAYAAN NUZUL QUR’AN*

Yaitu melaksanakan perayaan pada tanggal 17 Ramadhan, untuk mengenang saat-saat diturunkannya al-Qur’an. Perbuatan ini tidak ada tuntunannya dari praktek Rasulullah shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam, begitu pula para sahabat sepeninggal beliau.

*🛑 BERZIARAH KUBUR KARENA RAMADHAN*

Tradisi ziarah kubur menjelang atau sesudah ramadhan banyak dilakukan oleh kaum muslimin, bahkan di antara mereka ada yang sampai berlebihan dengan melakukan perbuatan-perbuatan syirik di sana. Perbuatan ini tidak disyariatkan. Ziarah kubur dianjurkan agar kita teringat dengan kematian dan akhirat, akan tetapi mengkhususkannya karena even tertentu tidak ada tuntunannya dari Rasulullah maupun para sahabat ridhwanullahi ‘alaihim ajma’iin.

Inilah beberapa bid’ah yang dilakukan oleh sebagian kaum muslimin, khususnya di negeri kita, semoga Allah ta’ala memberikan kita ilmu yang bermanfaat, sehingga kita bisa meninggalkan perkara-perkara tersebut dan melakukan perbuatan yang sesuai dengan tuntunan Nabi kita Muhammad shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam.

Reminiscing #YouthWeek / #YouthDay in #Cameroon
Youth Day once symbolized unity, hope, and a collective identity.

It was a time when young people from different schools, backgrounds, and communities came together, on football fields, handball courts, and in choir stands, not divided by tribe, language, or belief, but united by a common purpose.

For many of us, it was our first lesson in teamwork, respect, and peaceful competition. We remember the excitement of carefully ironing our uniforms, buying new socks, and eagerly waiting for February 11th to come, ready to represent our schools with pride and dignity.

Beyond the sports and songs, Youth Day taught us something deeper:
 that youth voices matter,
 that diversity is strength,
 and that progress is built through dialogue, not division.

Today, that spirit is more important than ever. As we strive to build a #HateFreeCameroon, Youth Day reminds us that young voices must be heard, included, and empowered to choose peace NOT #Hate.

The question is: Are we nurturing spaces where young people feel heard? Are we empowering youth to become peacebuilders and not instruments of division?

What did Youth Day mean to you ?

JUBA — In a critical move toward the 2026 electoral roadmap, the National Elections Commission (NEC) officially released the list of 102 national constituencies for the upcoming parliamentary race.

The announcement, formalized by NEC Chairperson Prof. Abednego Akok Kacuol, follows a landmark political decision by parties to the R-ARCSS peace agreement to decouple the elections from the long-delayed national census.

RJMEC: اتفاق السلام في جنوب السودان مهدد مع تدهور الوضع السياسي والأمني 

 تقرير: إيمانويل قارجيك

حذر اللجنة المشتركة المعاد تشكيلها للمتابعة والتقييم (RJMEC) يوم الاثنين، أثناء إحاطتها لمجلس الأمن التابع للأمم المتحدة، من أن اتفاق السلام الهش في جنوب السودان يواجه تهديدًا خطيرًا في ظل تدهور الأوضاع السياسية والأمنية.

وقال السفير والرئيس المؤقت للجنة، الجنرال جورج أقري أوينو (المتقاعد)، في كلمته أمام المجلس افتراضيًا، إن تنفيذ اتفاق 2018 المنقح لحل النزاع في جنوب السودان (R-ARCSS) أصبح "في خطر جدي" بسبب استمرار انتهاكات وقف إطلاق النار، والصراعات السياسية الداخلية، واتخاذ القرارات الأحادية داخل الحكومة.

وأشار أوينو إلى أن ترتيبات تقاسم المسؤوليات ضمن اتفاق السلام مستمرة في التآكل، مستشهدًا بإزالة واستبدال ممثلي المعارضة من المناصب التنفيذية والتشريعية على المستويين الوطني والولائي.

 كما لفت إلى أن النائب الأول للرئيس الدكتور ريك مشار، زعيم حركة تحرير السودان/الجيش الشعبي (SPLM/A-IO)، ما زال محتجزًا ويخضع للمحاكمة مع مسؤولين آخرين من حزبه، ما يزيد من تعقيد التوترات السياسية.

ووفقًا لـ RJMEC، تُتخذ القرارات بشكل متزايد ضمن الحكومة الوحدة الوطنية الانتقالية (RTGoNU) دون توافق جميع الموقعين على اتفاق السلام، بما يمثل انتهاكًا واضحًا للاتفاق.

على الصعيد الأمني، أشار أوينو إلى أن وقف إطلاق النار الدائم قد تم انتهاكه بشدة منذ مارس 2025، مع استمرار الاشتباكات بين قوات الدفاع الشعبي لجمهورية جنوب السودان (SSPDF) وSPLA-IO في ولايتي أعالي النيل وجونقلي، بالإضافة إلى قتال متكرر في أجزاء من منطقة أعالي النيل الكبرى.

وأظهرت بيانات آلية مراقبة والتحقق من وقف إطلاق النار والأمن الانتقالي (CTSAMVM) تسجيل مواجهات عسكرية في ست من أصل عشر ولايات جنوب سودانية وثلاث مناطق إدارية، مما أدى إلى نزوح مدني جديد وتفاقم الأوضاع الإنسانية.

ووثقت CTSAMVM 76 انتهاكًا مزعومًا لوقف إطلاق النار في ديسمبر 2025، منها 21 حادثة عدائية و25 حالة عنف ضد المدنيين والعاملين في المجال الإنساني، وارتفع العدد إلى 87 انتهاكًا مزعومًا في يناير 2026، مع استمرار الهجمات على المدنيين وتفاقم الأعمال العدائية.

ومع ذلك، حذرت RJMEC من أن قدرة CTSAMVM على التحقق من الانتهاكات تأثرت بشدة بسبب القيود المالية والتشغيلية الناتجة عن انخفاض الدعم الدولي، وهو تحدٍ وصفته اللجنة بأنه مقلق بشكل خاص مع اقتراب الانتخابات المقررة في ديسمبر 2026.

وحذر أوينو من أن استمرار التصعيد العسكري وفشل حل الجمود السياسي قد يعكس المكاسب التي تحققت بصعوبة ويهدد بإعادة البلاد إلى الصراع.

ودعت RJMEC مجلس الأمن إلى ضغط جميع الأطراف على وقف الأعمال العدائية فورًا، واستعادة وقف إطلاق النار الدائم، وإعادة الالتزام بالحوار السياسي الشامل. كما طالبت بإعادة توحيد القوات الأمنية وتطويرها تحت قيادة واحدة غير حزبية، وإيجاد حل سياسي لقضية احتجاز النائب الأول للرئيس وغيرهم من المعتقلين السياسيين.

كما ناشدت اللجنة إعادة تشكيل الحكومة الانتقالية وفقًا لاتفاق السلام، بما في ذلك استعادة حقائب SPLM-IO، والالتزام التام بأولوية اتفاق R-ARCSS.

ورغم التحديات، أكد أوينو أن اتفاق السلام المنقح يظل "المسار الوحيد القابل للتطبيق" لتحقيق السلام الدائم في جنوب السودان، ودعا المجتمع الدولي لدعم تنفيذه الكامل.

One Year Since the Removal of Lt. Gen. Alfred Futuyo Karaba as Governor of Western Equatoria State.
‎
‎February 10th, 2025 to February 10th, 2026 marks one year since Lt. Gen. Alfred Futuyo Karaba was removed from office as the Governor of Western Equatoria State (WES).
‎
‎Lt. Gen. Futuyo governed Western Equatoria State from 2020 to 2025, making nearly five years in power under the SPLM-IO, as part of the 2018 Revitalized Agreement on the Resolution of the Conflict in South Sudan (R-ARCSS), which established power-sharing among the parties to the peace agreement.
‎
‎According to the 2018 peace agreement, Western Equatoria State was allocated to SPLM-IO, meaning the Governor was to come from SPLM-IO while the Deputy Governor was to come from SPLM-IG.
‎
‎However, after the removal of Lt. Gen. Futuyo, the state was swapped to SPLM-IG, where the Governor position went to SPLM-IG and the Deputy Governor to SPLM-IO.
‎
‎Following the swap, Hon. James Ateib Berapai was appointed as Governor of Western Equatoria State from SPLM-IG to replace Futuyo, while H.E. Justin Joseph Marona was appointed as Deputy Governor from SPLM-IO.
‎
‎James Ateib later served only five months in office before being removed and replaced by H.E. Daniel Badagbu Rimbasa from SPLM-IG, who is the current Governor of Western Equatoria State, with H.E. Justin Joseph Marona continuing as the Deputy Governor.

Nimule, Eastern Equatoria, South Sudan - The Mayor of Nimule Municipal Council, His Worship Caesar Longa Fuli, has reaffirmed the council's dedication to transforming Nimule into a premier trade hub in the East African region. Addressing a high-level inter-ministerial trade corridor assessment mission on February 8, 2026, Longa Fuli underscored the significance of the Juba-Nimule corridor to South Sudan's economic growth.

He commended Governor Louis Lobong Lojore of Eastern Equatoria State for fostering a secure environment, enabling the delegation's safe passage from Juba. The mayor assured clearing agents, traders, and drivers of the council's steadfast support, acknowledging the longstanding challenges posed by institutional gaps.

The mission seeks to address trade barriers and stimulate economic growth. Longa Fuli called for a transparent business environment and reduced costs for traders, highlighting the One-Stop Border Post (OSBP) as a pivotal initiative to enhance digital efficiency and reduce delays.

The council has pledged to collaborate with the South Sudan Revenue Authority to combat smuggling and implement reforms, positioning Nimule as a fast and efficient trade hub. Longa Fuli emphasized Nimule's readiness to lead, stressing unity, progress, and prosperity.

The assessment mission, led by National Minister of Trade and Industry Hon. Atong Kuol Manyang Juuk, aims to evaluate border procedures, trade facilitation, and institutional coordination. The delegation  composed of Hon. Mary Hillary Pitia, Undersecretary of the Ministry of East African Community Affairs; Hon. Gloria Nyoka, Executive Director of the South Sudan National Bureau of Standards; representatives of the National Assembly Committee on Trade and Industry; the South Sudan Chamber of Commerce, Industry, and Agriculture; and other key stakeholders. engage with local stakeholders and border officials to identify bottlenecks and propose solutions.

A trailer park in Roswell, New Mexico. November 1962. That's where Demi Moore's story begins. Her mother Virginia was barely out of her teens. The biological father vanished before birth. Virginia found a husband named Danny Guynes. Both were serious alcoholics. The kind who destroyed furniture during fights. The kind neighbors reported to police weekly. Work never lasted for Danny. He'd find employment, lose it within weeks, find another job somewhere else. Always running from something. Usually debt collectors and eviction notices.
The family became nomads. Thirty moves before Demi turned 14. Some say closer to forty. New apartments, new towns, new schools. Nothing permanent. Nothing stable. A photographer who worked with Danny remembered the young girl as "malnourished and not so much abused as neglected." Parents consumed by alcohol and chaos. A child learning to raise herself.
Twelve years old. That's when Demi's innocence died completely. She found Virginia unconscious in bed. Pills scattered across the floor. Another attempt to end her life. Danny screamed at Demi to help. He forced Virginia's mouth open while Demi used her small fingers to extract pills one by one. "Something very deep inside me shifted then, and it never shifted back," Demi later wrote. "My childhood was over."
This became Demi's reality. Virginia attempted suicide repeatedly. Demi always watching. Always waiting. Always responsible for preventing her mother's death. No child should carry that weight. The pattern never broke. Drinking, fighting, brief separations, reconciliations, more drinking, more fighting. Danny and Virginia divorced twice, remarried, divorced again.
Teenage years brought new horrors. Virginia started bringing Demi to bars. Dressing her daughter up, using her youth to attract male attention and free drinks. Exploitation disguised as mother-daughter bonding. A middle-aged man entered their lives. Forties or fifties. Started appearing regularly. Lunches with Demi. School pickups. Acting friendly and helpful. Classic predator grooming.
Fifteen years old. Demi came home from school one afternoon. The man was inside their apartment. Alone. He had a key. Virginia had provided it. He raped her in her own home. Three times her age, twice her size. Escape was impossible. Fighting back was impossible. "For decades, I didn't even think of it as rape," Demi wrote. "I thought of it as something I caused."
Virginia announced another move a week later. Demi felt relief flooding through her. Distance from that apartment. Distance from him. Safety at last. Moving day arrived. Virginia invited the predator to help. He showed up carrying boxes while Demi watched in silent horror. During unpacking chaos, Virginia stepped away. The man approached Demi with a smile. "How does it feel to be whored by your mother for five hundred dollars?"
Five hundred dollars. Payment received. Access granted. A mother trafficking her own child. Asked years later if Virginia knowingly sold her, Demi said "I think, in my deep heart, no. I don't think it was a straightforward transaction. But she still did give him the access." Final divorce came when Demi turned fifteen. Two years passed with relative peace.
October 20, 1980. Danny Guynes shot himself. Demi was seventeen. Her stepfather chose death over continuing his pain. High school dropout at sixteen. No diploma. No prospects. Demi moved in with a guitarist twelve years older. Worked collecting debts. Tried modeling. Survival mode engaged. Zero training. Zero connections. Zero safety net. Pure desperation driving every decision. "I was figuring it out by the seat of my pants," she said. "The school of fake it till you make it."
Marriage at eighteen. Freddy Moore, thirty years old, musician. She took his surname before the wedding. Demetria Guynes disappeared. Demi Moore emerged. Four years later, divorce. Nineteen years old, 1981. General Hospital casting call. Her breakthrough opportunity. But cocaine and alcohol were destroying her. Fast spiral downward. "I don't have an off switch," she admitted later. Middle school smoking. Teenage drinking. Clubbing underage. Trauma creates wounds that demand numbing. Sexual assault, suicide attempts, poverty, neglect. Substances promised escape.
St. Elmo's Fire casting in 1984. Brat Pack member. Playing a reckless party girl. Perfect casting since she was living that life. Director and producer noticed her drug use immediately. Ultimatum delivered. Rehab or termination. "A profound gift that they gave me," Demi called it. Treatment worked. Sobriety lasted nearly twenty years.
St. Elmo's Fire saved her in 1985. About Last Night proved talent in 1986. Ghost exploded everything in 1990. Swayze. Goldberg. That pottery scene. Box office phenomenon. Ghost demanded Demi access buried trauma for emotional authenticity. Childhood anguish poured onto screen. Critics noticed the raw power.
Career ignited. A Few Good Men in 1992. Indecent Proposal in 1993. Disclosure in 1994. G.I. Jane in 1997 with that iconic buzzcut and muscular transformation. Fighting studio executives became routine. Demanding strong female characters. Refusing decorative romantic roles.
1996 arrived. Striptease contract. $12.5 million. Highest-paid actress in film history at that point. Critics nicknamed her "Gimme Moore." Greed accusations flew. Her response cut through: "Why shouldn't I? Why shouldn't all women be paid equal to the quality of their work?"
But success doesn't erase trauma. 1989. Demi funded Virginia's rehab at Hazelden Foundation in Minnesota. Virginia quit halfway through. Just walked out. Demi severed contact. Eight years silence. 1993. Virginia posed nude for High Society magazine. Mocking her daughter's Vanity Fair pregnancy cover. Parodying Ghost. Final exploitation for cash and attention.

1998, Brain tumor diagnosis. Virginia dying. Demi returned. Relocated family to New Mexico motel. Three months at her mother's bedside. "I had to figure out why," Demi explained. "How could I expect my children to hold compassion for me when I lost it for my own mother?" Virginia died July 2, 1998. Age fifty-four. Demi present, holding her hand.

September 2019. Inside Out published. Brutally honest memoir. Instant number one bestseller. 2025. Age sixty-two. Golden Globe winner for The Substance. Time Magazine's 100 most influential people. Hollywood Walk of Fame star incoming.
The trauma never vanished. Forties brought relapse. Body image struggles persisted. Insecurity haunted every achievement. But survival happened anyway. Pain transformed into performances. Neglect became character understanding. Chaos fueled determination. She cared for her dying mother despite everything. Shared her story to help others. Chose resilience. Hollywood's highest-paid actress built on a foundation of childhood horror. Proof that origins don't dictate destinations.

Six years ago, we came together from all sectors,  for an Enriching Day, Listening and Speaking at the Advancing Community Cohesion Conference.
We spoke about couragrous conversations,  trust, empathy and so much more anoit collaborations with transformative action  

We explored how communities come together and how they heal.
For decades, all organisations, community leaders, women’s groups, youth mentors, and faith leaders have invested deeply in social cohesion, often quietly, often without recognition. 

Moving forward, no one can claim social cohesion to be the responsibility of one group but rather a continuation of all the years of working together without blaming and shaming.

We have shown up, consistently.

So when we speak about social cohesion today, we do so not as critics from the outside, but as contributors from within.

But we need to cone together and ask, What does social cohesion mean in this moment in time?

In NSW, we are witnessing new laws that restrict protest and public expression. We are seeing increased policing of dissent. We are seeing Muslims portrayed, yet again, through the lens of suspicion, risk, or conditional belonging.
And at the same time, we are being told that we must “maintain social cohesion.”

This move by Sweden is reigniting a global debate about what citizenship truly represents. Supporters argue that becoming a citizen should require more than just residency—it should involve understanding the language, laws, and civic norms of the country you want to join. From that perspective, integration isn’t punishment; it’s a baseline expectation for social cohesion.

Advocates say policies like this are about fairness and stability, not exclusion. When newcomers learn the language and how institutions function, it strengthens trust, reduces isolation, and helps communities work together instead of fragmenting. Many also point out that long-time legal immigrants who put in the effort to integrate deserve a system that values their commitment.

Critics will call it harsh, but others see it as a government finally drawing clear lines after years of uncertainty. As immigration pressures rise across Europe, countries are experimenting with firmer standards—and watching closely to see what works. The real question is whether other nations will follow suit or continue down a different path.

CEPO Urges African Union to Take Decisive Action to Safeguard Peace in South Sudan

Mr. Edmund Yakani, Executive Director of the Community Empowerment for Progress Organization (CEPO), is calling on the African Union (AU) to take firm and decisive measures to ensure peace and stability in South Sudan.

Yakani expressed concern that a significant number of South Sudan’s political elites continue to resort to violence as a means of resolving political disagreements, undermining ongoing peace efforts and threatening national stability.

He emphasized that the African Union must move beyond statements of concern and adopt concrete actions that hold leaders accountable for actions that fuel conflict.

“One of the most effective and decisive measures would be the imposition of regional travel bans on leaders who choose violence over dialogue,” Yakani stated. “Those who promote or engage in war-mongering should not enjoy the privilege of unrestricted movement within the region while ordinary citizens suffer the consequences of instability.”

CEPO reiterated its call for strengthened regional intervention mechanisms to deter violence, promote accountability, and protect civilians from further political unrest.

What if the division IS the point?

Not in the dramatic sense everyone wants to argue about… but in the way pressure reveals what was already unstable. What if this moment isn’t about us cleanly splitting into metaphorical camps, but about being forced into clarity? Clarity about who and what is deserving of our time, energy, and success.

People keep framing it as left vs. right, awake vs. asleep, religious vs. secular, dem vs. rep,  blah vs. blah. What's the point in that?

What if the line being drawn runs somewhere quieter and far more uncomfortable, between truth and deception? Discernment vs deception...not just “their” deception, ours too.

I’m not convinced unity for unity’s sake is noble if it requires you to override your conscience just to stay liked, accepted, or safe. 

There are seasons where coming together is sacred and healing. And there are seasons where walking toward what you know in your bones to be true means the circle shifts. People fall away and I'm learning this is super important and liberating.
No hate or superiority, simply alignment because alignment has weight, and approval can’t be the compass.

Discernment gives way to clarity. It’s the slow willingness to question your own narratives, your own triggers, your own susceptibility to emotional manipulation. 
Deception thrives where we are reactive, where we want quick certainty, where belonging feels safer than integrity. 
Truth doesn’t usually shout. It stands, steady and often alone, and lets the noise exhaust itself...let's the trash take itself out. 👏

Maybe this isn’t about choosing a side at all. Maybe it’s about choosing integrity even if the crowd thins, even if it costs you comfort, even if it requires you to disappoint people who preferred the older version of you. There are worse things that being alone, like being with people who make you feel alone. 

Morning coffee thoughts before hitting the gym.

Make it a great day today, and power to the people findinh their own way apart from the mob.

“We are concerned that the recent renewed armed violence may return the country to war if the parties fail to embrace an inclusive political dialogue for resolving the ongoing political stalemate,” he stated. “Coordinated regional and international political pressure is required to be maintained and increased now. Evidently, we observed a series of attacks on humanitarian workers and properties, mainly in the areas witnessing armed violence.”

Yakani urged the Council to demand the immediate observation of the ceasefire, resumption of inclusive political dialogue, and release of political detainees.

We call for the unconditional and immediate release of the First Vice President, Dr. Riek Machar, and other SPLM-IO leaders, and urge all parties to engage in an inclusive dialogue to restore peace, stability, and constitutional order. As we look ahead to the African Union Assembly of Heads of State and Government, the AU C5, and the IGAD summit in Addis Ababa this week,We remain hopeful that these engagements will provide constructive solutions to the current political crisis. Padahal mereka tidak disuruh kecuali supaya menyembah Allah dengan memurnikan keta`atan kepada-Nya dalam (menjalankan) agama yang lurus…[Al-Bayyinah/98 : 5]

Segala Puji bagi Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala Rabb semesta alam Shalawat dam salam kita sampaikan kepada Nabi Muhammad Shalalllahu ‘alaihi wa sallam Pembawa risalah yang haq ini sebagai rahmat bagi semesta alam kepada keluarganya para shahabatnya dan orang-orang yang setia mengikuti jejaknya hingga akhir zaman.

Berikut ini adalah pembahasan secara singkat hal-hal yang berkaitan dengan pentingnya “keikhlasan” dalam seluruh amalibadah. Sesungguhnya perkara paling mendasar dan terpenting dalam dien ini adalah mengikhlaskan diri kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala dalam setiap amal ibadah yang kita lakukan, hal itu sebagai syarat utama diterimanya amal ibadah. Ikhlas adalah termasuk amalan hati yang perlu mendapatkan perhatian “istimewa” (secara mendalam) dan dilakukan dengan cara “istimrar” (terus menerus) di setiap kita hendak melakukan amalibadah, agar amalan kita menjadi bernilai di hadapan Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala.

PENTINGNYA AMALAN HATI.
Telah kita ketahui bahwa pengertian iman menurut Ahlus Sunah adalah : Keyakinan dengan hati, ikrar dengan lisan, dan amalan dengan seluruh anggota badan, bertambah dengan ketaatan kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala dan berkurang dengan perbuatan maksiat.

Perlu diketahui bahwa ikhlas adalah perkara terpenting dalam amalan hati, yang hal tersebut sangat erat hubungannya dengan pengertian iman tersebut di atas.

Syaikhul Islam Ibnu Taimiyah berkata : “Amalan-amalan hati adalah termasuk pokok-pokok dari keimanan dan tonggak-tonggak agama Islam ini, seperti: mencintai Allah dan Rasul-Nya, bertawakal kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala, mengikhlaskan seluruh macam ibadah hanya kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala semata, bersyukur kepada-Nya atas nikmat-nikmat-Nya dan berlaku sabar di atas hukum-hukum-Nya, khauf (perasaan takut kepada-Nya akan siksa atau adzab-Nya), raja (berharap) kepada-Nya…Semua amalan ini wajib atas seluruh makhluk berdasarkan kesepakatan para imam agama”.[1]

Ibnul Qayim juga menjelaskan keagungan amalan-amalan hati : Amalan–amalan hati ialah pokok adapun amalan–amalan anggota badan adalah pengikut dan penyempurna. Sesungguhnya niat sekedudukan dengan ruh, adapun amalan sekedudukan dengan jasad, sehingga apabila ruh telah terpisah dengan jasad maka binasalah. Oleh sebab itu mengetahui hukum – hukum hati lebih penting dari pada mengetahui hukum-hukum jasad.[2]

Hal inilah di antaranya yang mendorong kami untuk mengulas hal ini agar seluruh aktifitas kita sehari-hari tidak menemui kesia-siaan, yakni hampa, jauh dari berkah Allah atau Ramat-Nya, seolah-olah tiada nilainya aktifitas yang kita laksanakan setiap hari.

Niat berasal dari bahasa Arab, yang berarati tujuan. Sedangkan menurut istilah syara’ memiliki dua arti:

Ikhlash dalam beramal, yaitu semata-mata karena Allah, dan inilah yang sering dibicarakan oleh para Ulama ahli tauhid, suluk (perilaku) dan akhlak.
Membedakan antara ibadah yang satu dengan ibadah yang lain, atau ibadah dengan kebiasaan. Istilah ini sering dipakai oleh ulama-ulama Fiqh.
Niat dipakai untuk membedakan antara ibadah dan adat (kebiasaan yang dilakukan oleh manusia), misalnya : Mandi, apabila dimaksudkan (niatkan) karena Allah semata untuk menghilangkan hadats besar (mandi junub misalnya) maka hal yang semacam itu akan menjadi ibadah, lain halnya apabila mandi semata-mata dimaksudkan untuk membersihkan badan atau mendapatkan kesegaran, maka hal itu menjadi adat (kebiasaan) saja.

Kemudian bahwa niat itu tempatnya di hati dan apabila di lafadzkan menjadi bid`ah.

KEDUDUKAN IKHLAS.
Sesungguhnya ikhlas adalah hakekat dien dan kunci dakwah para rasul, yakni menyembah Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala semata dan menjauhi thagut :

ومَا أُمِرُوْا إِلاَّ لِيَعْبُدُوْا اللهَ مُخْلِصِيْنَ لَهُ الدِّيْنَ حُنَفَاءَ

Padahal mereka tidak disuruh kecuali supaya menyembah Allah dengan memurnikan ketaatan kepada-Nya dalam (menjalankan) agama yang lurus…[Al-Bayyinah/98: 5]

Yang dimaksud dengan ” (حُنَفَاءَ ) agama yang lurus” pada ayat di atas adalah terjauhkan dari perkara-perkara syirik dan menuju kepada tauhid. Di sinilah pentingnya ikhlash dalam selurus amal ibadah, agar amalan tersebut tidak sia-sia, dan tidak mendapat adzab dari Allah, baik di dunia maupun di akhirat kelak.

Kemudian bahwa pengaruh ikhlas terhadap amalan itu sangatlah besar, amal yang kecil dan sedikit jika dilakukan dengan ikhlas dapat memperoleh pahala yang besar. Syaikhul Islam Ibnu Taimiyah dalam perkara ini mengatakan: “Suatu jenis amalan yang dikerjakan oleh manusia dengan menyempurnakan keikhlasannya dan ketundukkannya kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala, terkadang Allah Subahnahu wa Ta’ala akan mengampuni dosa-dosa besar dengan sebab amalan itu, sebagaimana hadits al-bithaqah (seorang yang memiliki satu kartu Laa ilaaha illa Allah, lalu diampuni dosa-dosanya sebanyak 99 lembaran catatan amal keburukan-red)…ini karena dia mengucapkan Laa ilaaha illa Allah dengan ikhlas dan jujur/benar, karena kalau tidak, maka para pelaku dosa besar yang masuk ke dalam neraka semuanya juga mengucapkan tauhid, tetapi perkataan mereka tidaklah lebih berat terhadap dosa-dosa mereka sebagaimana pemilik kartu (Laa ilaaha illa Allah) itu.”

Hadits pemilik kartu Laa ilaaha illa Allah itu, adalah sebagai berikut:

عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ الْمَعَافِرِيِّ ثُمَّ الْحُبُلِيِّ قَال سَمِعْتُ عَبْدَ الهِb بْنَ عَمْرِو بْنِ الْعَاصِ يَقُولُ قَالَ رَسُولُ الهَِ n إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَيُخَلِّصُ رَجُلاً مِنْ أُمَّتِي عَلَى رُءُوسِ الْخَلاَئِقِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ فَيَنْشُرُ عَلَيْهِ تِسْعَةً وَتِسْعِينَ سِجِلاَّ كُلُّ سِجِلٍّ مِثْلُ مَدِّ الْبَصَرِ ثُمَّ يَقُولُ أَتُنْكِرُ مِنْ هَذَا شَيْئًا أَظَلَمَكَ كَتَبَتِي الْحَافِظُونَ فَيَقُولُ لاَ يَا رَبِّ فَيَقُولُ أَفَلَكَ عُذْرٌ فَيَقُولُ لاَ يَا رَبِّ فَيَقُولُ بَلَى إِنَّ لَكَ عِنْدَنَا حَسَنَةً فَإِنَّهُ لَا ظُلْمَ عَلَيْكَ الْيَوْمَ فَتَخْرُجُ بِطَاقَةٌ فِيهَا أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لاَ إِلَهَ إِلاَّ الهُب وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا عَبْدُهُ وَرَسُولُهُ فَيَقُولُ احْضُرْ وَزْنَكَ فَيَقُولُ يَا رَبِّ مَا هَذِهِ الْبِطَاقَةُ مَعَ هَذِهِ السِّجِلَّاتِ فَقَالَ إِنَّكَ لاَ تُظْلَمُ قَالَ فَتُوضَعُ السِّجِلاَّتُ فِي كَفَّةٍ وَالْبِطَاقَةُ فِي كَفَّةٍ فَطَاشَتِ السِّجِلاَّتُ وَثَقُلَتِ الْبِطَاقَةُ فَلاَ يَثْقُلُ مَعَ اسْمِ الهِق شَيْءٌ

Dari Abdullah bin ‘Amr bin ‘Ash Radhiyallahu ‘anhu , dia berkata: “Saya telah mendengar Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam bersabda: “Sesungguhnya Allah akan mengadili salah seorang laki-laki dari ummatku di hadapan seluruh makhluk pada hari kiamat. Lalu ditunjukan kepada laki-laki tersebut 99 catatan (amal keburukan), setiap satu catatan panjangnya sejauh mata memandang. Kemudian dikatakan kepada laki-laki tersebut: ”Apakah kau ingkari dari semua ini (kedzaliman yang telah kau perbuat)? Apakah para malaikat-Ku pencatat dan penjaga amalan menzhalimimu? Laki-laki tersebut menjawab: “Tidak Ya Tuhanku!”. Lalu Allah berkata kepada laki-laki tersebut: “Apakah engkau punya alasan (berbuat kezhaliman itu)? Laki-laki tersebut menjawab: “Tidak Ya Tuhanku!”. Kemudian Allah berkata kepada laki-laki tersebut: “Ya benar, tetapi sesungguhnya engkau memiliki satu kebaikan di sisi Kami, dan sesungguhnya tidak ada kedzaliman atasmu pada hari ini. Maka Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala mengeluarkan sebuah kartu kecil yang di dalamnya terdapat : Asyhadu an laa ilaaha illa Allah wa asyhadu anna Muhamadan ‘abduhu warasuluhu (Aku bersaksi bahwa tiada sesembahan yang haq kecuali Allah dan aku bersaksi bahwa Muhammad adalah hamba dan utusan-Nya). Kemudian Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala berkata kepada orang tersebut: “Datangkan timbanganmu”, maka orang tersebut berkata: “Ya Tuhan untuk apa kartu kecil ini dibandingkan dengan catatan (amal keburukan) ini ?”, maka Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala berkata kepada orang tersebut: “Sesungguhnya pada hari ini tiada kedzaliman”. Maka diletakkanlah catatan itu pada salah satu daun timbangan, dan kartu kecil itu diletakan pada satu daun timbangan yang lain. Maka jadi ringanlah catatan-catatan `amal keburukan itu dan beratlah kartu kecil tersebut, maka tiadalah sesuatupun yang menjadi berat dibandingkan dengan nama Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala. [HR. At-Tirmidzi dan An-Nasa’i].

PENGERTIAN IKHLAS DAN BATASNNYA
Ada beberapa pengertian tentang ikhlas yang disebutkan oleh ulama, antara lain :

Diantaranya ada yang mengatakan : Ikhlas ialah “Menjadikan Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala satu-satunya tujuan di dalam menjalankan ketaatan”.
Ada juga yang mengatakan : “Ikhlas ialah membersihkan perbuatan dari mencari pandangan manusia”.
Al-Harawi berkata: “Ikhlas ialah membersihkan amalan dari setiap noda”.
Dan sebagian yang lain ada yang mengatakan: “Orang yang mukhlis ialah orang yang tidak perduli, seandainya hilang seluruh penghormatan kepadanya di dalam hati manusia, untuk kebaikan hatinya bersama Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala. Dan dia tidak suka manusia mengetahui amalannya walaupun seberat debu. Allah.
Tidak diragukan lagi bahwa keikhlasan membutuhkan kesungguhan yang tinggi hingga seorang hamba meraihnya dengan sempurna.

PENGERTIAN RIYA’, SUM’AH, UJUB
Telah kita ketahui bahwa keikhlasan dapat dihilangkan oleh beberapa perkara, seperti: mencintai dunia, kemasyhuran, kemuliaan, riya’, sum’ah dan ujub.

Riya ialah melakukan `ibadah dengan tujuan dilihat oleh manusia, sehingga orang yang riya’ itu mencari pengagungan, pujian, harapan atau rasa takut terhadap orang yang dia berbuat riya’ karenanya.
Sum’ah adalah amalan yang dilakukan dalam rangka agar didengar orang lain, misalnya memperdengarkan bacaan Al-Qur’an atau yang lainnya.
Ujub adalah teman riya, yaitu perasaan bangga terhadap diri sendiri atas kemampuan yang dimiliki secara berlebihan.
Syaikhul Islam Ibnu Taimiyah membedakan antara keduanya (antara riya dan ujub ).
a. Riya adalah salah satu bentuk dari syirik kepada makhluk.
b. Adapun ujub adalah bentuk dari pada syirik kepada diri sendiri.[3]

DIANTARA BENTUK-BENTUK RIYA, UJUB DAN SUM’AH

Riya dalam ibadah sholat, misalnya : Memperbaiki posisi atau gerakan shalat karena mengetahui bahwa dia sedang diperhatikan oleh orang yang dianggap lebih ‘alim atau lainya.
Riya atau sum’ah dalam kepribadian misalnya : Karena di karuniai oleh Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala suara yang merdu misalnya, maka timbulah penyakit riyaatau ujub ini pada nimat tersebut; Mengeraskan/ menbaguskan bacaan dalam membaca Al-Qur`an atau ketika mengumandangkan adzan dengan harapan ingin mendapatkan pujian atau agar diakui bahwa dia memiliki suara yang bagus atau merdu. Pada hakekatnya membaguskan suara dalam membaca Al-Qur’an, dengan tidak dibuat-buat atau berlebih-lebihan merupakan sunnah Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam sebagaimana sabadanya:
زَيِّنُوْا اْلقُرْآنَ بِأَصْوَاتِكُمْ.

Baguskanlah (bacaan) Al-Qur`an dengan suara kalian [4]

Ujub atau Riya dalam berdakwah misalnya : Berceramah, menasehati orang, atau mentahdzir (memberi peringatan terhadap seseorang) dengan niat agar dikenal sebagai seorang penasehat, ahli pidato dengan harapan agar semua orang memujinya atau menyanjungnya. Kita berlindung kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala dari semua perkara ini. Hendaklah kita ikhlash dalam berda`wah agar orang yang mendengarnya pun menerima dengan ikhlash (yakni : mendapatkan hidayah dari Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala)
Riya atau Ujub dalam menuntut ilmu : Yaitu berbangga dengan ilmu yang dikaruniakan Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala kepadanya atau menuntut ilmu hanya dalam rangka ingin menjadi seorang yang ahli dalam berdebat, bukan mengharapkan wajah Allah atau mencari berkah dari Allah atas ilmu yang dimilikinya. Sehingga ilmu yang Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala karuniakan tidak mampu membawa dia ke dalam kebahagian di dunia ataupun diakhirat. Padahal rasulullah telah memperingatkan dengan keras bagi para penuntut ilmu dengan ancaman tidak akan mendapatkan bau surga, apabila mempelajari suatu ilmu dalam rangka untuk mencari dunia semata; Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam bersabada:
مَنْ تَعَلَّمَ عِلْمًا مِمَّا يُبْتَغَى بِهِ وَجْهُ اللهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ لاَ يَتَعَلَّمُهُ إِلاَّ لِيُصِيبَ بِهِ عَرَضًا مِنَ الدُّنْيَا لَمْ يَجِدْ عَرْفَ الْجَنَّةِ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ يَعْنِي رِيحَهَا

Barang siapa menuntut ilmu yang seharusnya untuk mencari wajah Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala ; tetapi dia tidak mempelajari ilmu itu kecuali untuk mendapatkan harta benda dunia, maka dia tidak akan mendapatkan bau surga pada hari kiamat kelak.[5]

Riya atau Ujub ketika bershadaqah, misalnya : Memperlihatkan harta yang telah dishadaqahkan, atau mengungkit-ungkit kembali pemberian yang telah lalu dengan harapan agar disebut sebagai seorang dermawan.
PENAWAR RIYA
Adapun di antara cara-cara mengobati riya adalah sebagi berikut:

Mengetahui seluk beluk riya itu sendiri dan takut terhadapnya. Sebagaimana hal tersebut adalah perkara yang paling ditakutkan oleh Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam. Beliau Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam bersabda:
” إِنَّ أَخْوَفُ مَا أَخَا فُ عَلَيكْمُ الشِّرْكُ اْلأَ صْغَر. قَا لوُا وَمَا الشِّرْكُ اْلأَ صْغَرُ يَا رَسُوْلُ الله ؟ قال : ” الرِّيَاءُ “.يقول الله تعالىيوم القيامة, إذا جازى الناس بأعمالهم : اذهبوا إلى الذين كنتم تراؤون في الدنيا فانظروا هل تجدون جزاء؟”

Sesungguhnya yang paling kutakutkan dari perkara yang aku takutkan atas kalian ialah syirik kecil. Para shahabat bertanya: “Apakah syirik kecil itu wahai rasulullah? Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam bersabda: “Riya’, Pada hari kiamat , ketika membalas amalan-amalan manusia, Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala akan berfirman: “Pergilah kepada orang yang kamu dahulu sewaktu di dunia berbuat riya’ kepadanya, dan lihatlah apakah kamu dapakan balasan (pahala) darinya? [6]

Memberikan sanjungan atau pujian hanya ditujukan kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala semata, karena Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala sumber dari segala kebaikan; maka hanya Allahlah yang berhaq mendapatkan pujian:
الحمد لله رب العالمين

Segala puji bagi Allah Tuhan semesta alam. [Al-Fatihah/1 :2]

Mengingat mati dan sekaratnya, hari akhir dan kedahsyatan adzabnya, kubur dan kerasnya siksa yang diberikan karena dosa-dosa yang diperbuat selama di dunia. Keadaan di kubur yang sunyi, gelap gulita dan sempit, tidak ada ibu dan bapak atau orang-orang yang dicinta di dekatnya.
Melihat akibat riya’, baik di dunia maupun diakhirat.
Maka perlu diketahui oleh setiap orang bahwa seandainya seluruh manusia berkumpul dalam rangka memberikan manfaat kepada siapapun, maka tiadalah mereka mampu memberikannya kecuali sesuatu itu telah ditentukan oleh Allah Subhanhau wa Ta’ala baginya; Oleh sebab itu sebagian orang-orang salaf mengatakan: “Bersungguh-sungguhlah dalam mencegah timbulnya riya` darimu, anggaplah orang lain bagimu seperti binatang dan anak-anak, janganlah kau bedakan adanya mereka atau tidak adanya, mereka tahu atau tidak tahu, cukuplah Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala saja yang mengetahuinya.
Kemudian singkirkan perasaan ingin dipuji ketika (syetan menggoda), dengan do’a-do’a yang diajarkan Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam seperti:

أعوذ الله من الشيطان الرجيم

Aku berlindung kepada Allah dari godaan syetan yang terkutuk.

Adapun akibat riya di akhirat antara lain ; sebagaimana sabda Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam.

مَنْ سَمَّعَ سَمَّعَ الهُ بِهِ وَمَنْ رَاءَى رَاءَى الهُ بِهِ

Barang siapa (yang beramal) ingin didengar maka Allah akan memperdengarkannya dan barang siapa (beramal) ingin dilihat maka Allah pun akan memperlihatkannya.[7]

Artinya : Bila seseorang beramal hanya ingin didengar atau dilihat orang lain maka itulah yang akan dia dapatkan, Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala Maha Sempurna tidak butuh sekutu-sekutu tersebut, Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam bersabda: bahwa Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala berfirman:

أَنَا أَغْنَى الشُّرَكَاءِ عَنِ الشِّرْكِ مَنْ عَمِلَ عَمَلاً أَشْرَكَ فِيهِ مَعِي غَيْرِي تَرَكْتُهُ وَشِرْكَهُ

Aku adalah Yang paling tidak butuh sekutu, barangsiapa yang mengamalkan suatu perbuatan, yang di dalamnya dia menyekutukanKu dengan selain Aku, maka Aku tinggalkan dia dan sekutunya.[8]

Memohon pertolongan kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala agar senantiasa berlaku ikhlas dalam segala amal ibadah dan berlindung dari-Nya dari riya. Seorang mumin atau muminah hendaklah tunduk, berserah diri kepada-Nya, berusaha semaksimal mungkin menghindarkan diri dari riya, sum’ah dan ujub; dan memperbanyak dzikir (mengingat Allah kapan saja di manapun berada) dan berdo`a kepada Allah Subhanahu wa Ta’ala, sebagaimana do’a-do’a yang diajarkan Rasulullah Shallallahu ‘alaihi wa sallam antara lain :
الشرك فيكم أخفى من دبيب النمل. وسأدلك على شيءٍ إذا فعلته أذهب عنك صغار الشرك وكبيره . تقول: اَللَّهُمَّ إِنِّي أَعُوْ ذُ بِكَ أَنْ أُشْرِكَ بِكَ وَأَناَ أَعْلَمُ, وَاسْتَغْفِرُكَ لمِاَ لاَ أَعْلَمُ. 

Kesyirikan yang ada pada kalian lebih tersembunyi merayapnya seekor semut, dan aku akan memberitahukan sesuatu kepadamu apabila hal itu kau kerjakan, maka akan menghilangkan kesyirikan kecil dan besar darimu. Yaitu engkau mengatakan (berdo’a): “Ya Allah aku berlindung kepada-Mu dari mensekutukan-Mu sedangkan saya mengetahuinya dan aku berlindung kepada-Mu dari apa-apa yang aku tidak aku tahu.”[9]

Listening, listening, listening 
Trusting, trusting, trusting

The Walk for Peace is the beginning of the movement. The people, the country, the world, we are all yearning for peace. 

It can be achieved.
It WILL be achieved
For ALL

Good Peace, Good Love, Good Energy with every foot fall

Excellent! They have done it.Twenty Buddist monk have done the peace walk of 2300 miles across the United States, accompanied by peace dog named Aloka.Their aim was to spread the message of INNER PEACE in modern civilization. 
Aloka symbolise all living beings, reminding us that loving kindness should extend to every beings in the universe. These monks have done great personal sacrifice to complete the demanding journey while in the path of udestanding Four Noble Truths through Noble Eight Fold pathway. The practice of loving kindness is broad, deep, inclusive and boundless. .
As described in Karaneeya Mettha sutra, a person who cultivate the loving kindness should be upright, assertive, gentle, very deciplined, tolerant and patient. Loving kindness should be extended to all being without an exception- those of higher or lower status, large or small or microscopic, visible or unvisible, near or far  born or unborn including those in wombs or eggs. One should not deceive others.These boundless loving kindness should radiate in all directions at all times just as a mother's loving kindness to her only son.
This loving kindness is developed through practice of Noble Eight Fold pathway which include mindfulness while practicing Vipassana Meditation leading to insight and wisdom  Vipassana knowledge. 

As stated in Dhammapada, hatred is never overcome by hatred, hatred is only overcome by loving kindness. 

Cultivating inner peace through loving kindness brings biological, psychological, social and spiritual benifits, not only in the individual but also to the wider society. 
People with compassionate and Noble minds from around the world are supporting and following peace walk.
May all of them share these wholesome merits. May Aloka also may partake these merits.
